author: whitekid
body:
## Summary

Close the read-side of the multipart S3 surface. `GET /:bucket?uploads` and `GET /:bucket/:key?uploadId=<id>` were falling through to `listObjects` and `getObject` respectively, so AWS SDK callers of `list_multipart_uploads` / `list_parts` got the wrong response shape. With this PR they get standard S3 XML.

This is the third multipart-area PR in a series:
- #241 — Move orphan sweep into the storage capability plan (T1)
- #242 — Wire AbortMultipartUpload (T2-a)
- **#243 (this) — Wire ListMultipartUploads + ListParts (T2-d)**

After this slice the multipart surface is complete: Create / UploadPart / Complete / Abort / List uploads / List parts / Sweep orphans. The originally-proposed "session lifecycle abstraction" (T2-c) was rejected on inspection — invariants already enforced at the right layer; adding a session wrapper would have been syntactic, not deepening.

## Design

### Backend interface (storage.go)

```go
ListMultipartUploads(ctx, bucket, prefix string, maxUploads int) ([]*MultipartUpload, error)
ListParts(ctx, bucket, key, uploadID string, maxParts int) ([]Part, error)
```

`maxUploads`/`maxParts` of `0` mean no cap.

### Implementations

| Backend | Approach |
|---|---|
| `LocalBackend` | Scan BadgerDB `mpu:` prefix (uploads), walk per-uploadID partDir (parts), re-hash part files for ETag |
| `SwappableBackend` | Pass-through to inner via atomic.Pointer |
| `PackedBackend` | Pass-through to inner |
| `RecoveryWriteGate` | Auto-passthrough via embedded `Backend` (read methods survive the gate) |
| `pullthrough.Backend` | Auto-passthrough via embedded `storage.Backend` |
| `DistributedBackend` | First-slice limitations — see Notes |
| `ClusterCoordinator` | `ListParts` routes via `routeObjectWrite`; `ListMultipartUploads` delegates to base |
| `Operations` (facade) | Thin pass-through |

### HTTP handlers (handlers.go)

`listMultipartUploads(ctx, c, bucket)` and `listParts(ctx, c, bucket, key, uploadID)` render standard S3 XML structs (`listMultipartUploadsResult`, `listPartsResult`) with `?prefix=`, `?max-uploads=`, `?max-parts=` parameters. ETag values are quoted per S3 convention. The `?uploadId=` branch in `getObject` is checked before `?versionId=`/Range because S3 routes to ListParts whenever uploadId is present.

`IsTruncated` is set conservatively: when returned count equals max, mark truncated. Proper pagination is a follow-up; consumers needing exact paging should request smaller batches.

## First-slice limitations (cluster mode)

Documented in code comments and intentional for this slice:

1. **`DistributedBackend.ListMultipartUploads` returns an empty list.** The FSM-replicated multipart record (`clusterMultipartMeta`) only stores `ContentType` + `PlacementGroupID` — bucket and key are not replicated, so a faithful bucket-scoped listing cannot be reconstructed from local FSM state. Single-node (`LocalBackend`) returns the real list.
2. **`ListParts` is best-effort in cluster mode.** Parts uploaded against another node's routed group are not visible from this node's local FS. `ClusterCoordinator.ListParts` routes via `routeObjectWrite` when the local group owns `(bucket, key)`; otherwise it falls back to local visibility.

Follow-up: extend `clusterMultipartMeta` to carry bucket+key (FSM schema migration), and add a forward op for cross-node ListParts.

## Test Coverage

**4 new sub-cases at storage level (`internal/storage/multipart_test.go`)**:

| Test | Covers |
|---|---|
| `TestLocalBackend_ListMultipartUploads` | Bucket scoping (alpha vs beta), prefix filter (`logs/` vs `snapshots/`), maxUploads cap |
| `TestLocalBackend_ListMultipartUploads_BucketNotFound` | `ErrBucketNotFound` for missing bucket |
| `TestLocalBackend_ListParts` | Out-of-order upload still returns sorted parts, ETag matches upload-time hash, maxParts cap |
| `TestLocalBackend_ListParts_NotFound` | Missing uploadID → `ErrUploadNotFound` |

**4 new sub-cases at server level (`internal/server/server_test.go`)**:

| Test | Covers |
|---|---|
| `TestListMultipartUploads_Success` | Full listing, `?prefix=` filter, abort cleanup removes from listing |
| `TestListMultipartUploads_BucketNotFound` | 404 NoSuchBucket |
| `TestListParts_Success` | Out-of-order parts return sorted, ETag fidelity through wire |
| `TestListParts_NotFound` | 404 NoSuchUpload |

**Test fakes across 6 packages** get pass-through stubs for the 2 new methods (`vfs/mockBackend`, `nfs4server/fileMetaCacheBackend`, `nfs4server/allocateTruncateBackend`, `cluster/fakeBackend`, `cmd/grainfs/migrationNoSuchBucketBackend`, `storage/contextRecorderBackend`, `storage/basicBackend`).

## Plan Completion

| Item | Status |
|---|---|
| Backend interface: ListMultipartUploads + ListParts | ✅ DONE |
| LocalBackend implementations (BadgerDB + filesystem) | ✅ DONE |
| 4 wrapper passthroughs (Swappable, Packed, RecoveryGate, pullthrough) | ✅ DONE |
| Operations facade pass-through | ✅ DONE |
| DistributedBackend stubs (cluster-mode limitations documented) | ✅ DONE |
| ClusterCoordinator routing (ListParts via routeObjectWrite) | ✅ DONE |
| HTTP handlers + S3 XML structs | ✅ DONE |
| `?uploadId=` branch ordering before `?versionId=` and Range | ✅ DONE |
| 4 new storage-level test sub-cases | ✅ DONE |
| 4 new server-level test sub-cases | ✅ DONE |
| Test fakes updated (6 packages) | ✅ DONE |
| `make test` PASS, no new lint warnings on changed files | ✅ DONE |

12/12 DONE.

## Out of scope (potential follow-ups)

- **Cluster-mode FSM schema extension** to carry bucket+key in `clusterMultipartMeta`, enabling proper `DistributedBackend.ListMultipartUploads` across all nodes
- **Forward op for ListParts** so cluster mode shows parts from any group's routed leader
- **Real pagination** (key-marker, upload-id-marker, part-number-marker, NextMarker) instead of the conservative `IsTruncated` heuristic
- **ETag caching** in part metadata so ListParts doesn't re-hash files (low priority — list isn't a hot path)

## Test plan

- [x] `make test` PASS (full unit suite, exit 0)
- [x] `make lint` — 0 new warnings on changed files (one pre-existing unrelated `data = nil` in EC code is preserved)
- [x] All 4 + 4 new sub-cases PASS
- [x] All existing multipart tests (TestMultipartUploadAPI, TestUploadPart_*, TestCompleteMultipartUpload_*, TestAbortMultipartUpload_*) continue to PASS

author: ave13
body:
## Summary
Replaced the standard TextInput widgets in the profile editor with a custom on-screen keyboard (`BigKeyboard`) for better UX on touch devices. The profile form now uses button-based field selection with an integrated keyboard for text entry.

## Key Changes
- **New `BigKeyboard` component** (`ui/keyboard.py`): A custom on-screen keyboard with:
  - Alphabetic and numeric layouts with mode switching
  - Shift key for capitalization
  - Backspace and Done keys
  - Callback-based key event handling
  
- **Refactored profile editor** (`ui/profile.py`):
  - Replaced `_row()` helper and TextInput widgets with a GridLayout displaying field labels and value buttons
  - Fields now show as buttons that highlight when selected
  - Integrated BigKeyboard for all text input
  - Changed from TextInput's direct text manipulation to state-based value tracking
  - Improved error message text ("must be > 0" instead of "must be greater than zero")
  - Adjusted layout sizing and spacing for better touch interaction

- **Window configuration** (`main.py`):
  - Added explicit window dimensions (1024x768) and fullscreen auto-detection for consistent display across devices

## Implementation Details
- Field selection uses an `active` index that tracks which field is being edited
- Button colors change based on selection state (active: blue, inactive: gray)
- Keyboard layout switches between alphabetic and numeric modes
- Enter key (Done) cycles to the next field for streamlined data entry
- All form values stored in a simple list for easy validation and submission

author: brianduff
body:
## Summary

Fix-forward for the 2026-05-07 incident where workers reported `ECONNREFUSED` on every hook for ~45 minutes while `bossctl agents list` showed the engine healthy. The events.sock was bound but not in the kernel listen state, and the on-disk file's mtime was 42 minutes younger than the engine pid — invisible to anyone reading process state alone.

tokio's `UnixListener::bind` does call `socket(2)` + `bind(2)` + `listen(2)` together, so the bind+listen *itself* was already atomic. The actual fragility was elsewhere: the `if path.exists() { remove_file }` gate races/lies on dangling symlinks, and there was no audit/log signal for "the accept loop is actually running," so a triage 45 minutes in had only mtime archaeology to work with.

This change:

- **Both sockets** (`/tmp/boss-engine.sock` and `events.sock`) now unconditionally `remove_file` and ignore `NotFound`, instead of gating on `path.exists()`. Dangling symlinks and concurrent file ops can't drop the unlink anymore. Every other error is fatal — the engine refuses to come up rather than proceed with a partially-bound socket.
- **`bind_events_socket`** documents the bind+listen atomicity contract callers depend on, with a regression test that `connect()`s immediately after bind (no `accept()` polled) and a second test that rebinds over a stale socket file and verifies the rebound socket accepts connections. The bind path now emits `tracing::info!` for unlink-stale-file and bind+listen-succeeded.
- **`record_accept_loop_started`** is a new audit record. Emitted once per socket (frontend + events) immediately before the first `accept()` poll. The audit log now reads `start` → `socket_bound` → `accept_loop_started` for both sockets, so the next person triaging an "engine appears healthy but workers can't connect" failure has timestamps instead of `ls -la`.

A bind/listen failure still propagates straight up to `main`, which records the failure in the audit log and exits non-zero — partially-bound sockets never reach the dispatch loop.

## Acceptance per the work item

- After a fresh engine start, both `/tmp/boss-engine.sock` and `events.sock` accept connections immediately. Verified with the new `connect_succeeds_immediately_after_bind` test which polls `connect()` from a separate thread before the listener is ever polled.
- Engine survives kill-without-cleanup. Verified with the new `rebind_after_stale_file_listens` test which leaves a stale socket file from a prior bind, then rebinds and asserts the rebound socket is in the listen state.
- Engine logs print socket-lifecycle events at `info` level: `frontend socket: unlinked stale file before bind`, `frontend socket: accept loop started`, `events socket: unlinked stale file before bind`, `events socket: bind+listen succeeded`, `events socket: accept loop started`. Audit log mirrors with `socket_bound` and the new `accept_loop_started` record.

## Out of scope (explicit per the work item)

- Worker reconnect — sibling task.
- Merging the two sockets — sibling task.

## Test plan

- [x] `cargo test --lib events_socket` — all 13 tests pass, including the two new regression tests.
- [x] `cargo test --lib -- --test-threads=1` — all 242 lib tests pass. (The audit module's pre-existing tests share a `OnceLock` and are flaky in parallel; this PR doesn't change that.)
- [x] `bazel test //tools/boss/engine/... //tools/boss/event-shim/...` — all green.
- [x] `bazel build //tools/boss/...` — full tree builds.
- [ ] Smoke test: kill engine, restart, verify `python3 -c 'import socket; s=socket.socket(socket.AF_UNIX,socket.SOCK_STREAM); s.connect("<path>"); print("ok")'` works for both paths immediately. Recommended to run before merging.

## Summary
The doctor's Pending Review queue was sorting purely by wait time, so within the same priority bucket every case looked equal. This adds a clinical severity score that bubbles the most acute cases to the top, plus a third P2 demo account at the low-severity end so the rotation is visible in the demo.

## Severity score (0–100, higher = more urgent)
- Priority weight: P1 = 80, P2 = 40, P3 = 10
- Pain component: `min(pain_score × 3, 30)`
- High-risk pain location boost (chest / abdomen / head / back): +10

|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Encik Faisal | **71** HIGH | P2(40) + pain 7 (21) + abdomen (10) |

| 3 | Pak Ramli (new) | **46** MODERATE | P2(40) + pain 2 (6) + no risky location |

- `lib/session-store.ts` — `pain_score` / `pain_location` added to `CaseRecord`

- `app/doctor/page.tsx` — `severityScore()` + `severityBand()` utilities, sort by severity desc + wait-time tiebreaker, colored severity badge per row
- `lib/demo-users.ts` — 4th P2 demo account: `0155555555` (Pak Ramli)
- `app/login/page.tsx` — surfaces Pak Ramli in the pre-seeded list, adds pain context to existing labels

## Test plan
- [ ] Login as each pre-seeded P2 (Faisal / Aishah / Ramli) → run triage → check case lands in doctor queue with the right severity score
- [ ] Doctor's Pending Review queue shows them sorted Faisal → Aishah → Ramli regardless of submission order
- [ ] Severity badge colors match (HIGH=red, ELEVATED=amber, MODERATE=blue)
- [ ] Existing P1 (Hassan) and P3 (Maya) flows still work
- [ ] No regression: manually-typed cases (Ahmad / Siti) still work without `pain_score` set

author: banks003
body:
Today's refresh hit the 90-min workflow timeout silently inside the
SCD2 SQL execution. The existing stage markers solve "which stage
owned the kill" but a healthy long-running stage looks identical to a
hung stage — operationally indistinguishable. This change makes the
silence go away on the long stages.

Two additions, no behaviour change in the pipeline itself:

1. stdlib logging adoption.

   - One ``logging.basicConfig`` call at the start of the ``run``
     command. Idempotent (basicConfig only configures on first call),
     stdout-only, format ``%(asctime)s %(name)s %(levelname)s %(message)s``.
     Tests don't get an unsolicited config because the function only
     fires when ``run`` actually executes.
   - ``logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)`` at module scope.
   - The existing ``_Stage`` class swaps ``click.echo(..., err=True)``
     for ``logger.info`` / ``logger.error``. Same payload, leading
     timestamp + module name come for free from the formatter. The
     failure path uses ERROR level so it's visually distinct in the
     workflow log.
   - The user-facing CLI output (e.g. ``Catalog: extract …``) still
     uses ``click.echo`` — that's command output, not log telemetry,
     and shouldn't carry the timestamp + level prefix.

2. _Heartbeat context manager.

   Daemon-thread heartbeat that emits ``[heartbeat] <name> alive at Ns
   elapsed (rss=X GB)`` every ``every_seconds`` (default 60). Stops on
   context exit via a threading.Event; thread is daemon so it never
   blocks process exit. Wrapped via ``with _stage(name), _heartbeat(name)``
   pattern so a single ``with`` line gets both timing + heartbeat.

   Wired into the two stages without natural progress signals:

   - ``build search index`` — DuckDB-driven join over main + trading,
     opaque from outside.
   - ``iceberg.<table> (bootstrap|update)`` — every_seconds=30 because
     this is the one we most want to observe; the bigger the gaps in
     output, the harder it is to know whether the SCD2 SQL is making
     progress.

Smoke-tested all four code paths (start/done timing, heartbeat firing
on schedule, nested stage+heartbeat, exception path with ERROR level).
129 tests passing locally; ruff clean.

Closes #27.

<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

## Motivation

Add sliding-window attention support to EAGLE series models. Related to #24663, in our upcoming paper we showed how SWA can help increase acceptance lengths if model is not trained to handle long context lengths. Some models are not usable without SWA as their training length is usually short (2-4K).

## Modifications

1. Add SWA support to EAGLE via CLI flag `--speculative-draft-window-size`, which defaults to None to disable SWA.
2. Support SWA in llama_eagle3.py
3. Unify D-Flash's SWA and EAGLE's SWA flags.

## Accuracy Tests

MT-Bench on gpt-oss-20b and llama3.1 ensured acceptance lengths are the same when SWA is disabled.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Qwen3.5 or GPT-oss-20b drafter accuracies are less effected by long context as they have internal sliding window layers. However some models like Llama 3.1 8B's accuracy hurts pretty badly when context length exceeds trained context length.

**Benchmark**: MT-Bench (80 questions)
**Temperature**: 0.7
**Max Tokens**: 2048

### Context Pre-fill: 32K tokens — gpt-oss-20b drafter

**Config 64-5-1-6**
| Setting  | Latency (s) | Output Throughput (tok/s) | Accept Length |
|----------|-------------|---------------------------|---------------|
| No SWA   | 72.38       | 1341.76                   | 2.370         |

|----------|-------------|---------------------------|---------------|
| No SWA   | 324.49      | 303.81                    | 2.401         |
| SWA=2048 | 311.974     | 324.83                    | 2.5576        |

body:
## Summary

PR A of the followed-countries watchlist primitive. Lays the foundation for personalization across the dashboard: per-user country watchlist with a server-authoritative free-tier cap, per-country reverse lookups for future fan-out (digest, breaking-news), and a reusable FollowButton mounted on three panel surfaces.

Plan: [`docs/plans/2026-05-02-001-feat-followed-countries-watchlist-primitive-plan.md`](docs/plans/2026-05-02-001-feat-followed-countries-watchlist-primitive-plan.md) — Codex-approved after 6 deepening rounds.

### What ships in PR A

- **Convex schema:** three new tables — `followedCountries` rows, `followedCountriesCounts` aggregate counter, `followedCountriesUserMeta` per-user serialization doc — with indexes `by_user`, `by_country`, `by_user_country`. Constants in `convex/constants.ts`: `FREE_TIER_FOLLOW_LIMIT=3`, `MAX_MERGE_INPUT=100`, `COUNTRY_COUNT_PRIVACY_FLOOR=5`.
- **Three mutations** (server-authoritative cap with **OCC-serialized per-user writes**, idempotency, atomic counter, ISO-2 registry validation, `ConvexError({kind})` typed errors): `followCountry`, `unfollowCountry`, `mergeAnonymousLocal`.
- **Three queries:** `listFollowed` (auth'd reactive), `countFollowers` (public, counter-table-backed O(1) with privacy floor), `listFollowersPage` (`internalQuery`, paginated cursor).
- **`/relay/followed-countries`** HTTP action — RELAY_SHARED_SECRET-gated; consumed by PR C's brief composer.
- **Client service** (`src/services/followed-countries.ts`) — three modes (anonymous / handoffPending / signed-in), auth-state listener with `_handoffGeneration` race guards, user-scoped subscription snapshot, cross-tab `storage` event, ConvexError → reason mapping, max-retry + exponential backoff with `failed-permanent` terminal state.
- **`FollowButton`** helper mounted on `CountryDeepDivePanel`, `CountryIntelModal`, and CIIPanel rows with proper teardown bookkeeping; exhaustive switch (`assertNever`) and `inFlight` busy-state.

### Implementation units (8)

- U1 ISO-2 normalizer · U12 schema · U13 mutations · U14 queries+relay · U2 service · U3 sign-in handoff · U4 FollowButton · U5 mount on 3 surfaces

### Test plan

- [x] `npm run typecheck` — clean
- [x] `npm run typecheck:api` — clean
- [x] `npm run test:convex` — **292 pass** (70 new tests)
- [x] `npm run test:data` — **7913 pass** (98 new tests)
- [x] Unit + integration coverage for: ISO-2 registry parity (set-equality, not just size), free-tier cap, idempotency, counter atomicity, sign-in handoff race guards, user-scoped snapshot leak prevention, anonymous-vs-loading distinction, `INPUT_TOO_LARGE` permanent-error classification, max-retry exhaustion, cross-tab storage sync, post-await auth re-check, FollowButton rapid double-click suppression, relay endpoint validation, privacy floor edges (4 vs 5), **concurrent same-user mutations preserve cap (TOCTOU)**

### Code review

Full `/ce-code-review` ran (13 reviewers). 19 of 19 actionable findings resolved across 5 follow-up commits including the P0 TOCTOU. Run artifact: `.context/compound-engineering/ce-code-review/20260502-195816-dae403d7/`.

### TOCTOU resolution (originally P0; fixed in `9b7dd885f`)

Convex per-document OCC tracks reads at the document level, not the index-range level. Two parallel `followCountry({country: 'US'})` from the same user could both pass the empty-row check and both insert. Fix: a per-user serialization document (`followedCountriesUserMeta`) that every mutation reads + writes. Concurrent same-user mutations now serialize via Convex's per-document OCC; the loser retries against the winner's commit and either passes correctly (still under cap), fails with `FREE_CAP` (cap now reached), or returns idempotent (row now exists for same `(userId, country)`). The denormalized count on the meta row also makes the cap check O(1) for both free and PRO paths.

`convex-test` does NOT simulate true concurrency (verified: it serializes mutations under a per-function lock). The new tests instead assert the **final-state invariant** (cap holds, no duplicate `(userId, country)`, count parity) under back-to-back execution, which is the exact behavior production OCC retry produces. Documented inline.

### Known issues — deferred to follow-up

**P2 — `countFollowers` unrate-limited.** Public unauthenticated query; needs Vercel edge route wrapper for rate limiting. Not pure Convex code; deferred to its own PR.

### Next: PR B (consumer wiring)

CII pin-to-top (followed countries first), "Followed only" filter chip on country-scoped panels, deep-dive star sub-action wired to alert-rule create form pre-fill.

### Plan + design

- Plan: [`docs/plans/2026-05-02-001-feat-followed-countries-watchlist-primitive-plan.md`](docs/plans/2026-05-02-001-feat-followed-countries-watchlist-primitive-plan.md) (1057 lines, deepened + Codex-approved)
- Codex review: 6 rounds total (1 initial + 4 revise + 1 final approval after architecture deepening from opaque-blob → dedicated table)

## Summary

Replace nodemailer SMTP transport + transactional outbox + cron dispatcher in `@repo/mail` with the SendSay HTTP API (`sendsay-api`) and switch every email send to synchronous. Remove the Mailhog dev container and all SMTP/MAIL_FROM/MAIL_DISPATCH env vars.

- **`@repo/mail`** — `nodemailer` is gone; new `sendsay.ts` wrapper hits `issue.send` on SendSay's HTTP API. `sendMailNow(args)` keeps the same signature (kind/to/data) but routes through SendSay. `enqueueMailEvent`, `dispatchPending`, `getMailTransport`, and the SMTP `transport.ts` are deleted. Sender is hardcoded to `noreply@anynote.ru` (must be a verified domain on the SendSay account).
- **Dev/CI fallback** — when `SENDSAY_API_KEY` is unset, `sendMailNow` logs `[mail] sendsay disabled (no SENDSAY_API_KEY); would send to <addr>: <subject>` and returns. Keeps Playwright and local dev running without SendSay credentials.
- **`@repo/auth`** — `afterEmailVerification` and the verified-user branch in `databaseHooks.user.create.after` now call `sendMailNow` directly (welcome mail). All sends synchronous.
- **`apps/engines`** — `MailerModule` and the cron dispatcher deleted; `@repo/mail` workspace dependency removed (and the matching prebuild step in the engines Dockerfile).
- **`compose.yml`** — `mailhog` service removed.
- **CI/deploy** — `playwright.config.ts`, `turbo.json`, `deploy/.env.template`, `.github/workflows/{deploy,ci,release}.yml` no longer reference SMTP/MAIL/MAIL_DISPATCH; deploy workflow now passes `SENDSAY_API_URL` + `SENDSAY_API_KEY` secrets through envsubst.
- **E2E** — `apps/e2e/helpers/{mailhog,dispatch-emails}.ts` and `auth-extended.spec.ts` deleted (they captured rendered HTML via Mailhog SMTP — incompatible with HTTP-API sends). Other specs use `signUpAndAuthAs` which sets `emailVerified=true` directly in Prisma, so they're unaffected.
- **Docs** — `CLAUDE.md`, `AGENTS.md`, `README.md` describe the new sync-send model and drop Mailhog/SMTP narrative.

The `outbox_events` table itself stays — the page indexer still uses it (`aggregateType='page'`). Only `aggregateType='email'` rows go away naturally; no migration needed.

## Required setup before merge

The SendSay account's verified sender domain must allow `noreply@anynote.ru`. The `SENDSAY_API_URL` and `SENDSAY_API_KEY` secrets are already configured at the GitHub repository level — verify they're populated before triggering a deploy.

## Test plan

- [ ] CI green on this PR (lint + check-types + build + tests across 23 workspace tasks).
- [ ] Pull, run `docker compose up -d` (no Mailhog now), then `pnpm dev` — sign up locally, confirm the `[mail] sendsay disabled` log appears for verify-email/welcome (no real send).
- [ ] On staging or a deploy with `SENDSAY_API_KEY` set, sign up with a real address, confirm verify-email arrives, click the link, confirm welcome arrives.
- [ ] Trigger `request password reset`, confirm reset-password mail arrives and the link works once.
- [ ] Confirm the production deploy workflow runs envsubst clean (no unsubstituted `${SMTP_*}` placeholders survive — the deploy step's grep gate catches this automatically).

body:
## 개요

agency-stub 모듈을 완전한 OIDC 클라이언트로 구현했습니다.
이전 PoC stub 코드를 실제 동작하는 구현으로 전면 교체합니다.

---

## 구현 내용

### 신규 파일 (7개)

| 파일 | 역할 |
|------|------|
| `AgencyWebConfig.java` | RestTemplate(CB/Retry 적용) + ObjectMapper Bean + AgencyApiKeyInterceptor 등록 |
| `AgencyApiKeyInterceptor.java` | X-Agency-Code + X-Agency-Key 헤더 검증 (SHA-256 DB 비교, 원문 로그 미기록) |
| `IdoVerifyClient.java` | POST /api/v1/handoff/verify 실제 HTTP 호출 + Resilience4j CB/Retry |
| `AgencySessionService.java` | 기관 세션 DB 완전 구현 (생성/조회/갱신/무효화/멱등처리) |
| `WebhookInboundController.java` | POST /api/v1/webhook/inbound — HMAC-SHA256 서명 검증 + 이벤트 처리 |
| `AgencyEventPollingController.java` | GET /api/v1/events/poll — priority 기반 폴링 (Option B) |
| `V2__add_webhook_and_api_key.sql` | agency_api_key / webhook_inbound / agency_event_queue 테이블 |

### 수정 파일 (5개)

| 파일 | 변경 내용 |
|------|-----------|
| `AgencyEntryController.java` | stub callIdoVerify() → IdoVerifyClient 실제 호출 / AgencySessionService DB 세션 / 로그아웃 엔드포인트 추가 |
| `HandoffEventConsumer.java` | JdbcTemplate 직접 조작 → AgencySessionService 위임 리팩토링 |
| `build.gradle.kts` | resilience4j-spring-boot3:2.2.0, spring-boot-starter-aop, jackson-datatype-jsr310 추가 |
| `application.yml` | Resilience4j CB/Retry 설정 + webhook.signing-secret 추가 |
| `docker-compose.yml` | onepass-agency-stub 서비스 (172.20.0.25:8084) 추가 |

---

## 완성된 OIDC 클라이언트 요청 흐름

```
[기관 앱]
  │
  ├─ POST /agency/entry?ticketId=XXX
  │     Header: X-Agency-Code: AGENCY_STUB_001
  │             X-Agency-Key:  stub-api-key-dev-001
  │
  ├─[1] AgencyApiKeyInterceptor
  │       SHA-256(rawKey) → agency_api_key 테이블 DB 검증
  │
  ├─[2] IdoVerifyClient.verify()
  │       POST http://onepass-ido:8083/api/v1/handoff/verify
  │       CircuitBreaker "ido-verify" (실패율 50% → 10s OPEN)
  │       Retry 2회 (5xx·네트워크 오류만)
  │       4xx → 즉시 REJECTED / CB OPEN → HOLD fallback
  │
  ├─[3] HandoffState 검증
  │       HOLD     → 503 (재시도 유도)
  │       REJECTED → 403
  │       APPROVED → 계속
  │
  ├─[4] Session Fixation 방지
  │       기존 AGSID → DB invalidate + 쿠키 삭제
  │
  └─[5] AgencySessionService.createSession()
          SecureRandom 192-bit → rawAGSID (쿠키)
          SHA-256(rawAGSID)    → DB 저장 (원문 미저장)
          agency_local_session INSERT
          AGSID 쿠키 발급 (Secure/HttpOnly/SameSite=Strict)
```

### Webhook 수신 흐름 (Option A — Push)
```
IdO WebhookDispatchOutboxRelay
  → POST /api/v1/webhook/inbound
     X-Webhook-Signature: sha256=HEX...
     X-Webhook-Timestamp: {epochSeconds}
  → [1] 타임스탬프 ±5분 검증 (재사용 공격 방지)
  → [2] HMAC-SHA256 서명 검증 (상수 시간 비교)
  → [3] webhook_inbound INSERT (중복 source_event_id 차단)
  → [4] 이벤트별 처리:
         HANDOFF_REVOKED  → invalidateByTicketId()
         SESSION_ADVISORY → invalidateByQimUserId() (Mandatory만)
         HANDOFF_ISSUED   → agency_event_queue 적재 (priority=3)
  → [5] 200 ACCEPTED
```

### 폴링 흐름 (Option B — Pull)
```
기관 앱 → GET /api/v1/events/poll?limit=20
  ← { events: [...], count: N }
     (delivered=TRUE 마킹 → 중복 배달 방지)
```

---

## 보안 특성

| 항목 | 구현 방법 |
|------|-----------|
| API Key 원문 미저장 | SHA-256(rawKey) → DB 저장, 로그 마스킹 |
| AGSID 엔트로피 | SecureRandom 192-bit → Base64URL |
| AGSID DB 저장 | SHA-256(rawAGSID) — 원문 서버 미보관 |
| Session Fixation 방지 | Verify 성공 직후 기존 AGSID DB 무효화 |
| Webhook 서명 검증 | HMAC-SHA256 + 상수 시간 비교 (타이밍 공격 방지) |
| 재사용 공격 방지 | X-Webhook-Timestamp ±5분 검증 |
| 중복 이벤트 방지 | source_event_id + agency_code UNIQUE 인덱스 |

---

## 컴파일 검증

```
./gradlew compileJava → BUILD SUCCESSFUL (전체 모듈: platform-common, agency-stub, ido, q-im, q-sign)
./gradlew :agency-stub:build -x test → BUILD SUCCESSFUL
```

- [ ] agency-stub Docker 네트워크 외부망 격리 (별도 브리지 네트워크)

body:
## Summary

Introduces a `StorageProvider` interface in `src/lib/storage.ts` and moves the package image filesystem operations (upload, delete) behind it. The only provider implemented is `LocalStorageProvider`, which preserves the existing `public/uploads/` behavior exactly. A `STORAGE_PROVIDER` env var (defaulting to `"local"`) selects the provider via a factory function, making it straightforward to add S3/R2/MinIO providers later without touching the API route.

The package images API route (`/api/packages/[id]/images`) is updated to import and use the `storage` singleton instead of calling `fs/promises` directly. No changes to API request/response shapes, role guards, validation, or DB operations.

**Files changed (2):**
- `src/lib/storage.ts` — new file: `StorageProvider` interface, `LocalStorageProvider` class, `createStorage` factory
- `src/app/api/packages/[id]/images/route.ts` — replaced direct `fs` calls with `storage.upload()` / `storage.delete()`

## Review & Testing Checklist for Human

- [ ] **Verify URL format is preserved**: Old code produced `/uploads/packages/{id}-{timestamp}-{name}`. New code calls `storage.upload(buffer, "packages/{id}-{timestamp}-{name}")` which returns `/uploads/packages/...` via `getUrl`. Confirm these are identical so existing DB records and image URLs remain valid.
- [ ] **Verify DELETE key extraction**: The delete handler uses `image.imageUrl.replace(/^\/uploads\//, "")` to recover the storage key from the DB-stored URL. This assumes all `imageUrl` values start with `/uploads/`. Check that no existing records have a different prefix (e.g. a full URL or different path).
- [ ] **Test upload + delete round-trip**: Upload an image via `POST /api/packages/{id}/images`, confirm the file appears in `public/uploads/packages/` and the response `imageUrl` is correct. Then delete it and confirm the file is removed from disk and DB.

### Notes
- The `storage` singleton is created at module load time using `process.cwd()`. This matches Next.js behavior where `cwd()` is stable, but differs slightly from the old code which called `process.cwd()` at each request. Should be fine in practice.
- Unknown `STORAGE_PROVIDER` values silently fall through to `local` via the `default` case — intentional for safety but could mask typos in future config.
- To add a cloud provider (e.g. S3), you would: (1) add a new class implementing `StorageProvider`, (2) add a `case "s3":` in `createStorage()`, (3) set `STORAGE_PROVIDER=s3` in env. No changes to the API route needed.

author: airspeedswift
body:
`emitThrow` previously asserted that the only legal mismatch between the in-flight error type and the throw destination was `any Error`, then existential-erased to `Error`. Anything else Sema accepted — `do throws(any P) where P: Error`, or a class subtype of the destination — crashed the assertion (or, before that was tightened, miscompiled at runtime).

Dispatch on the destination type:
- existential: erase, looking up conformance to each protocol in the destination's existential layout (so `any P` works, not just `any Error`);
- class: emit an `upcast`.

Anything else still hits an `unreachable` — Sema rejects those today, so hitting it would indicate a Sema regression rather than a missing SILGen path.

Fixes https://github.com/swiftlang/swift/issues/83826.

author: bonerush
body: 修复在 dev 模式下按下 Ctrl+O 切换 transcript 视图时 React 抛出 "Rendered fewer hooks than expected" 崩溃的问题。 Fixes #434 ## 根因分析 项目中有大量 hook（useState / useMemo / useRef / useSyncExternalStore 等） 被包裹在 `feature()` 三元表达式中条件调用，例如： const value = feature('X') ? useHook() : defaultValue; 在 build 模式下 `feature()` 是编译时常量，死代码消除会移除未使用的分支， hooks 数量在编译后是确定的。但在 dev 模式下（scripts/dev.ts 注入 --feature 启用全部 31 个 feature），`feature()` 是运行时调用， 但始终返回 true，因此所有 hooks 都会被调用，原本不会出问题。 真正的触发器是 REPL.tsx 第 5381 行的提前返回： if (screen === 'transcript') { return transcriptReturn; } 当用户按下 Ctrl+O 进入 transcript 模式时，该提前返回之后的所有 hooks （如 displayedAgentMessages 的 useMemo）都不会被调用，导致 React 在 下一次渲染时检测到 hooks 数量与上次不一致而崩溃。 此外，其他文件中也存在相同的条件式 hook 模式——虽然 dev 模式下 feature() 返回 true，所以这些路径实际上不会被触发，但它们是 潜在的隐患：若将来有人通过环境变量关闭某个 feature， 同样的崩溃会立即出现。 ## 修复策略 采用统一模式：**始终无条件调用 hook，将 feature() gate 应用到值上**。 // Before (unsafe — hook count varies by feature flag) const value = feature('X') ? useHook() : defaultValue; // After (safe — hook always called, gate on the value) const rawValue = useHook(); const value = feature('X') ? rawValue : defaultValue; ## 修改清单 ### 核心修复（REPL.tsx） - 将 `displayedAgentMessages` useMemo 及依赖变量（viewedTask / viewedTeammateTask / viewedAgentTask / usesSyncMessages / rawAgentMessages / displayedMessages）从 transcript 提前返回 之后移至之前，确保两模式下 hooks 调用顺序一致 - 修复 `disableMessageActions` / `useAssistantHistory` / `voiceIntegration` 的条件式 hook 调用 ### 条件式 hook 修复（11 个文件） - src/hooks/useGlobalKeybindings.tsx — isBriefOnly / toggleBrief keybinding 改为 isActive 门控 - src/hooks/useReplBridge.tsx — 5 个 BRIDGE_MODE 选值改为无条件调用 - src/hooks/useVoiceIntegration.tsx — 4 个 VOICE_MODE 选值修复 - src/components/PromptInput/Notifications.tsx — 4 个 feature 选值修复 - src/components/PromptInput/PromptInput.tsx — briefOwnsGap / companionSpeaking 修复 - src/components/PromptInput/PromptInputFooterLeftSide.tsx — 4 个 VOICE_MODE 选值修复 - src/components/PromptInput/PromptInputQueuedCommands.tsx — isBriefOnly - src/components/Spinner.tsx — briefEnvEnabled 修复 - src/components/TextInput.tsx — voiceState / audioLevels / animationFrame 修复 - src/components/messages/AttachmentMessage.tsx — isDemoEnv 修复 - src/components/messages/UserPromptMessage.tsx — isBriefOnly / viewingAgentTaskId / briefEnvEnabled 修复 - src/components/messages/UserToolResultMessage/UserToolSuccessMessage.tsx — isBriefOnly 修复 ### 其他修复 - src/components/FeedbackSurvey/useFrustrationDetection.ts — 将 3 个 提前返回合并为 shouldSkip 变量，handleTranscriptSelect 提前 return - src/hooks/useIssueFlagBanner.ts — useRef 移到 USER_TYPE 检查之前 - src/hooks/useUpdateNotification.ts — useState 改为 useRef， 避免版本号变化触发不必要重渲染 ### 构建/开发配置 - build.ts — 添加 `sourcemap: 'linked'` - scripts/dev.ts — NODE_ENV 从 'production' 改为 'development' --- Need help on this PR? Tag @codesmith with what you need. - [ ] Let Codesmith autofix CI failures and bot reviews ## Summary by CodeRabbit * **Chores** * Enhanced build tooling with source map support for improved debugging capability. * Improved development environment configuration. * **Refactor** * Restructured internal state management patterns to improve reliability and consistency. * Optimized feature flag handling across the application for more predictable behavior.

author: pawansingh3889
body:
Closes #42.

T-SQL accepts `UPDATE customers SET status = o.status FROM customers c, orders o WHERE c.customer_id = o.customer_id`. The comma form is a legacy implicit join: get the WHERE wrong (or omit it) and every row in the target table is updated against the Cartesian product. Silent data corruption, no syntax error.

Reported as `severity = error` rather than warning, because the failure mode is a write that touches every row of a table, not a read. The sister rule S001 covers SELECT FROM comma-joins as a warning.

Implementation mirrors the post-fix S001 from #46. Walk from each `UPDATE` keyword to the next `FROM`, then forward through the FROM clause tracking parenthesis depth, stop at `WHERE` / `GROUP BY` / `ORDER BY` / `HAVING` / `LIMIT` / explicit `JOIN` / `UNION` / `EXCEPT` / `INTERSECT`, and flag the first depth-0 comma. The `strip_strings_and_comments` helper that S001 introduced has been lifted to `sql_guard.rules.base` (first commit of this PR) so E009 reuses it without duplicating the regexes.

Deliberate suppression cases:

```sql
UPDATE c SET tag = sub.tag FROM customers c, LATERAL (SELECT tag FROM tags WHERE customer_id = c.id LIMIT 1) sub;
UPDATE customers SET status = o.status FROM orders o WHERE customers.id = o.customer_id;
UPDATE customers SET status = 'active' WHERE id = 1;
UPDATE c SET c.status = o.status FROM customers c INNER JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id;
```

LATERAL after a comma is a real Snowflake / Postgres lateral join. Postgres canonical UPDATE FROM with a single table is the recommended form. Plain UPDATE with no FROM is fine. The recommended fix from the rule message must not flag itself.

Tests: 7 new methods on `TestErrorRules` covering the issue example via the fixture, the recommended fix, Postgres single-table UPDATE FROM, LATERAL after comma, plain UPDATE without FROM, three-table comma join, and multi-line comma join. Plus an E009 line added to `tests/fixtures/errors.sql`.

Four commits on this branch. The first is a behaviour-preserving refactor lifting `strip_strings_and_comments` from `structural.py` to `base.py` so E009 reuses it. The next adds the rule in `errors.py` and registers it; registry counts move to 40 total and 11 errors. The third adds tests and the fixture line. The fourth documents the rule in CHANGELOG under `[Unreleased]` `Added`.

Full suite: 226 pass, 1 skipped. No regressions. Commits signed (ED25519).

author: themostrabidraccoon
body:
## Summary

Diagnosed every `"Memory extraction failed: Expecting value: line 1 column 1 (char 0)"` entry in the audit log. The error is identical across all failures because they share the same architectural cause: `extract_memory_delta` was calling `call_claude` after PR #16 added native tool-use, which broke the contract that extraction relies on.

## Two interacting bugs

**1. Tool-use loop consuming the output.** `call_claude` registers all 7 swarm_tools. When asked to extract memory, Claude sometimes investigates via `filestore_search` etc. before answering. The wrapper returns no text (only tool_use blocks). `json.loads("")` → "char 0" error.

**2. Role bleed from the persona prompt.** `call_claude` uses the full `"You are Claude, the Backbone node..."` system prompt plus `PERSISTENT_MEMORY_PROTOCOL`. The `MEMORY_EXTRACTION_PROMPT` in the user message ALSO assigns a role (*"You are the swarm's memory curator..."*). Two competing role assignments degrade output even when the loop succeeds.

## Observed impact

Conductor's swarm has **32 user-driven loops** post-corpus on disk, but only **~4 increments to `session_count`**. The other ~28 sessions ran extraction, hit one of these failure modes, logged silently, and the swarm "forgot" them.

## Fix

`extract_memory_delta` now calls `client.messages.create` directly:

- **No tools** registered — extraction is JSON-only by contract
- **Tight system prompt**: *"You extract structured memory ... Your only output is valid JSON. No prose, no preamble, no tool use, no markdown fences."*
- **`max_tokens` 2000 → 4000** — complex transcripts were producing deltas that the old cap truncated mid-JSON
- **Better error logging** — JSON parse failures now log the first 500 chars of Claude's actual response so future failures are diagnosable

## Why not just add a `tools=False` flag to `call_claude`?

Considered, rejected. Even with the flag, role bleed remains because `call_claude` always uses the persona system prompt. Memory extraction needs a different system prompt anyway. Inlining the API call is clearer than parameterizing for the one caller that needs this exact contract.

## Test plan

- [x] Syntax check passes
- [x] Module imports cleanly
- [ ] **Live**: run a `/start-loop` session and confirm `session_count` increments by 1 after synthesis (no JSON parse error in audit log)
- [ ] **Live**: complex/long transcript no longer truncates mid-JSON
- [ ] **Followup PR (post-AIES)**: backfill 32 existing post-corpus loops by running `scripts/distill_corpus.py` against `Logs_v2_live` to recover the memory the swarm "forgot"

body: ## Summary Closes #255 — prevents duplicate category names within the same parent level, with real-time typeahead feedback showing existing siblings as you type. **Backend:** Sibling-scoped duplicate validation on create (`POST /api/categories`) and rename (`PUT /api/categories/{id}`). Returns `409 Conflict` when a duplicate is detected. Same name under different parents is allowed. **Frontend:** Both `AddCategoryDialog` and `EditCategoryDialog` now use MUI `Autocomplete` (`freeSolo`) to show existing sibling names as the user types. An exact match (case-insensitive) immediately shows a red error state with "This name already exists at this level" helper text — no submission required. The `ManageCategoriesDialog` computes `siblingNames` from the already-loaded flat category tree (no extra API calls). | Scenario | Result | |----------|--------| | Type an existing sibling name | Autocomplete dropdown shows match; text field turns red | | Create with duplicate sibling name | 409 error, dialog stays open with Alert | | Same name under different parent | Allowed (succeeds) | | Rename to existing sibling name | 409 error, dialog stays open with Alert | ## Review & Testing Checklist for Human - [ ] Open Manage > Categories as admin. Click `+` next to "Root level" and start typing "Arch" — verify the autocomplete dropdown shows "Architecture" and the field turns red when you type the full name - [ ] Click `+` next to a category (e.g. Panoramas) and type a name that exists under a different parent (e.g. "American") — verify no error, creation succeeds - [ ] Click the pencil on a category and type an existing sibling's name — verify the field turns red and the dropdown shows the match - [ ] Confirm the autocomplete dropdown only shows siblings at the same level, not categories from other parts of the tree ### Notes The Autocomplete uses `freeSolo` so the user can type any new name — the dropdown is purely informational, showing existing siblings that match as a heads-up. author: svalench
body:
## Release v0.2.0 — LangGraph integration

This PR brings the **complete LangGraph integration** (Sprints 3 and 4, which were merged into the stacked feature branches but never reached `main`) plus the version bump and packaging metadata required to publish to PyPI.

### What's included

#### Sprint 3 — Conversational search
- New `POST /api/search/conversation/` endpoint with session memory.
- `langgraph_conversation` module + 5-node graph (`load_context → interpret_followup → maybe_clarify → execute_search → store_context`).
- Pluggable memory backends: `inmemory`, `cache` (`DjangoCacheBackend`), bring-your-own.
- Deterministic follow-up handling for "more / similar / filter X" patterns.
- Gated behind `CONVERSATIONAL.ENABLED=False` by default.

#### Sprint 4 — Smart indexing, streaming, hardening
- `SmartIndexer` produces structured per-section documents (`Title:`, `Description:`, `Category:` …).
- New `get_indexer()` factory; signals, `index()`, and `build_search_index` route through it transparently.
- `events.EventHub` and `StreamingSearchAPIView` (NDJSON / SSE) at `/api/search/stream/`.
- All flags default to `False` — public API unchanged.

#### Release plumbing
- Version bumped `0.1.2 → 0.2.0`.
- Real package metadata in `setup.cfg` (author, URL, keywords, `project_urls`, Django 5.x classifiers, `Development Status :: 4 - Beta`).
- `CHANGELOG.md` documenting every Sprint 1–4 change.
- `MANIFEST.in` ships `CHANGELOG.md` in the sdist.

### Backwards compatibility
- All new functionality is **off by default**. Upgrading from `0.1.x` is behaviourally a no-op.
- Public surface (`Searcher`, `Indexer`, REST endpoints, signals) is preserved.
- No new mandatory dependencies — `langgraph`, LLM SDKs, Redis all remain optional.

### Quality gates
- **58 / 58 tests pass** (`python -m pytest tests/`).
- `python -m build` produces both wheel and sdist.
- `python -m twine check dist/*` → PASSED for both artifacts.
- New modules verified to be packaged into the wheel.

### Release procedure (after merge)
1. Tag `v0.2.0` on `main`.

author: marianfoo
body:
## Summary

Follow-up to #218 and PR #219. After @oisee flagged that `'FUNC/FM': 'FUNC'` in
`SLASH_TYPE_MAP` is also wrong (function modules don't exist as TADIR rows; the real ADT
slash form is `FUGR/FF`), this PR systematically audits **every** ABAP object type ARC-1
exposes — 35 canonical short types and 24 slash-form aliases — against TADIR truth,
abap-file-formats, the Eclipse ADT plugin source, the live a4h S/4HANA test system, and
SAP docs/notes.

This PR is **research-only** — no source-code changes. It produces:
- 36 per-type evidence docs in `research/abap-types/types/`
- A methodology doc (`00-methodology.md`) and inventory (`01-inventory.md`)
- A master synthesis (`02-master-overview.md`)
- Three ralphex plans in `docs/plans/` for the follow-up implementation work

## Findings

Five bugs of the same class as `STRU/DS`, plus two structural issues, plus an
architectural smell:

### P0 — invented or mis-routed slash aliases

| Bug | Real form | Currently | Should be |
|---|---|---|---|
| `FUNC/FM` is invented (issue #218 follow-up) | (does not exist) | `FUNC/FM → FUNC` | (remove) |
| `FUGR/FF` mis-routes | `FUGR/FF` (function module) | `→ FUGR` | `→ FUNC` |
| `VIEW/V` is invented | `VIEW/DV` | `VIEW/V → VIEW` | `VIEW/DV → VIEW` |
| `VIEW` URL is missing | `/sap/bc/adt/vit/wb/object_type/viewdv/object_name/` | falls through to `/programs/programs/` | add VIT URL |
| `CLAS/LI` is invented | `CLAS/I` | `CLAS/LI → CLAS` | `CLAS/I → CLAS` |
| `FTG2` short form invented | (no SAP equivalent) | `FTG2` | rename `FEATURE_TOGGLE` |

### P1 — read/write enum drift

- `MSAG` is missing from `SAPREAD_TYPES_*` (write works, read forgot it)
- `MESSAGES` (read) ↔ `MSAG` (write) asymmetry — collapse with deprecated alias

### P2 — architectural smell (deferred to next major)

`API_STATE`, `INACTIVE_OBJECTS`, `VERSIONS`, `VERSION_SOURCE`, `TABLE_CONTENTS` are
mis-modeled as siblings of `CLAS`/`PROG`. They're cross-cutting ADT views over real
objects, not TADIR types. Long-term shape: `SAPRead(type='TABL', view='contents')`.

## Cross-cutting methodology finding

ADT silently ignores unknown `objectType` filters in
`/sap/bc/adt/repository/informationsystem/search` — request status 200 does **not** mean
the alias was honored. This is why six of these bugs hid for so long. Future audits MUST
inspect the returned `<adtcore:type>` attribute, not just status. This is folded into
Plan A's tests.

## Plans

- **Plan A** (`docs/plans/audit-purge-invented-adt-types.md`) — 10 tasks, executes the
  P0 fixes + adds anti-cargo-cult guards (citation-required test, exhaustive
  `objectBasePath`, returned-type SAPSearch assertions, VIEW round-trip integration test)
- **Plan B** (`docs/plans/audit-symmetry-and-ftg2-rename.md`) — 7 tasks, P1 fixes
  (`MSAG` read, `MESSAGES` deprecation, `FEATURE_TOGGLE` rename)
- **Plan C** (`docs/plans/audit-pseudo-type-view-parameter.md`) — sketch, deferred to
  next major

## Test plan

This PR adds no code, so there's nothing to run. After merging, the follow-up PRs for
Plans A + B will:

- [ ] Add unit tests for every changed `SLASH_TYPE_MAP` entry (~6 tests)
- [ ] Add `objectBasePath('VIEW')` unit test
- [ ] Add fixture-replay confirmation for `DDLX/EX` and `TRAN/O`
- [ ] Add VIEW round-trip integration test on a4h (the missing test that hid the bug)
- [ ] Add SAPSearch returned-type assertions
- [ ] Add citation-required guard for `SLASH_TYPE_MAP`
- [ ] Add read/write enum symmetry test

author: xiaoxiaojx
body:
**Summary**

Fix multiple bugs and performance issues in `TsconfigPathsPlugin`:

- **Circular project references → stack overflow**: When project references form a cycle (A references B, B references A) with `references: "auto"`, `_loadTsconfigReferences` recurses infinitely. Fixed by tracking visited reference config paths in a `Set` and skipping already-visited ones.
- **Unscoped npm package extends not resolved**: `extends: "my-base-config"` (unscoped package, no sub-path) failed to resolve to `node_modules/my-base-config/tsconfig.json`. The existing fallback logic only handled scoped packages (`@scope/name`) and sub-path packages (`pkg/tsconfig`). Added an else branch for unscoped packages.
- **`readFile` used for existence check**: `_loadTsconfigFromExtends` called `readFile` just to check if a path exists, discarding the buffer. Changed to `stat` which avoids reading the entire file content unnecessarily.
- **`substituteConfigDir` regex on every call**: The regex replacement ran even when paths contained no `${configDir}`. Added a fast `includes` check to skip the regex when not needed.

**What kind of change does this PR introduce?**

fix, perf

**Did you add tests for your changes?**

Yes. Added 3 new test cases:
- `test/tsconfig-paths.test.js`: "should handle circular references without hanging or crashing"
- `test/tsconfig-paths.test.js`: "should resolve paths from a circular-referenced project"
- `test/tsconfig-paths.test.js`: "should resolve paths inherited from an unscoped npm package tsconfig"

Test fixtures added:
- `test/fixtures/tsconfig-paths/references-circular/` — A↔B circular reference project
- `test/fixtures/tsconfig-paths/extends-unscoped-pkg/` — unscoped npm package extends

**Does this PR introduce a breaking change?**

No.

**If relevant, what needs to be documented once your changes are merged or what have you already documented?**

No documentation changes needed.

**Use of AI**

This PR was authored with the assistance of Claude Code (Claude Opus 4.6). The bugs were identified through code review, test cases were written first to reproduce, then fixes were applied and verified.

## Summary
- 実機 lv350481542 で観測された 2 事象の fix。
- **A. ボタン消失問題**: ボタンを 1 回押すと「取得開始」prompt が hide され、OFF に戻せなくなる → トグル化
- **B. サイドバー閉じない問題**: 「お困りの方はこちら」配信で autoOpen の close が効かず、サイドバーが開いたまま残る → 4 段 close

## A. popup ボタンのトグル化

### Before (v0.1.231 まで)
- 押した → flag set + prompt hide → 元に戻せない
- ユーザー: 「ボタンが消えてしまった」

### After (v0.1.232)
- lid がある限り **常時表示**
- enabled 状態に応じて文言切替:
  - OFF: 「ギフトランキング取得を開始（β）」
  - ON: 「ギフトランキング取得を停止」
- 押下で flag toggle (ON は \`set: true\`、OFF は \`remove\`)

## B. autoOpen close 強化

### 4 段 close + 残存チェック
\`\`\`
1) close ボタン click → 200ms 待ち
2) 残存していれば Escape キー dispatch (Vue モーダル対応) → 200ms
3) 残存していれば giftBtn toggle → 200ms
4) 残存していれば close ボタン再 click（保険）
\`\`\`
各段で \`isSidebarStillVisible()\` を呼び、既に閉じてれば早期 return。

最終待機: 400ms → **600ms** (rescue link 観測時は 1000ms → **1200ms**)

`isSidebarStillVisible()` は \`[class*="rich-view-status"]:not([hidden])\` 等で判定。

body:
## Summary

Implements Option C from #936: a new `BackendSchedulerType.NONE` that skips PodGroup CR creation and runs pods on the K8s default scheduler — removing the kai-scheduler hard dependency for workflows that don't need gang scheduling.

- `BackendSchedulerType` accepts `'none'` in addition to `'kai'`.
- `get_k8s_object_factory()` returns the base `K8sObjectFactory(scheduler_name)` for `NONE`. The base class already does what 'none' needs:
  - no PodGroup CR (just pods)
  - `scheduler_name` written to `pod.spec.schedulerName`
  - no scheduler resource CRDs (queues, topologies)
  - `priority_supported` / `topology_supported` return `False`
- `openapi.json` + UI generated types mirror the new enum value.

15 lines of code change across 5 files. The default behavior (`scheduler_type='kai'`) is unchanged.

## Test plan

OETF scenario test (in the internal harness, not part of this PR) exercises the path end-to-end on KIND:

1. POST `/api/configs/backend/default` with `scheduler_type='none'`, `scheduler_name='default-scheduler'`.
2. Submit `validation/workflow/serial_workflow.yaml`.
3. Expect `COMPLETED`.
4. `addCleanup` restores the original backend config.

TDD verification on `oetf:deploy --env kind --build-local`:

| Run | State | Result |
|-----|-------|--------|
| pass-on-good | full Option C | **PASS** (workflow completes; no PodGroup CR is created) |
| fail-on-bad | enum + factory branch reverted | **FAIL** with `422 Input should be 'kai'` (the exact symptom from #936) |
| pass-on-good (re-verify) | fix restored | **PASS** |

## Summary
The spine's "Coordinating Coworkers" section was a one-liner that pushed agents toward `<message to="parent">` as the default reply shape. That's almost never right — it pages the supervisor for every routine progress update, turning them into a noisy rubber-stamp for work they have no context for.

Replace with an explicit four-pattern guide:

| Case | Shape |
|---|---|
| Replying to the sender of the current turn | `<message>...</message>` (omit `to=`, follow `session_routing`) |
| Dispatching work to a coworker | `<message to="worker-a">...</message>` |
| Invoking a critique / subagent | internal — stays inside the session, no `<message>` |
| Escalating to parent | `<message to="parent">...</message>` — ONLY when stuck |

Plus a one-line rule of thumb at the bottom:
> if what you're about to say is *"I did X, here's the result"* → omit `to=`. *"I can't continue"* → `to="parent"`. *"hey @reviewer"* → `to="reviewer"` directly.

## Relation to #198
PR #198 put the same routing guidance on the critique-overlay's gate-status templates. This PR lifts it to the **spine** so every agent sees it — not just critique-gated ones. Pair.

- `container/spines/base/identity/main-body.md` (+8/-1)

- [ ] Human sanity check on wording.

body:
## Summary
Every dropdown on the contacts page is now multi-select, and four new status filters are exposed (the ones surfaced by the company-detail Statuses tab).

### Multi-select everywhere
- **Lead status** pill row: was single-select with an "All" pill the only way to clear. Now multi-toggle. New pills: Engaged, Unqualified (matches schema enum).
- **Country**, **Email status**, **Source**, **Contact status**: <select> → MultiSelect popover with checkboxes.

### New filters (not previously exposed)
- **Language** (sv / no / da / fi / et / lv / lt / en, with flag prefixes)
- **Lifecycle stage** — joined via `companies.lifecycle_stage`
- **Customer status** — joined via `companies.customer_status`
- **Has app account** — `yes` / `no`, joined via `companies.wl_workshop_id`

The three company-joined filters use a `!inner` join only when active, so contacts without a company aren't silently dropped from unrelated queries.

### Server-side
`ContactFilters` + `resolveContactIdsByFilters` updated to accept either `string[]` (new) or `string` (legacy) on every multi-select field. Bulk-action API routes that consume `currentFilters` need no change — they just pass through. The legacy fallback keeps any in-flight bulk-action requests from old client tabs working through the deploy.

### New UI primitive
`src/components/ui/multi-select.tsx` — popover with checkboxes, search box when ≥6 options, click-outside to close, clear button on the trigger when populated.

## Test plan
- [ ] Build / lint / tsc green (verified locally)
- [ ] Open `/contacts` → multi-toggle lead-status pills, confirm `.in()` query in network tab
- [ ] Pick 3 countries → list narrows to those 3
- [ ] Pick lifecycle = `paying` + customer_status = `active` → only contacts whose company matches both
- [ ] Has app account = "App user" → only contacts whose company has `wl_workshop_id` set
- [ ] Select-all-matching → bulk action affects exactly the visible filtered set (server-side resolver mirrors the UI)
- [ ] Clear all → all filters reset, full list returns

author: udondan
body:
## Summary

Adds two new use case examples to the README:

- **Self-managing Config** — avanti can sync its own config file. A self-update entry keeps `~/.avanti.yml` in sync from a central repo, with a minimal bootstrap pattern for first-time setup on new machines. Enables fleet management: update the central repo once, all clients pick it up on the next pull.

- **Avanti as a Package Manager** — treat source repos as "packages" and the avanti config as a `package.json` equivalent. Each team or project publishes its own files/snippets; projects declare what they consume and from where. The two patterns compose: a central config assembles team snippets and self-manages its own distribution.

## Test plan

- [ ] Read both new sections and verify the examples are accurate and self-contained
- [ ] Verify the self-update entry pattern makes sense (config loads at startup, updated config takes effect next run)

## What's Changed

Fixes #110.

Anypoint MQ API completely ignores the `destinationIds` query parameter when fetching lists. The API always returns the full list of queues/exchanges for the environment, which caused the Terraform provider to return 90+ elements even when users only requested 1 ID via `destination_ids` in the `params` block.

This PR adds a temporary local filtering workaround directly in the provider.

### 🐛 Bug Fixes
- **`anypoint_amq` and `anypoint_ame` data sources** — Added [filterAMQDestinationsByIds](cci:1://file:///Users/souf/Workspaces/cat/Anypoint-Devops-Collective/terraform-provider-anypoint/anypoint/data_source_amq.go:195:0-227:1) to manually filter results locally after the `req.Execute()` API call, before they are mapped and saved into the schema. 
- Results are now correctly limited to exactly the IDs passed to `destination_ids` if that parameter is set.

> **Note:** The local filter function has been annotated with a comment to ensure we remove it once Mulesoft fixes the underlying API endpoint to properly respect the `destinationIds` query parameter.

author: kotama7
body:
## Summary

ARI **v0.7.0** release. Tagged on this branch as `v0.7.0`. Single release commit (`8e6a387`) that bundles five landmark changes plus follow-on cleanup; full per-section detail is in `CHANGELOG.md`.

- **PaperBench-compatible Open Replication System (ORS).** Replaces the v0.6 single-shot reproducibility check. New pipeline `ors_generate_rubric → ear_publish → ors_seed_sandbox → ors_build_reproduce → ors_run_reproduce → ors_grade` driven by [PaperBench](https://github.com/openai/preparedness) vendored at `ari-skill-paper-re/vendor/paperbench` (single-source `sys.path` injection via `_vendor_path.py`). New skill `ari-skill-replicate` provides two-stage rubric generation (skeleton + parallel subtree fan-out, `asyncio.gather`, semaphore=4) — leaves jump from 33–34 (single-call) to 71–149 (two-stage), depth from 3–4 to 5; ~5× output tokens, ~140 s wall-clock at concurrency 4. New `AriPBSolver(BasicAgentSolver)` runs PaperBench's `BasicAgentSolver` / `IterativeAgent` against ARI's HPC sandbox via new `LocalComputer` / `ApptainerComputer` and `LocalPBTask` (bypasses `paperbench.paper_registry`). Per-leaf grading uses the new `LiteLLMTurnCompleter` so judge_model accepts any provider LiteLLM understands (gpt-5-mini default, anthropic/claude-..., gemini/..., ollama/...).
- **EAR lifecycle: curate · publish · promote · clone · registry.** `{checkpoint}/ear/publish.yaml` controls bundle contents (`include` / `exclude` globs, `max_file_mb`, `visibility`, `license`, `backend`); built-in deny list (`.env*`, `secrets/**`, `*.pem`, `*.key`, `id_rsa`, `id_ed25519`) always wins. New CLI: `ari ear curate` / `status` / `publish` / `promote` (always staged; promotion is one-way upward). New CLI: `ari clone <ref>` is a verify-by-digest fetcher (`file://`, `https://`, `ari://`, `gh:`, `doi:`); recomputes per-file sha256 against `manifest.lock`; **never executes** (no `setup.sh`, no `curl|bash`). Optional self-hosted `ari registry serve / token issue / token revoke / token list` (FastAPI + sqlite, content-addressed by `sha256(bundle.tar.gz)[:16]`, Apptainer / docker-compose / pip deploy paths in `scripts/registry/`). License templates emitted from `publish.yaml::license`. `paper-skill:inject_code_availability` injects machine-readable `\codeavailability{}` / `\codedigest{}` / `\coderef{}` LaTeX macros plus a Code Availability section, sourced from `manifest.lock` + `publish_record.json`.
- **`node_report.json` per BFTS node — foundational substrate.** Every BFTS node writes a structured self-report at `experiments/{run_id}/{node_id}/node_report.json` on success/failure (`files_changed`, `original_direction` preserved past evaluator overwrite, `self_assessment`, `next_steps_hints`, literal `build_command` / `run_command`, artifact metadata classified by role). New `ari.orchestrator.node_report` + `ari.orchestrator.node_selection` (`filter_nodes` for `for_synthesis` / `for_code` / `for_narrative`). JSON Schema `ari/schemas/node_report.schema.json`. `node_report.json` lives in `META_FILES` so children never inherit a parent's report. New CLI `ari migrate node-reports <checkpoint>` backfills legacy checkpoints. `generate_ear` rewritten around it — paper-companion repo layout (`README` / `reproduce.sh` / `environment.json` / `code/` / `data/` / `figures/` / `LICENSE`); `code/` collected via `select_source_files_for_publication` (deepest contributor wins per `rel_path`, no size budget). Companion `_run_env.json` per work_dir captures hardware metadata (hostname, SLURM job/partition/nodelist, CPU model/threads/MHz/arch, memory total, compiler versions) **from inside the executing process** so SLURM-job hardware is correct. Reproducibility git shim (`ari/agent/shims/git.sh`) intercepts only `git clone` matching `code_availability_ref`; logs to `<sandbox>/repro_clone_log.jsonl`.
- **LLM lineage decisions + dynamic axes (default on, `stagnation_rule` mode).** A judge LLM sees a `LineageState` (active idea, axis scores, recent composite trajectory, alternatives pool, venue constraints, ancestor thread) and chooses one of `{continue, switch_to_idea, fanout, terminate}`. Fires only when composite scores stay flat for `stagnation_window=5` nodes with delta below `stagnation_threshold=0.05`; `every_node` and `off` are alternatives. Per-run rate limit `rate_limit_per_run=5`, `min_nodes_before_decision=3`. Every fired decision (including `continue`) appended to `{checkpoint}/lineage_decisions.jsonl` for post-hoc analysis. New `ari.orchestrator.lineage_decision`, `ari.orchestrator.root_idea_selector`, `ari.lineage` (walks `meta.json:parent_run_id` to expose every ancestor's `idea.json` to descendants). `ari.evaluator.dynamic_axes` projects each `rubric.score_dimensions` entry into a BFTS axis plus plan-derived axes keyword-scanned from the VirSci plan; `LLMEvaluator` keys its axis cache on a content hash (sha1 of rubric YAML + plan §-tag titles), not mtime.
- **End-to-end ORS hardening (2026-05-08 final integration polish).** Six independent bugs — each one alone enough to abort the chain — were discovered and fixed running the chain on real hardware against a CSR-format SpMM paper; a real 18-minute agent rollout (`gpt-5-mini`, BasicAgent, 7+ git commits including a Numba JIT kernel, sweep experiments, roofline model, performance-model refinement) now scores **9/28 leaves (`ors_score=0.331`)** vs 1/37 (`ors_score=0.042`) on the original cut. (1) `MCPClient.call_tool` gained `_VERY_SLOW_TOOLS` tier (13 h) — the 300 s default killed the rollout mid-flight, then `MAX_RETRIES=3` retry hit the skip path on a partial workspace and returned a misleading `"skipped"` envelope. (2) `_bypass_docker_sanity_check` now also patches the solver module's local names (early-bound via `from X import Y`) — without this the post-rollout `upload_heavy_logs` ran upstream's `mkdir -p /home/submission` and exited 1. (3) `pipeline.py` disabled-stage check distinguishes "intentionally `enabled: false`" from "missing/not yet run" so EAR off no longer cascade-skips `write_paper` → `finalize_paper` → every ORS stage. (4) `dynamic_axes.py` handles dict-shaped `experiment_plan` (the newer `generate_ideas` variant emits `{"Design Steps": [...], ...}`) — without this `ari paper` rerun crashed at `LLMEvaluator.__init__` with `TypeError: expected string or bytes-like object, got 'dict'`. (5) `ari-skill-replicate` rubric post-processing: `_collapse_single_child_chains` folds parent-with-1-child non-leaves into a graded leaf (preserving the parent's claim text via `" — "` concatenation); `_strip_leaf_fields_from_non_leaves` is a defensive second pass for grader violations (`Non-leaf node cannot have a task category`). (6) `_replicator_agent` now uses PaperBench upstream's `get_instructions` + `get_system_message` verbatim (`"Use as much of the available time as possible"`, `"Do not stop until you have replicated all results"`) with `_adapt_vendor_paths` rewriting `/home/{submission,paper,agent.env,logs}` for ari's workspace-flat layout; the previous ari-authored `"5-minute proof-of-concept is fine"` license that encouraged early-submit is removed. `AriPBSolver._get_tools` wraps every non-submit tool with `_BoundedOutputTool` capping `execute()` output at 200 KB byte-wise (UTF-8 safe) — without this a single huge stdout (e.g. printing a NumPy array) tripped OpenAI's 10 MB per-string limit and aborted the rollout.

**Skill count:** 13 default + `ari-skill-orchestrator` (no change vs v0.6.0). New skill `ari-skill-replicate` is invoked from the ORS chain (`ors_generate_rubric` / `audit_rubric`).

**Frontend:** new `LineageDecisionsPage` reads `lineage_decisions.jsonl` per run; "Lineage" column in `ExperimentsPage` shows the latest decision; new `RubricTreeVisualization` renders the PaperBench-format tree with leaf grades; "Report" tab in `DetailPanel` surfaces `node_report.json` structured view; `MemoryEntryCard` extracted as a standalone component; CSS split into `tokens.css` / `layout.css` / `components.css` / `widget

body:
## Summary
Closes the cross-tenant read/write path through `/query` (Cypher-ish). Pre-fix, `ExecutionContext` carried `context.Context` for cancellation but the executor never read tenant from it; every graph read used tenant-blind methods. A JWT-authenticated tenant-A caller could `MATCH`, `CREATE`, `UPDATE`, or `DELETE` across all tenants' data via `/query`.

## Architecture (per spike doc §3 Q1)
**Decision: thread `tenantID` through `ExecutionContext`. Don't wrap the graph.**
- Added `tenantID string` field, snapshot once from `ec.context` at construction via `tenant.MustFromContext`
- New helper `newExecutionContext(ctx, graph)` used at all 4 entry points (`executor.go`, `executor_plan.go`, `executor_explain.go`). A 5th construction in `executor_steps.go` (MergeStep sub-context) inherits `tenantID` from parent
- Step authors call `ctx.graph.XForTenant(args, ctx.tenantID)` — no per-call ctx parsing in the hot path

## Migrated (14 sites)
| File | Sites | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `executor_steps.go` | 6 | IndexLookup, CreateNode/Edge, UpdateNode, RemoveNodeProperties, DeleteNode |
| `match_node.go` | 1 | Replaced "iterate 1..NodeCount via GetNode" cross-tenant scan with `GetAllNodesForTenant` (same shape as the A6c-graphql-resolvers cleanup) |
| `match_path.go` | 5 | `GetNode×2`, `GetOutgoingEdges×2`, `GetIncomingEdges×2` in BFS traversal |
| `aggregation_grouping.go` | 1 | Sub-context inherits parent's `tenantID` |

## Storage addition (bounded scope)
**`RemoveNodePropertiesForTenant`** — pre-fix `RemoveNodeProperties` was tenant-blind with no scoped variant. Required by the executor's `REMOVE` clause migration. Mirrors `UpdateNodeForTenant`'s lock-then-delegate pattern. Adding it here (rather than punting) was the right call: alternative left a real gap and the addition is bounded to one method.

## Tests
`pkg/api/handlers_query_a6c_test.go` — 4 HTTP-level sub-tests:

**`TestA6c_Query_MatchIsolation`**
- tenant-A `MATCH (p:Person)` → only A's nodes
- tenant-B `MATCH (p:Person)` → only B's nodes
- tenant-C (no data) → empty

**`TestA6c_Query_CreateLandsInCallerTenant`**
- `CREATE (p:User {...})` through `/query` stamps the node with the caller's tenant, not `default`. Ownership-stamping check, mirror of A6a's `TestA6a_CreateNode_LandsInCallerTenant`.

End-to-end gate for the executor migration. Existing query tests still pass (default-tenant single-tenant path preserved by `MustFromContext` semantics).

## Stacked queue
`main → #17 → #18 → #19 → #20 → #22 → #23 → #24 → THIS`. 9 deep.

PR #21 (A6c spike) is independent.

## After this lands
Per spike doc §6, **A6c-algorithms** — migrate `pkg/algorithms/*` traversal algorithms (`khop`, `cycle_detection`, `pagerank`, `scc`, etc.) to `*ForTenant` variants. Then **A6c-algorithms-handlers** wires them into the `/algorithms/*` endpoints. After that A6c is closed.

author: benbaichmankass
body:
## Summary

Self-driving the PM-side diag relay so future debugging sessions don't need operator clicks.

**Problem:** the v1 workflow (PR #486) only had `workflow_dispatch`. Sandbox sessions have no MCP tool to dispatch a workflow, no MCP tool to read run artifacts, and no MCP tool to stream logs — so every diag fetch required the operator to click `Run workflow` and either eyeball the run-log preview or download the artifact.

**Fix:** add `issues.opened` (filtered to label `vm-diag-request`) as a second trigger for the same workflow. End-to-end loop a session can drive on its own:

1. `mcp__github__issue_write` opens an issue titled `[diag-request] <path>` with the label.
2. Workflow fires, parses the path from the title, runs the existing SSH-tunnelled `curl` against `/api/diag/<path>` on the VM.
3. `actions/github-script@v7` posts the JSON back as an issue comment from `github-actions[bot]` and closes the issue with `state_reason=completed`.
4. Session reads the comment via `mcp__github__issue_read` (or whatever the equivalent MCP tool is in a future session).

`workflow_dispatch` is preserved for the operator-driven case — that path keeps the artifact upload (the issue path skips it to avoid duplicating data into both the comment and an artifact).

Failure path: structured error comment back to the same issue, closes with `state_reason=not_planned`. Common-cause table in the new doc.

## Files

- `.github/workflows/vm-diag-snapshot.yml` — new `issues` trigger, label-filter `if`, `Resolve and validate diag path` step that handles both event shapes, success/failure issue-reply steps. `permissions.issues: write` added (was `contents: read` only).
- `docs/claude/diag-relay.md` — **new.** Canonical reference: TL;DR for both flows, why the shape (no `run_workflow` MCP), trust boundary (still S-051 / `vm-operator-mode.md` § 9), prerequisites, failure modes, when not to use.
- `docs/claude/INDEX.md` — links to the new doc.
- `CLAUDE.md` — short "Reaching `/api/diag/*` from a PM-side session" subsection under Diagnostic API, points at `diag-relay.md` for the full flow.
- `docs/claude/vm-operator-mode.md` § 9.a — new subsection describing the relay; the existing § 9 trust contract is unchanged.
- `scripts/bootstrap_diag_relay.sh` — **new.** Idempotent operator-side helper that creates the `vm-diag-request` repo label (color `0e8a16`, "open / read-only" green) and verifies both required secrets are present. Session can't create labels (no `mcp__github__create_label` MCP), so the operator runs this once on their laptop / Colab.

## Trust contract (unchanged)

Read-only Tier 1 — same class as S-051. The relay can only ship a fixed-form
`curl -sS --fail -H 'Authorization: Bearer …' http://127.0.0.1:8001/api/diag/<path>`
over SSH. The path is regex-validated against `^[A-Za-z0-9/?&=_.-]+$` before any interpolation, so an issue title can't smuggle shell. Mutating routes don't exist on `/api/diag/*` and the workflow can't reach them by construction.

`secrets.VM_SSH_KEY` and `secrets.DIAG_READ_TOKEN` are auto-masked by GitHub Actions.

## Test plan

- [x] `python3 -c "import yaml; yaml.safe_load(open(...))"` on the workflow
- [ ] Operator: run `bash scripts/bootstrap_diag_relay.sh` (or create the `vm-diag-request` label manually) — secrets are already in place from PR #486
- [ ] Session opens a `[diag-request] snapshot?limit=20` issue with the label
- [ ] Workflow comments JSON back within 60 s and closes the issue with `completed`
- [ ] Re-run with a malformed path (e.g. `[diag-request] foo;rm -rf`) — workflow rejects in the validate step before any SSH, posts failure comment

## Future improvement

If the operator adds the official `github/github-mcp-server` (with the `actions` toolset) as a project MCP server, this relay can collapse back to a single `run_workflow` MCP call from the session. Until then, the issue-driven loop is the contract. Doc note included in `diag-relay.md` § "Why this shape".

body:
## バグ報告

天井近くまで埋まった daily 盤面 (38/50 ターン等) で:
- AI Best ボタンを押しても何も起こらない
- 手動で active pair を ama 推奨位置まで動かして Drop してもコミットされない

ユーザの推測「14段目に一切置けなくなってそう」は半分正解で、 14段目自体は本家準拠で sutepuyo (lock 不可) のままだが、 **「片方が 14段目で discard される手」 全体が commit できない状態** になっていた。

## 原因

PR #64 で追加された \`isMoveProductive\` が `added === 2` (= 2 ぷよ全部着地必須) と過剰に厳しく、 本家ぷよぷよ通の有効テクニックである **捨てぷよ** (片方を意図的に 14段目で discard) を全部塞いでいた。

ama (native / wasm) は捨てぷよ手も legal として suggest するため、 提案された手を commit ゲートで弾く divergence が発生。

PR #64 author 自身のコメント:

> productivity が必要なのは、 floor kick で row 0 col=sealed まで 軸を持って 行ける場合があり、 そこで commit すると lockActive が **両方を** 黙って discard する (= turn だけ消費する no-op) ため。

意図は **「両方 discard」 を弾くこと** だったが、 実装の \`=== 2\` が片方 discard も巻き込んでいた。 コメントの意図に合わせて修正。

## 修正内容

\`isMoveProductive\`: \`added === 2\` → \`added >= 1\`

| 状況 | 旧挙動 | 新挙動 |
|------|--------|--------|
| 両方着地 (added=2) | productive=true | productive=true |
| 片方着地 + sutepuyo (added=1) | **productive=false ❌** | **productive=true ✓** |
| 両方 discard (added=0) | productive=false | productive=false |

## 影響範囲

- **\`commit()\` (store.ts)** — AI Best / Drop ボタン両方の gate に効く。 天井詰まり盤面で commit が通るように。
- **\`enumerateLegalMoves\` (moves.ts)** — 候補手列挙に sutepuyo を含めるように。 ama suggest の subset チェック (\`reachability-vs-ama.test.ts\`) は引き続きパス。
- **\`useGestures\` の preview gate** — gesture 中の ghost プレビューに sutepuyo 位置も表示されるように。

## Test plan

- [x] \`npx tsc --noEmit\` 通る
- [x] \`npm run test -- --run\` 222 passed (pre-existing wasm-ama 1 failure は無関係)
- [x] \`sealed-column.test.ts\` 期待値を新セマンティクスに更新:
  - 「封印列に axis 横置きは productive=true (捨てぷよ)」 — 旧 false → 新 true
  - 「封印列縦置きは productive=false」 — 変わらず
  - 「全列封印で全配置 no-op」 — 変わらず (両方 discard なので 0 added)
- [ ] 端末で実機検証: 画像の 38/50 盤面相当で AI Best が動く / 手動 Drop で sutepuyo 配置できる

body:
This pull request updates the Sia-Compost-Sync Dashboard to support per-device MQTT data topics, improving clarity and scalability for device data management. The changes affect both the web dashboard (`index.html`) and the device firmware (`src/main.cpp`), ensuring data is published and subscribed to topics that include the device ID. Additionally, error handling and user feedback have been improved in the Python logger and firmware.

**MQTT Topic Handling and Device ID Integration:**

* The dashboard and firmware now use per-device MQTT data topics (`sia/compost/data/<device-id>`) instead of a shared topic, both for subscribing and publishing data. This allows for better separation of device data. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-0eb547304658805aad788d320f10bf1f292797b5e6d745a3bf617584da017051L37-R37) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-0eb547304658805aad788d320f10bf1f292797b5e6d745a3bf617584da017051L64-R64) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-0eb547304658805aad788d320f10bf1f292797b5e6d745a3bf617584da017051R107-R111) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-0eb547304658805aad788d320f10bf1f292797b5e6d745a3bf617584da017051R131) [[5]](diffhunk://#diff-0eb547304658805aad788d320f10bf1f292797b5e6d745a3bf617584da017051R142-R159) [[6]](diffhunk://#diff-0eb547304658805aad788d320f10bf1f292797b5e6d745a3bf617584da017051L157-R181) [[7]](diffhunk://#diff-34d21af3c614ea3cee120df276c9c4ae95053830d7f1d3deaf009a4625409ad2L29-R29) [[8]](diffhunk://#diff-34d21af3c614ea3cee120df276c9c4ae95053830d7f1d3deaf009a4625409ad2R66) [[9]](diffhunk://#diff-34d21af3c614ea3cee120df276c9c4ae95053830d7f1d3deaf009a4625409ad2L165-R181) [[10]](diffhunk://#diff-34d21af3c614ea3cee120df276c9c4ae95053830d7f1d3deaf009a4625409ad2L242-R246)

* The dashboard UI and logic have been updated to display and subscribe to the correct per-device data topic based on user input, and to resubscribe when the device ID changes. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-0eb547304658805aad788d320f10bf1f292797b5e6d745a3bf617584da017051L37-R37) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-0eb547304658805aad788d320f10bf1f292797b5e6d745a3bf617584da017051L64-R64) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-0eb547304658805aad788d320f10bf1f292797b5e6d745a3bf617584da017051R74) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-0eb547304658805aad788d320f10bf1f292797b5e6d745a3bf617584da017051R107-R111) [[5]](diffhunk://#diff-0eb547304658805aad788d320f10bf1f292797b5e6d745a3bf617584da017051R131) [[6]](diffhunk://#diff-0eb547304658805aad788d320f10bf1f292797b5e6d745a3bf617584da017051R142-R159) [[7]](diffhunk://#diff-0eb547304658805aad788d320f10bf1f292797b5e6d745a3bf617584da017051L157-R181)

**Dependency Management and Security:**

* The dashboard now pins specific versions of `mqtt.js` and `chart.js` and uses the `crossorigin="anonymous"` attribute for improved security and reliability.

**Firmware Logging and Warnings:**

* Improved firmware log messages to clarify security implications when TLS certificate validation or command token protection is disabled.

**Python Logger Error Handling:**

* The Python data logger (`data_logger.py`) now distinguishes between serial port errors and file I/O errors for more precise error reporting.

## Summary
- add a single local `./deploy` entrypoint for safe VPS rollouts
- support both `./deploy main` and `./deploy current-branch` with server-side safety checks and verification
- document the new workflow and remove the obsolete deployment wrapper scripts

## Why
The repo previously had narrow helper scripts that hard-switched branches and always force-recreated containers. This change consolidates rollout behavior into one documented path that matches the verified production topology and supports optional branch deploys safely.

## What changed
- added `scripts/deploy.ts` and the root `./deploy` wrapper
- added local prechecks, remote git safety checks, compose rebuilds, and public/container health verification
- added package scripts for the deploy commands and synced the Docker workspace snapshot
- updated deployment docs for the `152.53.80.229` workflow and deleted the old helper wrappers

## Validation
- `./deploy --help`
- `bun run check:docker-workspace`
- `bun test`

## Notes
- branch deploys intentionally leave the server checkout on the deployed branch until `./deploy main` is run
- the server-side precheck allows the known untracked `deployment/docker/signal-cli-0.14.3-Linux-native.tar.gz` file and blocks on other unexpected changes
