author: copilot
body:
This PR introduces a new standalone `layout.py` project for a local-only quiz workflow (no internet), with a GTK4/Libadwaita teacher interface and a browser-based student client. The implementation follows a gnome-classshare-compatible shape (`LayoutState`, `LayoutHandler`, `LayoutWindow`, `LayoutApp`) and keeps quiz/ranking data strictly in RAM.

- **Core architecture & compatibility**
  - Added `layout.py` with the required class structure and shared-server style:
    - HTTP server on port `0` (ephemeral)
    - WebSocket server on a separate port (threaded)
  - Added `get_local_ip()` and settings/desktop integration paths:
    - `~/.config/layout/settings.json`
    - `~/.local/share/applications/layout.desktop`

- **Teacher UI (GTK4 + Libadwaita)**
  - Implemented tabs for:
    - custom task launch (question/answer/timer, reveal)
    - random math generator (`+`, `-`, `×`, `÷`, mixed; configurable range/timer)
    - raised-hand queue (ack/reset)
    - more-time requests (extend timer for requesters)
    - ranking view + reset
  - Added live aggregate status and progress updates.

- **Student web client (HTML/CSS/JS, no framework)**
  - Name capture with `localStorage` persistence.
  - Active-task UI with timer, numeric answer input (`inputmode="numeric"`), Enter-to-submit, raise-hand, more-time, and progress (`answered/total`).
  - Feedback/status flows:
    - answer feedback (right/wrong when enabled)
    - raise-hand acknowledgement from teacher
    - reveal/times-up messaging

- **Waiting screen: times-table mode + ranking**
  - When no teacher task is active, students are moved to continuous times-table training.
  - Server-side scoring and live ranking broadcast.
  - Ranking filters to students with at least 10 solved times-table tasks.
  - No persistence of scores or quiz state across restarts.

- **Protocol + fallback transport**
  - Implemented JSON message handling aligned with the requested protocol shape (`task`, `random_task`, `waiting`, `timer_update`, `progress`, `raise_hand_ack`, `reveal`, `ranking`, `times_up`, etc.).
  - Added transport fallback when `websockets` is unavailable:
    - HTTP polling via `GET /state` every 2 seconds
    - REST endpoints for submit/raise-hand/more-time/times-table answer.

- **Documentation**
  - Updated `README.md` with startup instructions, dependency notes, architecture overview, and runtime behavior.

Example (state shape + launch style):

```python
state = LayoutState()

# optional threaded WS server (if websockets is installed)
ws_server = LayoutWebSocketServer(state)
ws_server.start()

# HTTP server on port 0 (ephemeral), same style as classshare
http_server = start_http_server(state, ws_port=ws_server.port if ws_server.port else None)
print(http_server.server_address)  # ('0.0.0.0', <random_port>)
```

author: jaylfc
body:
Three layers fixed together because they're the same bug surfacing at different points, plus a follow-up to the migration script that exposed itself when run live on the Pi.

## 1. Manifest layer
\`mlc-llm\` declared top-level \`type: llm-runtime\` which \`auto_register_from_manifest\` read as the backend type. Now follows the pattern every other catalog service uses:

| Field | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| top-level \`type\` | \`llm-runtime\` | \`service\` |
| \`category\` | \`llm-runtime\` | \`llm-runtime\` (kept — UX grouping) |
| \`lifecycle.backend_type\` | _missing_ | \`openai-compatible\` |
| \`lifecycle.default_url\` | _missing_ | \`http://localhost:8000\` |

## 2. Registration layer
\`auto_register_from_manifest\` used to write ANY string into \`config.backends\`. One bad manifest meant every health-check loop hit \`ValueError\`. Now validates against \`VALID_BACKEND_TYPES\` at registration time, logs a loud warning with the offending name + type + the allowed set, and skips the entry. Loud failure beats limp-along.

## 3. Read layer
Even if a bad backend somehow ended up in config (old data file from before #2 lands, manual edit), \`check_backend_health\` used to raise \`ValueError\` up through the FastAPI handler and 500 the whole \`/api/backends\` response. Now returns a structured envelope:

\`\`\`json
{ "healthy": false, "status": "unsupported", "error": "...", "models": [] }
\`\`\`

…so the dashboard renders the bad entry as offline-with-reason instead of taking down the entire endpoint. Same envelope for adapter exceptions during \`health()\` calls.

## 4. Migration script (follow-up from live Pi run)
The script in #430 picked the install dir from \`$SUDO_USER\`'s \`$HOME\`, but the real production install on the Pi is under \`/root/rk-llama.cpp/\` (the systemd unit runs as \`User=jay\` even though the binary lives in /root). Result: it scanned \`/home/jay/rk-llama.cpp/models/\` (a build dir holding only \`ggml-vocab-*\` test fixtures), migrated those, and re-pointed an \`active.gguf\` to a path that didn't exist — service refused to start.

Now the script:
- Reads the \`ExecStart\` line of \`/etc/systemd/system/rkllamacpp.service\` to find the **actual** install dir (\`/root/rk-llama.cpp\` or \`~/rk-llama.cpp\`)
- Uses the install dir's filesystem owner for chown, not \`SUDO_USER\`
- Skips \`ggml-vocab-*\` filenames (rk-llama.cpp's bundled test fixtures, not user-installed models)

## Net effect
- ✅ Master CI goes green again — \`test_routes_dashboard.py::test_backends_api\` had been failing for the past 4+ PRs (#427-#430) on this exact \`llm-runtime\` warning the live controller logged every 30s
- ✅ \`/api/backends\` never 500s because of one bad backend
- ✅ Future malformed manifests fail loudly at startup instead of silently poisoning every health-check round
- ✅ Migration script robust to dual rk-llama.cpp install dirs (production at /root, source build at ~/, etc.)

## Test plan
- [x] 3 new tests in \`test_backend_adapters.py\` — unknown type returns unsupported envelope, raising adapter returns error envelope, missing name doesn't crash
- [x] 2 new tests in \`test_config_auto_register.py\` — catalog-format manifest with unknown backend_type is skipped + warning logged; flat-format ditto
- [x] Live: ran updated migration logic by hand on the Pi — moved \`/root/rk-llama.cpp/models/{e2b,e4b}.gguf\` → \`/root/models/rk-llama.cpp/gemma/...\`, re-pointed active.gguf, restarted rkllamacpp, /v1/models reports model loaded
- [ ] Master CI green after merge

---
_Surfaced while debugging \`test (3.13)\` failure on PR #430. Jay said "fix it properly no workarounds" — the manifest fix alone would patch the symptom; the registration + read layers are the actual fragility. Migration-script bug surfaced in live testing._

body:
# Pull Request

## Description

This pull request introduces several enhancements and improvements across the vessel analysis backend and the analysis report UI. The main changes include richer vessel and activity data models, improved activity descriptions with geospatial context, and interactive UI elements for navigating to activity locations on the map.

**Backend Enhancements:**

*Vessel and Activity Data Modeling:*
- Added new properties to the `Vessel`, `VesselPosition`, and `VesselActivity` models to more comprehensively represent vessel state and activity, including navigation status, speed, heading, draught, destination, ETA, and flag. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-8ce4a332faf13e48b88ab8141c5f1a9bb84675715eb2fa6ec6412b2ef66f7f3fR15-R26) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-6a6649d31d0822b7754c22e36cdf2ef0fe0767dadf0348ff3f3825949b98611dR5-R18) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-df05cfc3abaf83ce4dba6eb511d65f3748e68c79e92ce0fb0b59a239a261157dR5-R18)

*Activity Data and Description Improvements:*
- Activity descriptions now include geospatial coordinates (latitude/longitude) for AIS gaps, loitering, speed anomalies, and ports of interest, improving clarity and enabling UI navigation to these locations. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-7f4d7229d0e389cd0e3e337ce35463da525c130bfb79fb4aaa25e4f6afbbc5bdR145-R146) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-7f4d7229d0e389cd0e3e337ce35463da525c130bfb79fb4aaa25e4f6afbbc5bdR190) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-7f4d7229d0e389cd0e3e337ce35463da525c130bfb79fb4aaa25e4f6afbbc5bdL310-R323)
- The `source` of a port of interest activity is now dynamically determined from the ports of interest dataset, falling back to the activity details or 'FleetLeaks' as default.
- Removed the hardcoded `'FleetLeaks'` source from the infractions list API response, as source attribution is now handled per-activity.

*Operational Improvements:*
- The entrypoint script now includes a step to rebuild vessel analysis on startup, ensuring up-to-date analysis data.

**Frontend/UI Improvements:**

*Analysis Report Modal Interactivity:*
- The analysis report modal now accepts an `onNavigate` prop, enabling clickable coordinates in activity descriptions. When clicked, the map centers on the relevant location and the modal closes. Implemented Vercel Web Analytics for the RoastMe project.

## What was implemented

Successfully configured Vercel Web Analytics for this HTML5 static website project.

## Changes made

Modified:
- `index.html` - Added Vercel Web Analytics tracking scripts to the <head> section

## Implementation details

This is a static HTML5 project, so I used the HTML5-specific implementation from the official Vercel documentation:

1. Added the analytics initialization script that creates the `window.va` function and queue
2. Added the deferred script tag that loads `/_vercel/insights/script.js`

The scripts were placed in the `<head>` section after the Google Fonts link and before the `<style>` tag, following best practices for third-party analytics scripts.

## Code added

```html
<script>
  window.va = window.va || function () { (window.vaq = window.vaq || []).push(arguments); };
</script>
<script defer src="/_vercel/insights/script.js"></script>
```

## Why this approach

- This project is a static HTML5 website without a frontend framework (Next.js, React, Vue, etc.)
- The Vercel documentation provides specific instructions for HTML5 projects that use the `/_vercel/insights/script.js` endpoint
- The `defer` attribute ensures the analytics script loads asynchronously without blocking page rendering
- The initialization script creates a queue for analytics events that might fire before the main script loads

## Next steps

To complete the setup:
1. Deploy the changes to Vercel
2. Enable Web Analytics in the Vercel dashboard (Analytics section in sidebar)
3. Verify tracking is working by checking the browser Network tab for requests to `/_vercel/insights/`
4. View analytics data in the Vercel dashboard once users visit the site

## Notes

- No npm dependencies were needed since this is a static HTML project
- No build process required - the changes are ready to deploy
- The analytics script is served directly by Vercel's infrastructure when deployed

author: theodore-evans
body:
## Summary

Fixes two regressions surfaced after the state-machine collapse, plus a small UX cleanup.

### Time picker prevents past / within-1h slots
Form-level prevention in PublishSheet: today's day cell only offers times ≥1 hour in the future, days with no remaining valid times are disabled, and \`nextDefaultTime\` falls through the ladder to the first valid option. Service-level defense: \`publish()\` validates each slot via \`validateSlotFields\` before \`canPublish\` so direct API callers get the specific \"Start time must be at least 1 hour in the future\" error instead of the generic message.

### Author offered-times view restored + enriched
- Author path through \`getPromptDetail\` now uses \`get_my_prompt_slots\` SECURITY DEFINER RPC so authors see \`exact_location\` on their own slots (venue name + address + map link).
- Includes accepted slots — the section is the full inventory of times the author put up, with booked ones rendered dimmed with a \"booked\" label.
- \`hydrateFromInitial\` in PublishSheet drops past slots so pre-fill matches the time picker's filter (no select-vs-state drift).

### Removed duplicate meetings section
\"Your scheduled meetings\" on the author's read view was duplicating the meeting card that's already attached to the responder's response card. Dropped the section; the response-attached card has the right context (partner, cancellation reason if any).

### Seed
The legacy \"archived\" seed row becomes an \"Unpublished\" example (state='draft' + published_at IS NOT NULL) with one past + one future slot for testing the pre-fill filter.

## Test plan

- [ ] Open the publish sheet at 11 PM. Today's day cell is dimmed (no valid times left). Tomorrow onwards work normally.
- [ ] On Lisa's \`seed-prompt-unpublished\`, open the publish sheet. Only the future slot pre-fills; the past one is dropped.
- [ ] On Nina's \`seed-prompt-scheduled\`, view the author read view. \"Times you offered\" shows both slots — the booked one dimmed with a \"booked\" label, plus the open one. Each card shows the venue name + address.
- [ ] Same view: no separate \"Your scheduled meetings\" section. The meeting card lives on the responder's response card below.
- [ ] As Marco, open \`seed-prompt-completed\` (has a past completed meeting). Click Unpublish. State flips to draft, no error.

## Post-Deploy Monitoring

- Watch for any 500 errors from \`/api/prompts/[id]/publish\` mentioning the new \`validateSlotFields\` path.
- Verify \`get_my_prompt_slots\` is being called from the read view loader (network tab).
- No author-side surface should now ever show a past time the form lets through.

- **Patch** (`0.0.x`) — bug fixes, doc corrections, ADR amendments

git checkout main

author: svozza
body:
First step of #7. Opts in only `lambda/notify` and `lambda/ws-authorizer`; the other 29 lambdas keep their per-directory `package.json`, `package-lock.json`, and terraform block untouched. npm workspaces is opt-in per directory, so this is incremental — as we add tests to more lambdas (e.g. #65/#66/#67) they can join the workspace one PR at a time.

## Summary

- **Root `package.json`** declares `"workspaces": ["lambda/notify", "lambda/ws-authorizer"]` and hoists shared devDeps: `vitest`, `esbuild`, `aws-sdk-client-mock*`, plus the `@aws-sdk/*` clients used only by tests.
- **Per-lambda `package.json`** drops devDeps and adds an esbuild build script that writes a single `.mjs` bundle with `@aws-sdk/*` externalised (already in the Node 24 Lambda runtime).
- **Terraform packaging** for both lambdas switches from `npm ci --omit=dev` + zip-whole-dir to `npm run build -w <name>` + `:zip <lambda>/.build`. Root `npm ci` is now a pre-step in `scripts/deploy-terraform.sh` so the two lambda modules don't race on parallel installs.
- **notify migrated from CJS to ESM** (continuing #41 alongside ws-authorizer which landed in #63). Test suite updated to use dynamic `import()` in place of `createRequire` + `require.cache` — `vi.mock` hoisting doesn't intercept CJS requires cleanly, so going ESM removes the friction.
- **`.gitignore`** adds `lambda/*/.build/`; **`dependabot.yml`** adds a `/` entry for the root lockfile while keeping the `/lambda/*` entry for the 29 untouched lambdas.

## Result

| Lambda | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| notify | ~10+ MB zip | **730 bytes** |
| ws-authorizer | ~500 KB zip | **9.2 KB** |

Bundles inline declared prod deps (aws-jwt-verify for ws-authorizer, none for notify) and externalise `@aws-sdk/*` to the runtime.

## Test plan

- [x] `npm install` at root → succeeds, produces root `package-lock.json`.
- [x] `npm test` at root → notify 7/7, ws-authorizer 9/9.
- [x] `npm run build -w notify` + `npm run build -w ws-authorizer` → produce `.build/<entry>.mjs`, both expose a `handler` export via dynamic `import()`.
- [x] Deploy to `eu-west-1` dev → terraform plan scoped to the two Lambda functions, apply succeeds.
- [x] `aws lambda invoke` on notify with a smoke payload → `{"statusCode":200}`.
- [x] Lambda configuration shows the new zip sizes as reported above.

author: badlazzor
body:
## Summary

Three small changes folded into one PR — vendor noise aside they're all small enough to review together. Replaces #126 (CLI bump), #127 (wrap helper, this PR), and #128 (e2e SDK fix).

## Changes

1. **Bump `github.com/bitrise-io/bitrise-build-cache-cli/v2` from v2.5.0 to v2.6.0** (vendored) — required because the wrap helper only exists from v2.6.0 onwards.
2. **Wrap gradle with `bitrise-build-cache react-native run` when RN cache is active.** In `runGradleTask`: between `cmdSlice` assembly and `command.New(...)`, call `wrap.Detect(context.Background(), wrap.DetectParams{})` and `wrap.Wrap(det, gradleTool, gradleArgs)`. The wrapped (name, args) feeds into `command.New(name, wrappedArgs...)` so existing stdout/stderr / `commandhelper.RunAndExportOutput` branches pick up the wrap transparently. Logs `Bitrise Build Cache: React Native cache active — wrapping gradle with %s` only when wrapping kicks in. Part of the rollout already applied to `bitrise-step-android-build` PR #59 / `bitrise-step-android-unit-test` PR #45 / `bitrise-step-android-lint` PR #34 / `steps-gradle-unit-test` PR #28.
3. **Fix e2e: install missing Android SDK platforms before gradle.** The shared `_common` workflow runs gradle directly against `sample-apps-android-sdk22` (which pins `compileSdkVersion 27`) without first ensuring the SDK platform is available, so every gradle e2e fails with `Failed to install the following SDK components: platforms;android-27`. Added `install-missing-android-tools@3` between the fixture clone and the self-test step. Standard pattern used by other Android steps; makes the e2e stack-image-independent.

Linked epic: [ACI-4307](https://bitrise.atlassian.net/browse/ACI-4307) (React Native Build Cache Support).

## Test plan

- [ ] CI green on this PR (the SDK install fix should unblock the gradle e2e workflows that were failing on `chore/bump-cli-v2.6.0`).
- [ ] After merge, confirm subsequent gradle-runner releases pick up CLI v2.6.0 vendor changes.
- [ ] On a workflow that runs `activate-build-cache-for-react-native` followed by `gradle-runner`, confirm the `wrapping gradle with` info log appears and analytics show the gradle child attached to the RN parent.

[ACI-4307]: https://bitrise.atlassian.net/browse/ACI-4307?atlOrigin=eyJpIjoiNWRkNTljNzYxNjVmNDY3MDlhMDU5Y2ZhYzA5YTRkZjUiLCJwIjoiZ2l0aHViLWNvbS1KU1cifQ

body:
## Summary

Phase O-2 of the PDP onboarding standardization track. Adds the 4 typed taxonomy columns peng agreed to in the playbook (Decision 1: Hybrid taxonomy):

| Column | Type | Source |
|---|---|---|
| \`price_tier\` | VARCHAR(16) | Deterministic from \`product.price\` |
| \`use_case_tags\` | JSONB | Conservative regex / keyword extraction from title+desc+tags |
| \`lifestyle_tags\` | JSONB | Same |
| \`demographic\` | VARCHAR(16) | Same |

Single shared helper at \`services/pdp_taxonomy.py\` (pure functions, no DB I/O, no LLM). All 3 onboarding paths call into it so the derivation is identical across:
- Path A: \`ingest_standard_products\` (Shopify/Wix/Woo/BigCommerce)
- Path B: \`mirror_external_seeds_to_catalog_products.py\` (external seed mirror)
- Path C: \`run_catalog_enrichment.py\` (catalog enrichment agent JSONL)

## Conservative-by-design extractors

- \`extract_lifestyle_tags\`: literal substring match against curated rules (vegan, cruelty-free, fragrance-free, paraben-free, hypoallergenic, organic, etc.) → canonical Pivota tokens.
- \`extract_use_case_tags\`: whole-word regex so \"professional\" doesn't match \"non-professional\", \"sport\" doesn't match \"transport\".
- \`extract_demographic\`: single value, \`kids\` takes precedence over \`men\`/\`women\`/\`unisex\` when ambiguous. Returns \`None\` when no clear signal — Phase O-3 LabelAgent fills the long tail.
- \`derive_price_tier\`: 0/NaN/negative all distinguished. Zero is \`unknown\` (free / login-walled), not \`under_50\`.

## Schema guard

- mig 076 + ensure_required_schema_light ALTER both add the 4 columns. Deploy-safe even if migration didn't run separately (same fail-safe pattern as mig 075 for \`tags\`).

## Tests

76 pass across 6 suites:
- \`tests/test_pdp_taxonomy.py\` (NEW) — 22 tests for the helper module, including the substring-precedence cases that ruled out earlier false-positive patterns.
- \`tests/test_catalog_sync_service_integration.py\` — new test asserts Path A writes all 4 columns.
- \`tests/test_catalog_enrichment_ingestion.py\` — new test asserts Path C writes the JSONB-stringified shape.
- \`tests/test_schema_guard_psp_columns.py\` — extends existing assertion to cover all 4 new column names.

## What this DOES NOT do

- Doesn't fill columns for already-existing rows in \`catalog_products\` (Phase O-6 backfill territory; canonical-only per Decision 5).
- Doesn't add LLM classification — Phase O-3 LabelAgent uses Gemini for rows the deterministic extractors leave NULL/empty.
- Doesn't change recall code — Phase O-5 wires lifecycle filtering once there's something to filter on.
- Doesn't pre-bake price tiers per vertical — uses the playbook-recommended 5 universal buckets.

## Next

Phase O-3 — LabelAgent v1. Fills the long tail (NULL demographic, empty use_case_tags / lifestyle_tags) via Gemini classification on rows where the deterministic extractors didn't fire.

author: cradcliff187
body:
## Summary

Two related improvements to the admin Role Management experience.

### 1. Edit Profile → Edit User slide-out

`EditProfileModal` was using a centered `Dialog`. The canonical pattern in this app is the right-anchored `Sheet` slide-out — used by `CreateUserModal` for new-user flows and by `PayeeForm` (wrapped in `PayeesList`) for payee edit. Now `EditProfileModal` matches: same `w-full sm:max-w-[600px] flex flex-col p-0` shell with sticky header, scrollable body, and sticky footer.

- Renamed title `Edit Profile` → `Edit User` so the action matches the surface.
- Field heights bumped from `h-8` to default to match create/payee forms (consistent touch targets, easier on phones).
- No prop changes — drop-in replacement at all call sites.

### 2. The "Enable" button bug

The "Enable" button shown next to a `field_worker` user without a payee row was hard-coded to create an `is_internal=true, payee_type='internal_labor'` payee. That's correct for W2 employees but **wrong for subcontractors who clock time** — they need `is_internal=false, payee_type='subcontractor', provides_labor=true`, with `amount=0` enforced by the [`enforce_time_entry_category_from_payee`](https://supabase.com/dashboard/project/clsjdxwbsjbhjibvlqbz) DB trigger.

Symptom path: admin creates a user via `CreateUserModal` and picks `Subcontractor with hourly time tracking`. If the auto-payee step fails (network blip, race), `CreateUserModal` toasts `"User created, but expense & time setup did not save. Enable it from Role Management."` Admin goes to Role Management, clicks Enable. Today: silently created as W2. **First time entry then posts as `category=labor_internal × $75/hr` instead of `category=subcontractors × $0`** — phantom labor cost, no warning.

The fix: clicking Enable on a field worker now opens a small DropdownMenu with two labeled items matching `CreateUserModal`'s existing copy:

> **Internal Employee (W2)**
> Clocked time × rate flows into the project as labor cost.
>
> **Subcontractor with hourly time tracking**
> Time captured for visibility only — actual cost flows through normal vendor bills.

For admin/manager users (NO_PAYEE + not field_worker), the existing single ghost-button `Enable` is preserved — they don't log labor so the W2/sub distinction doesn't affect them.

### Implementation

- [`useCreateLinkedPayee`](src/hooks/useEmployeesAudit.ts) now takes `{ row, workerType }` instead of a bare row. `workerType: 'internal' | 'subcontractor'` defaults to `'internal'` so all current callers (admin/manager Enable, legacy `EmployeeAuditSection`) stay the same shape. Mutation sets `is_internal`, `payee_type`, `provides_labor`, and `hourly_rate` correctly per type.
- [`RoleManagement.tsx`](src/pages/RoleManagement.tsx) `renderEmployeeRecord` swaps the field-worker `Enable` button for the DropdownMenu. Both desktop table and mobile card layout call this same helper, so behavior is identical on both.
- [`EditProfileModal.tsx`](src/components/EditProfileModal.tsx) rewritten as a Sheet.

## Verification

Local browser preview, chris@radcliffcg.com on fresh storage:

- ✅ Desktop 1280×800: kebab menu → `Edit Profile` opens a 600px right-anchored Sheet titled `Edit User` with Email/Name/Phone/SMS controls
- ✅ Mobile 375×812: card kebab → `Edit Profile` opens full-width Sheet (375px wide, 812px tall, no clipping)
- ✅ Mobile card layout already wires `renderEmployeeRecord` so the new Worker Type dropdown lights up there too
- ✅ `npm run pre-deploy` exit 0
- ✅ Type-check clean

## Test plan

- [x] `npm run pre-deploy` passes
- [x] Edit User opens as Sheet (desktop + mobile)
- [x] Enable dropdown for field workers offers two Worker Type options
- [x] Admin/manager Enable still renders as single ghost button (no Worker Type prompt)
- [ ] After publish: new field-worker subcontractor user → fail auto-payee → click Enable → pick Subcontractor → DB shows `is_internal=false, payee_type='subcontractor'`

## Production deployment

Ship via Lovable Publish (no DB migration, no edge function changes — frontend-only).

author: vucaotung
body:
## Summary

Final PR of the orchestration refactor. Replaces PR2's per-company queue with **per-(runtime, tenant) queues**, slots a **runtime adapter registry** between worker and external runtimes, removes the deprecated `/api/jobs/*` alias, and ships an **Executions tab** on a new task detail page so operators can watch logs, retry, and cancel agent_jobs from the webapp.

## Architecture (now landed)

```
deo.tasks            ← business work
   ↓ 1:N
deo.task_executions  ← per-attempt control plane     (PR2)
   ↓ 1:1+ (sequence_index for chains)
deo.agent_jobs       ← per-runtime artifact          (PR2)
   ↓ id pushed to Redis
jobs:queue:<runtime_type>:<company_id>                (PR3)
   ↓ LPOP
worker → orchestrator/dispatcher → runtime adapter   (PR3)
   ↓ writes back
agent_jobs.queue_state, log_tail, tokens, cost
   ↓ cascade
task_executions.status → tasks.execution_status
```

## Backend

### New: `apps/api/src/orchestrator/`

- **`dispatcher.ts`** — `buildQueueKey(runtime_type, company_id)` and `dispatchAgentJob({agentJobId, runtimeType, companyId})`. Single source of truth for queue naming. Format: `jobs:queue:<runtime_type>:<company_id>` so a noisy runtime or tenant cannot starve others.
- **`runtimes/types.ts`** — `RuntimeAdapter` interface, `AgentJobContext`, `RuntimeRunResult`. Real adapters slot in without touching dispatcher or worker.
- **`runtimes/{claude-code, openclaw, n8n, internal}.ts`** — stub adapters that return `succeeded` with a small `log_tail`. Real CLI spawn / HTTP POST / n8n webhook wiring is tracked separately.
- **`runtimes/index.ts`** — registry exposing `getRuntimeAdapter()` and `listRuntimeTypes()`.
- **`sweeper.ts`** — marks `agent_jobs` claimed/running > 10 min as `'dead'` and cascades parent `task_executions` to `'failed'`. Runs on the worker loop every 60s.

### Rewrite: `apps/api/src/worker.ts`

- Discovers `(runtime_type, company_id)` pairs with queued `agent_jobs` via SQL, LPOPs the matching per-runtime queue (no dead-queue polling).
- Loads context (`agent_job + task_execution + task`), dispatches to the matching adapter, persists `output`, `log_tail` (16K cap), `tokens_in/out`, `cost_usd`, `finished_at`.
- Cascades `task_executions.status` and `tasks.execution_status`.
- Adapter exceptions and missing adapters mark `agent_jobs.queue_state = 'dead'` with the error embedded in `output` and the parent execution's `error`.

### Modified

- **`apps/api/src/routes/agent-jobs.ts`** — `createExecutionAndEnqueue` now uses `buildQueueKey()` and `dispatchAgentJob()`. Removed `legacyJobsRouter` and its export.
- **`apps/api/src/index.ts`** — removed `app.use('/api/jobs', legacyJobsRouter)` mount and import.

## Webapp

### New types + API client

- **`apps/web/src/types.ts`** — `TaskExecutionListRow`, `AgentJob`, status / queue_state unions matching the API.
- **`apps/web/src/api/client.ts`** — `getTask`, `getTaskExecutions`, `createTaskExecution`, `getAgentJob`, `patchAgentJobStatus`, `retryAgentJob`, `cancelAgentJob`.

### New components

- **`apps/web/src/components/AgentJobCard.tsx`** — queue_state badge, runtime label, duration / tokens / cost, scrollable preformatted `log_tail`, collapsible output JSON, **Retry / Cancel** buttons. Polls `GET /api/agent-jobs/:id` every 2s while in `queued/claimed/running`.
- **`apps/web/src/components/ExecutionsList.tsx`** — task_executions latest-first, each row expandable to its `AgentJobCard`. **"Chạy mới"** button posts a new execution. Polls `GET /api/tasks/:id/executions` every 5s while any execution is `pending/running`.

### New page + routing

- **`apps/web/src/pages/TaskDetail.tsx`** — route `/tasks/:id` with tabs **"Tổng quan"** (description, assignee, due, timestamps) and **"Lần chạy"** (mounts `ExecutionsList`).
- **`apps/web/src/App.tsx`** — added `<Route path="/tasks/:id" element={<TaskDetail />} />`.
- **`apps/web/src/pages/Tasks.tsx`** — slide panel now shows **"Mở chi tiết"** + **"Chỉnh sửa"** side by side (link → `/tasks/:id`).

## Verified

- **API** — `npx tsc --noEmit` exit 0. Build emits orchestrator + worker output cleanly.
- **Web** — my new and modified files (`TaskDetail.tsx`, `AgentJobCard.tsx`, `ExecutionsList.tsx`, `App.tsx`, `Tasks.tsx`, `types.ts`, `api/client.ts`) typecheck clean. The 52 errors `tsc` prints are pre-existing tech debt in unrelated pages/components — out of PR3 scope and tracked separately.
- **Diff** — 18 files, +1035 / -498. New: 8 backend orchestrator files, 3 web components/pages. Removed: 320+ lines of `legacyJobsRouter`.

## Test plan

- [ ] **Backend smoke** — start api + worker; `POST /api/tasks/:id/executions {runtime_type:'internal'}` returns 201; row pushed to `jobs:queue:internal:<company>`; worker LPOPs, runs `internalAdapter`, writes `agent_jobs.queue_state='done'`, `output={stub:'internal',...}`, `log_tail` populated; execution `succeeded`, task `execution_status='success'`.
- [ ] **Each runtime** — same with `runtime_type` `claude-code` / `openclaw` / `n8n`. All resolve to the corresponding stub.
- [ ] **No adapter** — manually insert `agent_job.runtime_type='nonexistent'` and enqueue. Worker marks job `dead`, execution `failed` with error message.
- [ ] **Sweeper** — manually set `agent_jobs.started_at = NOW() - INTERVAL '11 minutes'` with `queue_state='running'`. Within 60s, sweeper marks it `dead` and cascades execution to `failed`.
- [ ] **Webapp** — open `/tasks`, click a task, click **"Mở chi tiết"** → land on `/tasks/:id`. Switch to **"Lần chạy"** tab. Click **"Chạy mới"** → new execution row appears; expand → `AgentJobCard` shows `running` then transitions to `done` within 2-5s with log_tail and output. **Retry** disabled while active, enabled after terminal; clicking creates a new execution. **Cancel** PATCHes status to `cancelled`.
- [ ] **`/api/jobs/*` removed** — `curl /api/jobs/anything` returns 404. (External callers have been migrated; documented in PR2.)

- Real runtime adapter implementations (Claude Code CLI subprocess, openclaw HTTP, n8n webhook callback). Stubs unblock the UI today; real wiring is a separate PR per runtime.

author: thejchap
body:
## Summary
Adds a parent-death watchdog so `python -m tryke.worker` processes don't survive their parent. Repro: starting `tryke test --watch` (or `tryke server`) and then killing the rust process used to leave 6+ python workers chewing CPU in the background.

## Key changes

**Python worker (`python/tryke/worker.py`)**
- `_parent_is_alive()` compares the current parent PID against the one captured at module import — comparing against the *initial* PPID (rather than hard-coding 1) keeps the check correct inside containers where the spawning process is itself PID 1.
- `_watch_parent_and_exit()` polls every 500 ms and calls `os._exit(0)` when reparented.
- `main()` only spawns the watchdog daemon thread on `os.name == "posix"` — non-posix platforms have no portable reparenting signal, so the thread would otherwise be a permanent no-op sleeper. Pipe-close cleanup handles parent exit on Windows.

**Rust server (`crates/tryke_server/src/server.rs`)**
- Connection spawning extracted into `spawn_connection()`.
- Accept loop selects on a once-pinned `tokio::signal::ctrl_c()` future; on Ctrl-C it calls `pool.shutdown()` and returns.
- Comment documents that the rust shutdown is best-effort — the python watchdog is the load-bearing guarantee.

**Rust watch mode (`crates/tryke/src/watch.rs`)**
- `spawn_signal_listener()` flips `WatchKeys::quit` on Ctrl-C, so the watch loop breaks through its existing shutdown path.
- Coexists with the progress reporter's `ctrlc::set_handler` via `signal-hook-registry`'s multi-handler support.

**Worker pool (`crates/tryke_runner/src/pool.rs`)**
- `shutdown` is now `&self` so the server can call it through its `Arc<WorkerPool>`.

**Cargo.toml**
- Adds the `signal` feature to the workspace `tokio` dependency.

**Tests (`tests/test_worker.py`)**
- `_wait_for_pid_exit` helper polls process aliveness.
- `test_orphaned_worker_exits` is the load-bearing end-to-end check: the wrapper sends a 30 s `run_test` RPC before orphaning the worker, so the worker is busy in test code (not reading stdin) and only the watchdog can kill it within the 5 s deadline. Also asserts wrapper return-code/stderr before parsing the worker pid.
- Sanity tests for `_parent_is_alive` and the watchdog symbol.

## Why polling rather than signals

- Catches every parent-death path (SIGINT, SIGKILL, panic, OOM) without depending on signal delivery.
- Survives the container case where the spawning process is itself PID 1.
- Doesn't race with `Worker.run`'s blocking stdin read.

## Test plan
- [x] `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`
- [x] `cargo nextest run --workspace --all-features` — 620 passed
- [x] `uv run cargo run -- test` — 220 passed / 3 skipped / 3 xfailed / 1 todo
- [x] `uvx prek run -a`
- [x] Manual repro: kill `tryke test --watch` from ghostty, confirm no surviving `python -m tryke.worker` processes

## Summary

- Manual-grant users (\`cardAccessGrantedAt\` set on the BE → \`hasCardAccess: true\`) keep reaching their card even when the FE maintenance kill-switch \`disableCardPioneers\` is on. Lets us run a closed-test cohort without exposing the public Pioneer waitlist.
- Flips \`disableCardPioneers\` to \`true\` so the gate takes effect on deploy.

## Behaviour matrix

| Maintenance flag | hasCardAccess | Profile "Your Card" | \`/card\` route |
|---|---|---|---|
| OFF | any | shown | accessible (unchanged) |
| ON | false | hidden | redirects to \`/home\` |
| ON | true | shown | accessible (AddCard or YourCard) |

## Files

- \`src/hooks/useCardPioneerInfo.ts\` — fetch unconditionally for authed users (was gated on the maintenance flag); expose \`hasCardAccess\` convenience boolean.
- \`src/app/(mobile-ui)/card/page.tsx\` — redirect + null-render bypass for \`hasCardAccess\` users; redirect now waits for cardInfo so we don't bounce them before reading state.
- \`src/components/Profile/index.tsx\` — gate "Your Card" menu on \`!disableCardPioneers || hasCardAccess\`.
- \`src/config/underMaintenance.config.ts\` — \`disableCardPioneers: false → true\`.

## Test plan

- [ ] On staging, user **without** \`cardAccessGrantedAt\`: \`/card\` redirects to \`/home\`; "Your Card" hidden in profile.
- [ ] Grant access via \`POST /dev/grant-card-access\` (or \`scripts/grant-card-access.ts\`).
- [ ] User **with** \`cardAccessGrantedAt\`: \`/card\` opens AddCardEntryScreen; "Your Card" visible in profile.
- [ ] Granted user can complete Rain card application end-to-end.

## Notes

- BE-side \`CARD_PIONEERS_ENABLED\` constant is independent of this change and remains \`false\` on \`dev\`/\`main\`. The BE \`/card\` info endpoint already returns \`hasCardAccess: !!cardAccessGrantedAt\` regardless of the BE flag, so no BE change needed.
- Pioneer **modal** on \`/home\` and **carousel CTA** still gated only on the maintenance flag — they're marketing surfaces, not access surfaces, and don't block manual users from getting a card. Out of scope here.

## Summary

Phase 4 W1-4 per [`docs/build-spec.md` § Phase 4 scope item 13](../docs/build-spec.md). Unblocks the **H1 operational hand-off** (Bicep apply → AI Search Basic provisioned in dev) and the Wave 2 W2-3 embedding pipeline + index population (per [ADR-0021](../docs/adr/0021-ai-search-index-schema.md)'s `pinwiz-rag-v1` index schema).

This is the smallest planned PR of Wave 1 — a 1-line param flip + the post-deploy smoke probe needed for H1 verification.

## What ships

- **`infra/main-shared.dev.bicepparam`**: add `param deployAiSearch = true`. AI Search Basic was deferred during Phase 3 H1 fix-up via the `deployAiSearch=false` override in `main-shared.dev.local.bicepparam` (East US 2 capacity exhausted on H1 day, 2026-05-07; Phase 3 doesn't consume AI Search). Phase 4 RAG ingestion is the consumer; flipping the committed param makes the intent explicit.
- **New `AiSearchOptions`** in `Core/Configuration/`: `Endpoint` ([Url]-validated) + `IndexName` (default `pinwiz-rag-v1`); mirrors `AiFoundryOptions` sectioning + `EndpointKey` constant for gating.
- **New `IAzureAiSearchSmokeProbe` + `AzureAiSearchSmokeProbe`** in `Infrastructure/Integrations/AiSearch/`: connects via `DefaultAzureCredential`, calls `SearchIndexClient.GetServiceStatisticsAsync` (lightest call exercising endpoint reachability + AAD auth), returns a structured result. Idempotent, structured-result-on-failure, safe to re-run. Mirrors `AzureFoundrySmokeProbe` line-for-line.
- **New `AddAzureAiSearchIntegration`** DI extension: binds options + registers the probe with `ValidateOnStart`. Mirrors `AddAzureFoundryIntegration`.
- **New `--ensure-ai-search` CLI flag** in `Program.cs`: exit-code-2 + remediation message when `AiSearch:Endpoint` isn't configured; success message reports the endpoint + expected index name. Gated DI via `CreateHost` so absence is valid config in Phase 0/1/2/3 and in local dev before H1.
- **New `Azure.Search.Documents` 11.7.0** NuGet — the GA major covering the semantic-ranker + vector-field surface ADR-0021 locks. Wave 2 W2-3 extends consumption for index creation + upsert; Wave 3 W3-3 adds hybrid-retrieval queries.
- **6 new unit tests** mirroring `AzureFoundrySmokeProbeTests` shape (empty/whitespace/malformed endpoint, custom-IndexName preservation through failure result, ctor null guards).

## Test Plan

- [x] `dotnet build PinballWizard.slnx` — **0 warnings, 0 errors**
- [x] `dotnet test PinballWizard.slnx` — **724 / 724 passing** (was 718; +6 from `AzureAiSearchSmokeProbeTests`)
- [x] Sibling-diff against `Integrations/Foundry/AzureFoundrySmokeProbe` — see "Local review" section
- [ ] **Post-merge H1 verification** (operator hand-off, not part of this PR — see below)

## Out of Scope

- The Bicep `apply` itself (operator hand-off H1 — see "Operator follow-up" below).

author: nlemoine
body:
This implements Cupitt's sketch from #55. Instead of running load and resize as two separate libvips calls, the resize-family modifiers now call `thumbnail()` / `thumbnail_buffer()` directly on the original source (file path or buffer).

For that to work, the decoder keeps a reference to the source. `FilePathImageDecoder` and `BinaryImageDecoder` store one on Core after a clean decode. Any modifier that mutates the image goes through `Core::setNative()`, which clears the reference. So the new path only kicks in for a chain of resizes right after a decode, with no other modifier in between.

It also only kicks in when `!isAnimated()`. CoverModifier additionally requires CENTER alignment, because libvips' `Interesting` enum has no directional crops.

Two readonly value classes (`Source\PathSource`, `Source\BufferSource`) hold the reference. The decoder does not store it for sources where the parent decoder transforms the image (BW/GREY16 to SRGB conversion, auto-rotation), since the source bytes can not reproduce that.

Bench (cover()+jpeg85, docker, libvips 8.18.1, php 8.3.31, noise JPEG fixtures):

| Source | Op | develop | this PR | Δ |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 960x1280 | cover(800,300) | 13.09 ms | 13.22 ms | within noise |
| 4000x3000 | cover(800,300) | 63.26 ms | 53.94 ms | -15 % |
| 6000x4000 | cover(800,300) | 122.68 ms | 103.47 ms | -16 % |
| 6000x4000 | cover(150,100) | 138.94 ms | 83.63 ms | -40 % |

The speedup grows with source size and with how much smaller the target is. Cupitt reports ~4x on a real 6k x 4k photo in #55. Our fixtures are noise JPEGs, less favourable than real photos, so we see less.

Output bytes change a bit. The new path does not produce the same exact pixel values as decoding fully then resizing in memory. Cupitt acknowledged this in #55. Existing tests still pass without changing any pixel-value assertions.

author: copilot
body:
Adds the JetBrains fetcher (MVP 2), which introduces the first case of grouping multiple API entries into a single versioned JSON file via a `builds[]` array.

## Changes

- **`scripts/fetchers/jetbrains.py`** — Paginates the JetBrains Marketplace API (`/plugins/17718/updates`), parses version strings (e.g. `1.9.0-251` → semver + IDE build), groups all per-build-line entries by semver, collapses into one JSON per version with a `builds[]` sub-array. Uses earliest `cdate` across builds as `release_date`. Handles all real-world version formats from the API (no updates are ever skipped due to version format).
- **`scripts/common/http.py`** — Added `use_auth=False` parameter to `get_json()` and a `get_session_no_auth()` helper so third-party APIs (like JetBrains Marketplace) are not sent the GitHub token.
- **`scripts/common/schema.json`** — Updated `ide_build` in the `builds[]` items to allow `null` (needed for legacy universal releases that have no per-build-line suffix).
- **`config/ides.yml`** — Adds `jetbrains` IDE entry (`start_version: all`).
- **`data/jetbrains/`** — 133 JSON release files written from a live run against the Marketplace API, covering all versions from `1.0.1` to `1.9.0`.
- **`.github/workflows/fetch-jetbrains.yml`** — Daily cron + `workflow_dispatch`, direct push to `main`, same pattern as Eclipse workflow.
- **`tests/test_jetbrains_fetcher.py`** — 76 tests covering version parsing (all four formats), semver grouping, pagination deduplication, `builds[]` contents, date derivation, legacy version handling, and edge cases (`cdate` as string, missing `cdate`, unexpected version formats).

## Key design detail

A single semantic version like `1.9.0` ships as separate Marketplace entries per JetBrains IDE build line (`-241`, `-242`, `-243`). These are collapsed into one file:

```json
{
  "version": "1.9.0",
  "release_date": "2026-05-07",
  "builds": [
    { "ide_build": "251", "since": "251.0", "until": "", "downloads": 0 },
    { "ide_build": "243", "since": "243.0", "until": "243.*", "downloads": 667994 }
  ]
}
```

Older releases shipped as universal entries with no build-line suffix — either 4-part (e.g. `1.5.29.7524`) or 3-part (e.g. `1.1.1`). These are stored with `ide_build: null`.

## Real API quirks fixed (discovered via live run)

1. **HTTP 403** — the shared session was forwarding `GITHUB_TOKEN` to `plugins.jetbrains.com`. Fixed with `use_auth=False`.
2. **`cdate` is a string** — the API returns `"1778131970000"` (not an integer). Fixed with an explicit `int()` cast.
3. **Legacy no-build-suffix versions** — entries like `1.5.29.7524` and `1.1.1` have no `-NNN` suffix. The version regex now accepts any `X.Y.Z+` format (3 or more parts), so no updates are ever skipped due to version format.
4. **Duplicate entries across pages** — the API repeats the same entry `id` on consecutive pages when a new release is published during pagination. Fixed by deduplicating on `id` in `_paginate_updates()`.

author: ivanbooth6-sketch
body:
### Motivation
- Avoid having the main conservative update kernel read neighboring cells from the field it is simultaneously writing, and remove device-side prints from the limiter path.
- Ensure the pressure limiter reads a stable snapshot of the new state (including ghost fills) so limiter decisions and corrections are deterministic and race-free on devices.
- Apply negative-pressure corrections using a local floor derived from a stable snapshot rather than from `S_new` that is still being updated in-place.

### Description
- Removed in-kernel pressure limiting and device-side `amrex::Print()` from the main `ParallelFor`; the main kernel now only computes and writes conservative/diagnostic values into `S_new` (`StateUpdate`).
- Added `#include <AMReX_Reduce.H>` and a post-update `FillPatcherFill(S_new, ...)` followed by creation of a scratch `MultiFab stable_state` copied from the freshly updated `S_new` so limiter reads stable data.
- Implemented a reduction (`ReduceOps<ReduceOpSum>`) over `stable_state` to count cells with non-positive pressure, print a single host-side warning if any were found, and then run a separate GPU pass that reads only `stable_state` and writes only the corrected `UENG` entries (uses a `pressure_floor`), followed by `Gpu::streamSynchronize()`.
- Made `EN` const in the main update and replaced direct `VectNew` writes with `StateUpdate` array accesses; preserved other diagnostics (vorticity, magGradRho) in the same update pass.

### Testing
- Ran `git diff --check` to validate the patch formatting and it completed without errors.
- Attempted to build the `Exec/ShockTube_OY` target with `make -C Exec/ShockTube_OY -j2`, but the build could not proceed in this environment because `AMREX_HOME` / AMReX makefiles are not configured, so a full compile/test was not executed.

body:
## Summary

- Bumps the `claude-pr-review` reusable workflow pin from `@v2.4.0` to `@v2.4.1`.
- One-line YAML change in `.github/workflows/claude-pr-review.yml`.

## Why

The previous bump to `@v2.4.0` (#297) did **not** fix the shadow quality-gate `marker_missing` failure. PR #298 (the first review run on v2.4.0) confirmed it: `claude-pr-review/quality-gate-shadow` still posted `state=error / description=marker_missing`.

Root cause turned out to be upstream and orthogonal to the producer/consumer skew originally diagnosed in #296: the `v2.4.0` tag in `glitchwerks/github-actions` was placed on a stale commit whose workflow pinned an old `claude-runtime-review` container digest — built before [glitchwerks/github-actions#228](https://github.com/glitchwerks/github-actions/pull/228) added the structured-marker emission directive to the review persona. The bad pin landed because PR #238's branch was based on a pre-promote state of `main`, and the merge stomped a runtime promote ~2 days old. `main` was re-promoted minutes later, but `v2.4.0` was tagged before the re-promote.

`v2.4.1` ([release notes](https://github.com/glitchwerks/github-actions/releases/tag/v2.4.1)) retargets `main` HEAD — pinning `claude-runtime-review@sha256:0db0d558…`, the correct post-#228 image that emits the marker.

## Test plan

- [ ] CI completes without workflow-validation startup failures
- [ ] Once merged, the next PR review run posts `claude-pr-review/quality-gate-shadow` with `state=success` (or legitimate `state=failure` on a review with BLOCKING/MAJOR markers) — not `state=error / marker_missing`

## Related

- Prior bump that didn't fix it: #296, #297
- Upstream diagnosis: glitchwerks/github-actions#242
- Upstream fix: glitchwerks/github-actions release [v2.4.1](https://github.com/glitchwerks/github-actions/releases/tag/v2.4.1)

Fixes #299

author: cjs77
body:
Replaces the daemon's fixed `setInterval` driver with a cron-aware scheduler backed by a file-based config layer. Operators can now set `schedule` in `~/.minesweeper/config.json` to drive the poll loop with one or more cron expressions; the existing interval fallback is kept for deployments that configure nothing. A global `pollCooldownSeconds` gate (default 120 s) prevents overlapping schedules from double-polling within the cooldown window.

## Changes
- `src/config.ts`: added `schedule`, `pollCooldownSeconds`, `pollCooldownMs` to `ConfigSchema`; new `ConfigFileSchema` (omits derived fields, `.strict().partial()`); `readConfigFile` helper with `null`-sentinel for tests; `loadConfig` gains `{ configFile?: string | null }` and resolves precedence env > file > hard-coded defaults
- `src/daemon/poller.ts`: replaced `specs: readonly number[]` with `Schedule = { kind: "interval" } | { kind: "cron" }` discriminated union; cron schedules self-reschedule via `setTimeout`; immediate first-tick fires only when an interval schedule is present; `cooldownMs`/`now()` are injectable so tests can pin the clock
- `src/cli.ts`: builds `Schedule[]` from `config.schedule` (cron) or `config.pollIntervalMs` (interval fallback); startup-log message includes cooldown
- `src/daemon/index.ts`: re-exports `Schedule` type
- `.env.sample` / `README.md`: document `MINESWEEPER_POLL_COOLDOWN`, `MINESWEEPER_CONFIG_FILE`, precedence rule, and cron-only no-immediate-tick behaviour
- `package.json`: add `cron-parser ^4.9.0` (parse-only; we keep our own timer scheduling)
- All `*.test.ts` files calling `loadConfig(...)`: append `{ configFile: null }` so a local `~/.minesweeper/config.json` cannot leak into CI or developer test runs
- Config-literal test fixtures in `claude/` and `child/` tests: add `schedule: []`, `pollCooldownSeconds: 120`, `pollCooldownMs: 120_000`

## Test plan
- `npm run typecheck` passes
- `npm run lint` passes
- `npm test` passes — 323 tests pass, 23 e2e skipped; new poller suite covers cron-only no-immediate-tick, cron fires at computed delay (fake timers), cooldown skips overlapping ticks, cooldown=0 disables gate, `stop()` cancels pending cron timeouts
- `npm run build` passes
- Note: `cron-parser` v4 ships CJS; import is `import cronParser from "cron-parser"` with `cronParser.parseExpression(...)` — the named-export form in the plan fails under Node ESM

Fixes #12

author: t3lurid3
body:
Summary:
Mirrors the previous commit's GlobaltimerCalibration refresh — now applied to the CudaReferencePoint baseline used by eager-mode CudaWaitEvent. The colltrace poll thread already calls `GlobaltimerCalibration::get().refresh()` once per second; this commit adds a parallel `CudaReferencePoint::tryGet()->refresh()` call from the same site so eager-mode timestamps stay aligned with PTP wall time at the same cadence.

The previous CudaReferencePoint design captured a single (cudaEvent, host_time) pair in its constructor and used it for the lifetime of the process. cudaEventElapsedTime is bounded by the GPU's oscillator (±10–100 ppm), so without re-anchoring the mapping drifts ~36–360 ms per hour against PTP. With 1 Hz refresh, residual intra-anchor drift is bounded below 100 ns at 100 ppm.

Refactor — symmetric with `GlobaltimerCalibration`:

- `CudaReferencePoint` now holds `folly::Synchronized<Anchor>`, where `Anchor = {cudaEvent_t event, system_clock_time_point time}`. Readers (`getTimeViaEvent`) hold an rlock for the entire `cudaEventElapsedTime` call so `refresh()` cannot destroy the reference event mid-read.
- `refresh()` records a fresh event on a private idle stream, syncs, swaps the anchor under wlock, then destroys the old event after the wlock is released. Holding the wlock briefly during the swap guarantees in-flight readers complete before the new event is published, so the old event is unreachable to any subsequent reader and safe to destroy without holding a writer lock across a CUDA call. CUDA failures are logged via `XLOG_EVERY_MS(WARN, 5000)` and the prior anchor is kept (no thrown exceptions, no anchor corruption).
- Static `tryGet()` returns the singleton if it has ever been constructed, otherwise `nullptr`. Backed by an atomic `g_referencePointInstance` set at the end of the constructor with release semantics; `tryGet()` reads with acquire semantics. Lets the colltrace poll thread skip the eager-mode refresh entirely in CPU-only colltrace deployments where no `CudaWaitEvent` is ever created — avoids forcing CUDA initialization.
- Constructor now explicitly `cudaStreamSynchronize`s before reading `precisionNow()` so the host_time anchor is not earlier than the GPU reading. The leak philosophy (intentional non-destruction at process exit to avoid `cudaErrorCudartUnloading` segfaults) is documented in the class comment.

Poll thread (`CollTrace.cc`): the existing 1 Hz block (now gated on `NCCL_COLLTRACE_PERIODIC_REANCHOR`) also calls `CudaReferencePoint::tryGet()->refresh()` when the singleton exists. Both refreshes share the `kReanchorInterval = 1s` cadence and the same `lastReanchor` timestamp — one wake-up handles both calibrations.

Known limitation: the first eager-mode collective on a thread still uses the constructor's anchor (≤1 second before refresh kicks in, when enabled). Drift accumulated over 1 second at 100 ppm is ~100 µs, well below typical collective timing resolution.

## — addressed review feedback

- **Reuses `NCCL_COLLTRACE_PERIODIC_REANCHOR`** which was previously introduced to gate the eager-mode CudaReferencePoint refresh as well. The colltrace poll thread now wraps both the GlobaltimerCalibration and the CudaReferencePoint refresh calls in a single `if (NCCL_COLLTRACE_PERIODIC_REANCHOR)` block, sharing one shared `lastReanchor` timestamp — one wake-up handles both calibrations, both off by default.
- **Fixed the misleading lock-scope comment** on `CudaReferencePoint::refresh`. The wlock scope only covers the swap; `cudaEventDestroy(oldEvent)` runs after the wlock is released. Code is unchanged (it was already correct — the wlock guarantees in-flight readers have released their rlock before the new event is published, so the old event is unreachable when destroyed). The comment now accurately describes the protocol.

---

Reviewed By: YulunW

Differential Revision: D102076826

author: billdenney
body:
Semi-mechanistic exposure-response model of uric acid (UA) disposition in adults (Aksenov et al., Physiol Rep 2018, doi:10.14814/phy2.13614). Models UA balance as production (kP) minus intestinal clearance (CL_I) minus renal flux (GFR x F_E x [S]_UA), with three drug interventions entering as time-varying plasma-concentration covariates: oxypurinol (active metabolite of allopurinol) and febuxostat inhibit production (Eq. 9), and lesinurad (URAT1 reabsorption inhibitor) increases F_E (Eq. 10). Parameter values come from Aksenov 2018 Table 1 and Appendix 2 Table 2; drug-PK parameters are not published in the source so the user supplies CP_OXY_NGML, CP_FBX_NGML, CP_LSN_NGML directly.

Registers three new canonical covariate columns (CP_OXY_NGML, CP_FBX_NGML, CP_LSN_NGML) following the CP_MGL drug-specific pattern. GFR registers under CRCL with source_name = "GFR" (Cockcroft-Gault, non-BSA-normalized, mL/min). Compartments serum / urine are paper-named mechanistic states; checkModelConventions raises only the expected two compartment-name warnings (justified in vignette Assumptions).

Vignette validates: steady-state hold (drift < 1e-6 mg/dL over 500 h), mass balance at SS (production = intestinal + renal flux to machine precision), 35% reduction at oxypurinol 10000 ng/mL matching Eq. 13 narrative, ~800 mg/day urinary UA at typical 75-kg adult matching Bianchi 1979 reference, monotonic SS-vs-GFR curve matching Figure 6, single-dose lesinurad time profiles qualitatively replicating Figure 4 (50/200/600 mg), and conceptual sequential-treatment Figure 5 replication.

### Motivation

- Make Task 01 deterministic and easier to test by tightening the PowerShell task specification for artifact export and environment checks.
- Remove ambiguity about fatal vs non-fatal diagnostics for Docker and endpoints so solutions and hidden tests can be robustly evaluated.
- Improve automated testability by expanding the export summary schema and clarifying include/exclude precedence and exit-code semantics.

### Description

author: dennybiasiolli
body:
### What

Add `clear(c.watchedKeys)` to `Context.Abort()` so that all transactional state — including WATCH registrations — is fully reset when a transaction is aborted.

### Why

`Abort()` resets `keys`, `inTx`, `txnID`, and `txSnapshot`, but leaves `watchedKeys` populated. When `closeSession()` calls `Abort()` on a mid-transaction disconnect, stale WATCH state survives in the `Context`. The Redis layer is unaffected because it always calls `ClearWatches()` explicitly, but the SQL session teardown path relies solely on `Abort()`.

While `Context` is not reused today, the leftover state violates `Abort()`'s contract of producing a clean slate and is a latent bug if `Context` reuse is ever introduced (e.g., connection pooling).

Fix #27 

### Changes

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `effects/context.go` | Add `clear(c.watchedKeys)` to `Abort()` |
| `effects/emit_test.go` | Add 3 test cases covering the fix |

### Tests Added

- **`TestAbortClearsWatchedKeys`** — `Watch` two keys, `BeginTx`, `Abort`, assert `watchedKeys` is empty.
- **`TestAbortClearsWatchedKeysWithoutTx`** — `Watch` a key, `Abort` without `BeginTx`, assert `watchedKeys` is empty.
- **`TestAbortAllowsCleanReuse`** — `Watch` + `BeginTx` + `Emit` + `Abort`, assert every field (`keys`, `watchedKeys`, `inTx`, `txnID`, `txSnapshot`) is fully reset.

### Verification

Full `./effects/` test suite passes with no regressions.

## Summary
- Per-session mutable state container — the data layer the loop reads and writes each iteration.
- Foundational scaffolding: real behavior for prompt assembly, steering, context pressure, scratchpad, and the error counter; stable seams (no impl) for compaction/nudges/truncation/cache, which land with the guardrails module.

## What's in
- `Turn`, `Note`, `Prompt` dataclasses
- `ToolSpec` / `ModelAdapter` Protocol stubs so `state.py` doesn't have a backwards dep on the tools or adapters modules
- `build_prompt()` with stable/dynamic boundary (G1) — `stable` is byte-identical across iterations as long as role + tools don't change, so adapters that support prompt caching can mark it cacheable
- `refresh_context()` for `iters_remaining`, `now`, `answer_id` (G6); G7 ("surface relevant prior notes") left as a no-op hook until retrieval skills land
- Steering queue: `enqueue_steering`, `has_pending_steering`, `consume_steering` (SPEC §5.6) — FIFO list of `(message, mode)` tuples; the loop decides interrupt vs queue semantics when consuming
- `add_note()` FIFO scratchpad (G8), capped at `max_session_notes`
- `context_pressure()` driven by a pluggable `token_counter` field; default is tiktoken `cl100k_base` (lazy-imported, cached); users can pass `len(s)//4`, an Anthropic counter, or anything else
- `record_tool_error` / `record_tool_success` / `consecutive_errors()` (G4 hook)

## Deliberately deferred
- Compaction (G5/G10), nudges (G3/G4), per-tool truncation (G2), tool result cache (G9) — owned by the guardrails task. State exposes the data they mutate but does not implement them.
- Real relevance scoring for G7 — placeholder hook only.

## Deps
- Adds `tiktoken>=0.7` to project dependencies.

- [x] `uv run ruff format --check .`

author: shutovdef-dotcom
body:
## Problem

User reports on mobile: opening any \`/v/[slug]/\` page, the apply button is only reachable at the very top (hero) and at the very bottom (sidebar). Between them — nothing tappable while reading.

Existing CSS at \`[slug].astro:1782\` (\`.apply-btn-hero { position: fixed }\` for ≤ 768 px) was supposed to keep the hero button pinned to the viewport bottom on mobile — but on the user's actual device something overrides it. Without access to that device for live debugging, this PR ships a separate, self-contained component that delivers the behaviour reliably.

## What it does

New \`src/components/VacancyStickyApply.astro\` — sticky bar at viewport bottom on every \`/v/[slug]/\` page.

| State | Bar |
|---|---|
| Hero \`.apply-btn-hero\` is in viewport (top of page) | hidden — no point duplicating the visible button |
| User scrolls past hero | bar slides up, follows the user |
| User scrolls back up to hero | bar hides again |
| Disabled vacancy (no \`apply-btn-hero\`, just \`apply-btn-disabled\`) | bar skipped entirely |

Tap on bar → programmatic \`.click()\` on the hero button. All existing flows run unchanged:

- Default \`<a data-apply-cta>\` → browser opens partner URL (with UTM)
- Ozon \`<button data-lead-form-type=\"ozon\">\` → existing click delegate opens \`OzonLeadModal\`
- GA4 \`apply_click\` event fires via the \`BaseLayout.astro\` delegate (it listens to any \`[data-apply-cta]\` click, regardless of source)

No new GA4 events, no new env vars, no new endpoints, no data changes.

## Z-index strategy

\`vacancy-sticky-apply\` is set to **\`z-index: 91\`**, one above the existing mobile-fixed rule's \`90\`. So if that existing CSS does fire on some devices (where the user's bug doesn't reproduce), the new bar still wins visually — single button, no double-button stack.

## Scope

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| \`src/components/VacancyStickyApply.astro\` | new (128 lines, mostly inline JS + scoped CSS) |
| \`src/pages/v/[slug].astro\` | +1 import, +1 mount before \`</main>\`. Existing \`.apply-btn-hero\` rule untouched. |

## Build verified

5565 pages. \`vacancy-sticky-apply\` markup:
- present in all **4584** \`/v/*/\` pages
- absent in every other page (home, city, category, blog, contacts, etc.)

## Preview

Cloudflare Pages should publish a preview at \`https://feat-vacancy-sticky-apply.<project>.pages.dev\` ~ 2 minutes after push.

Open any vacancy on mobile, scroll past the hero — the bar appears at the bottom. Tap → same effect as tapping the original.

## Rollback

\`git revert <this-commit>\` removes both files in one step.

author: ivankobzarev
body:
● ## Fix CPU offloading init hang: bypass DTensor dispatch for param init

  ### Problem

  When running with `--training.enable_cpu_offload`, model initialization hangs indefinitely during `init_weights`. No error, no traceback — just a silent deadlock. Observed on 8B model (10+ min hang), 70B would be proportionally worse.

  ### Root Cause

  When `enable_cpu_offload=True`, parameters are materialized on CPU as DTensors whose device mesh uses NCCL (CUDA). Two issues compound to cause the deadlock:

  **1. SimpleFSDP parametrization triggers allgather during init**

  `simple_fsdp` wraps each module with a `ReplicateComputation` parametrization. During `_init_self_parameters`, `named_parameters(recurse=False)` triggers the parametrization getter → `replicate_compute()` → allgather on every parameter
  access. For CPU tensors with an NCCL-backed mesh, this allgather deadlocks because NCCL expects CUDA tensors.

  **2. DTensor dispatch hangs for in-place random ops on CPU with CUDA mesh**

  Even with the parametrization disabled, `nn.init.normal_(dtensor)` routes through DTensor's `__torch_dispatch__`, which attempts to coordinate the random initialization across ranks via NCCL collectives. NCCL cannot operate on CPU tensors →
   deadlock.

  ### Investigation

  Added timing instrumentation to isolate the bottleneck:

  - `parallelize_fn`: 0.12s ✓
  - `to_empty(cpu)`: 0.02s ✓
  - `init_weights` layers (32 transformer blocks): 4.91s ✓
  - `init_weights` lm_head (SimpleFSDPLinear, 525M params): **HANG**

  Notably, `tok_embeddings` (same 525M params) succeeded — it runs first before NCCL is fully initialized. By the time `lm_head` runs, NCCL strictly requires CUDA tensors.

  Benchmarked plain CPU `normal_()`: ~42s for the full 8B model, ~5s with tp=8 sharding. The hang is not CPU being slow — it is a deadlock in DTensor/NCCL dispatch.

  ### Fix

  **`protocols/module.py` — init local tensor directly:**

  ```python
  # Before (hangs — DTensor dispatch tries NCCL collectives on CPU):
  self._param_init[name](param)

  # After (bypasses DTensor dispatch entirely):
  from torch.distributed._tensor import DTensor
  init_target = param._local_tensor if isinstance(param, DTensor) else param
  self._param_init[name](init_target)

  Each rank initializes its own local shard independently, which is correct for random initialization of sharded parameters.

  trainer.py — disable parametrization during init:

  # Before (allgather on every param access during init):
  cast(BaseModel, model).init_weights(buffer_device=buffer_device)

  # After (skips allgather):
  from torchtitan.experiments.graph_trainer.simple_fsdp import disable_active_parametrization
  with disable_active_parametrization():
      cast(BaseModel, model).init_weights(buffer_device=buffer_device)

  Result

  8B model init_weights with CPU offloading: 10+ min hang → 9.25s

  Test Plan

  - Verified 8B graph_trainer with --training.enable_cpu_offload completes init_weights in ~9s (was hanging indefinitely)
  - Verified 8B graph_trainer without CPU offloading still works (no regression, init_weights ~0.25s)
  - CI integration tests

detection engines model **scanners** — the previous v0.10.0 attempt
to register engines as connectors mixed two unrelated abstractions.

  \`RevokeResult\`.
* github connector implements \`verify(secret)\` against
  \`GET /user\`; new \`pleno-dlp verify <connector> --token …\` CLI.
* Pipeline keyword renamed: \`detector=\` → \`engine=\`.

255 passing, ruff clean, src mypy strict clean.

body:
## Problem

The analysis pipeline was silently stopping after StockExtract with no log output to indicate whether data collection, agent analysis, or post-processing had started or failed. Exceptions in `_process_horizon`, `data_collector.collect`, and the top-level `except` block were either swallowed or logged without stack traces, making it impossible to pinpoint where the flow broke down.

## Solution

Added `[Checkpoint]` log entries at every major step in `_run_job_inner`: graph initialization, intent parsing, data collection start/completion, `asyncio.gather` launch, per-horizon `astream` entry/first-chunk/completion, structured extraction, DB save, and job completion. All `except` blocks now use `logger.error` with `traceback.format_exc()` to emit full stack traces. The top-level exception handler captures elapsed time alongside the traceback so the exact failure point and duration are visible in logs.

### Changes
- **Modified** `api/main.py`

author: codex
body:
`swift test` failed because non-UI targets imported macOS-only frameworks (`SwiftUI`, `AppKit`, `Combine`). This PR isolates UI-only types and conditionally builds macOS-only targets so shared logic compiles in non-macOS toolchains.

- **SPM Target Gating**
  - Split always-buildable targets (`Models`, `Utilities`, `Core`, `Scanning`, `Visualization`) from macOS-only ones.
  - Make `Permissions`, `FileOperations`, `ViewModels`, `UI`, `DiskScopeApp`, and `DiskScopeTests` conditional on `os(macOS)` (`/home/runner/work/DiskScope/DiskScope/Package.swift`).

- **SwiftUI Decoupling (Shared Layers)**
  - Introduce SwiftUI-free primitives in `Models`:
    - `DiskScopeColor` (+ SwiftUI conversion behind `#if canImport(SwiftUI)`)
    - `DiskScopeAngle` (+ SwiftUI conversion behind `#if canImport(SwiftUI)`)
  - Replace direct `SwiftUI.Color`/`SwiftUI.Angle` usage in `Models` and `Visualization` with these primitives (`/home/runner/work/DiskScope/DiskScope/Sources/Models/FileNode.swift`, `/home/runner/work/DiskScope/DiskScope/Sources/Visualization/SunburstSegment.swift`, `/home/runner/work/DiskScope/DiskScope/Sources/Visualization/SunburstLayoutEngine.swift`).

- **Platform Guards**
  - `DriveMonitor` only uses `AppKit`/`NSWorkspace` when available; otherwise yields a single snapshot stream (`/home/runner/work/DiskScope/DiskScope/Sources/Core/DriveMonitor.swift`).
  - Guard `Combine` usage in view models / scanning manager for toolchains where it’s not available (`/home/runner/work/DiskScope/DiskScope/Sources/Scanning/DiskScanManager.swift`, `/home/runner/work/DiskScope/DiskScope/Sources/ViewModels/AppViewModel.swift`, `/home/runner/work/DiskScope/DiskScope/Sources/ViewModels/InspectorViewModel.swift`).

- **Correctness Hardening**
  - Remove potential overflow in color selection by avoiding `abs(Int.min)` on `hashValue` (`/home/runner/work/DiskScope/DiskScope/Sources/Scanning/FileScanner.swift`).
  - Drop `CoreGraphics` imports in `Visualization` where `Foundation` already provides the needed geometry types for this toolchain (`/home/runner/work/DiskScope/DiskScope/Sources/Visualization/SegmentHitTester.swift`).

Example (UI consumes shared primitives):
```swift
path.addArc(
  center: drawCenter,
  radius: segment.outerRadius,
  startAngle: segment.startAngle.swiftUIAngle,
  endAngle: segment.endAngle.swiftUIAngle,
  clockwise: false
)
context.fill(path, with: .color(segment.color.swiftUIColor))
```

author: billdenney
body:
Two-compartment population PK/PD model with first-order oral absorption and a peripheral effect compartment normalized per body weight (digoxin in adults; structural parameters carried from Reuning 1973). Renal elimination is linear in CRCL (kel = knr + kr * CRCL); volumes and clearances scale linearly with body weight. Per-parameter IIV is 20% CV per the paper's stated assumption.

The model file uses log-transformed rate-constant primaries (lknr, lkr, lkcp, lkpc) instead of the canonical lcl/lq/lvp form because Jelliffe 2014 explicitly parameterizes the model with rate constants and describes the peripheral compartment as having no associated volume of distribution -- the deviation is documented in the vignette's Assumptions and deviations section.

Replicates Figures 1-4 of Jelliffe 2014 (typical-value serum and peripheral trajectories for the three illustrative adult patients) and includes a single-dose PKNCA sanity check. Day-8 simulated peak / trough values agree with the paper's narrative within ~10%.

Both the **Built Images** and **Base Images** panels now expose Delete via the shared kebab (⋮) menu pattern (popover-based, defined in 	emplates/_macros.html + .btn-kebab / .kebab-menu CSS + positionKebab() in pp.js) instead of as a standalone Delete button per row.

author: megoru
body:
This update introduces critical security and stability enhancements:

1. **IPC Hardening**: The wide-open IPC bridge in `preload.ts` has been replaced with a strict whitelist of typed methods. Generic `invoke`, `send`, and `removeAllListeners` are no longer available to the renderer.
2. **Input Validation**: All incoming IPC messages in the main process are now validated using `zod` schemas to ensure type safety and prevent malicious payloads.
3. **Async FS**: Heavy synchronous filesystem operations have been moved to the asynchronous `fs.promises` API to prevent main process blocking.
4. **Traversal Protection**: Recursive folder operations now have a maximum depth limit of 20 and include protection against symlink loops.
5. **Encrypted Vault**: SSH passwords are now stored in a separate `encryptedPasswords` vault using AES-256-GCM. A 32-byte Recovery Key is generated for each user, allowing for secure transport and recovery of secrets.
6. **Local Auto-Unlock**: The Recovery Key is securely cached on the local machine using `electron.safeStorage`, enabling a seamless user experience while maintaining high security.
7. **Data Migration**: Existing passwords stored as base64 or simple `safeStorage` strings are automatically migrated to the new vault structure upon the first launch.
8. **Listener Cleanup**: Improved cleanup logic ensures that event listeners on sockets and streams are properly removed when connections are closed, preventing memory leaks.
9. **Version Bump**: The application version has been updated to 1.9.3.

**Potential Breaking Changes**:
- Users will be prompted with a one-time Recovery Key display. This key MUST be saved to restore passwords on other devices or after a clean reinstall.
- Configuration files from version 1.9.3 are backward compatible with older versions (they will ignore the vault), but passwords changed in 1.9.3 will not be visible to older versions.

author: novolei
body:
## Summary

- **Fix minimap visibility (root cause)**: `ScrollMinimap` was rendered inside `Conversation`'s `overflow-y-auto` div, so its `position:absolute` was relative to the scrolling content rather than the viewport — once messages exceeded one screen the minimap silently scrolled out of sight. Wrapped `Conversation` with a relative outer shell and have `ScrollMinimap` `createPortal` into it so it stays fixed against the visible viewport.
- **Refine minimap to a minimal, modern look**: dropped the heavy card chrome and the top icon / vertical guide rail; bars themselves are now the indicator. Graduated lengths (visible 14px > user 9px > assistant 3px) make the contrast obvious, with hover-grow + brighten.
- **Popover panel**: cleaner shell — search bar carries the title and embeds the visible-count chip; soft shadow + backdrop blur; primary accent stripe on visible items; pronounced item hover (full bg, slide, shadow, press-down).
- **Auto-track scroll**: opening the popover scrolls its list so the first currently-visible message lands ~30% from the top.
- **Hide native scrollbar duplication**: removed the self-drawn scroll thumb on the minimap; rely on the OS-native scrollbar alone.
- **Push dock off the scrollbar**: `right-1` → `right-5` to leave breathing room.
- **Responsive layout**: dropped `max-w-[min(72rem,100%)] mx-auto` on both `ChatView` and `AgentView` main panels so content fills the available width.
- **Chat appearance entry consolidation**: `ChatAppearancePopover` (Aa icon) now lives only in `AgentHeader` (left of the file-panel toggle). Removed the duplicate from `ChatHeader`.

## Why

Multiple prior commits tried to make the minimap "more visible" with stronger borders / colors / chrome, but the user could never see it because the issue was structural, not stylistic — the element was absolute-positioned inside a scrolling container, so it scrolled out of the viewport with the content. author: siropkin
body:
## Goal

Surface an actionable balloon when the local daemon's `api_version` is older than the floor this plugin requires (`MIN_API_VERSION = 1`). Parity with `siropkin/budi-cursor#51`.

## Why

The `MIN_API_VERSION` gate already drops the status bar to `RED` when the daemon is stale (#6) — but `RED` looks the same as "daemon offline" today, and a user who has the daemon running but on an old build would have no idea why the cost numbers stopped updating. The balloon names the cause and hands the user the exact command to fix it.

## Stacked on PR #13

This branch is opened against `ivan/issue-5-scaffolding`. **Merge PR #12 → PR #13 → this PR**, in that order. After PR #13 merges, GitHub retargets this PR onto `main` automatically.

## Behavior

- Daemon healthy: balloon stays silent. Per-session latch resets so a within-session regression *can* re-show.
- Daemon stale + first time this session: sticky balloon under the `Budi` group:
  > **budi daemon needs an update**
  > Daemon api_version **0** is older than this plugin requires (**1**). Update budi to keep the status bar working.
  >
  > [Show update command] [Don't show again]
- "Show update command": opens a modal dialog listing both:
  - Universal: `budi update`
  - Platform fallback (e.g. macOS): `brew upgrade siropkin/budi/budi`
  Each with a "Copy" button. **Nothing is auto-executed.**
- "Don't show again": flips `suppressUpdateNotification` in `BudiSettings`. Auto-resets on the *upward edge* — when the daemon catches up after a stale episode and the next stale episode would otherwise be silent. The reset means a new stale episode after a recovery produces a fresh prompt.
- Settings → Tools → budi exposes the suppress toggle directly so users who want it permanently silenced can flip it without waiting for the balloon.

## Throttle correctness

The decision logic is a pure function `evaluateUpgradePrompt(currentApi, previousApi, sessionShown, persistentSuppress)` — no IDE deps, no I/O. Eight unit tests cover the matrix:

| current | previous | sessionShown | persistentSuppress | → showPrompt | resetSession | resetSuppress |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| null | * | * | * | false | false | false |
| ≥ floor | ≥ floor | true | false | false | true | false |
| ≥ floor | < floor | true | true | false | true | **true** |
| ≥ floor | ≥ floor | false | true | false | true | false |
| < floor | ≥ floor | false | false | **true** | false | false |
| < floor | < floor | true | false | false | false | false |
| < floor | ≥ floor | false | true | false | false | false |
| (full recovery sequence — see test) | | | | | | |

## What's in this PR

- \`notifier/BudiUpgradeNotifier.kt\` — application-scoped service that calls into the pure decision function and renders the balloon.
- \`evaluateUpgradePrompt\` — pure decision helper, exported alongside the service.
- \`settings/BudiSettings.kt\` — add `suppressUpdateNotification` and `lastObservedApiVersion`.
- \`settings/BudiConfigurable.kt\` — surface the suppress toggle.
- \`poller/BudiPoller.kt\` — invoke `onHealthObserved` after every poll.
- \`plugin.xml\` — register `BudiUpgradeNotifier` as an `applicationService`.

## Tests (8 new, 48 total green)

- `UpgradeDecisionTest` — full throttle / suppress / reset matrix; includes a four-step recovery scenario (first stale → suppress → recover → re-stale → fresh prompt).

## Verified locally

- \`./gradlew test\` → 48/48 green.
- \`./gradlew verifyPlugin\` → Compatible against IC-242, IC-243, IC-251, IC-252.

## Acceptance

- [x] Notification with "Show update command" + "Don't show again" actions when api_version < MIN_API_VERSION.
- [x] Never auto-runs `budi update`.
- [x] Settings toggle to suppress permanently.
- [x] Per-session throttle so it shows at most once per IDE start.
- [x] Persistent suppress auto-resets on stale → healthy → stale transitions.
- [x] Universal `budi update` one-liner *and* platform fallback both copyable.

## Out of scope

- Daemon-side detection of "an update is available" — that's a budi-core concern (the daemon's `/health.api_version` is the only signal we use here).
- Auto-running `budi update` — explicitly disallowed; the user always pastes and runs themselves.

## References

- Closes #7.
- Stacked on #5 (PR #13).
- Mirrors: \`siropkin/budi-cursor\` upgrade-prompt flow (#51).
