**D. `Restart=` policy correction (Option A).** All 5 unit templates: `Restart=always` retained; added `RestartPreventExitStatus=78`. CLI shim returns `RUNTIME_CHECK_ABORT_EXIT_CODE = 78` (= `EX_CONFIG` per `sysexits.h`) on any `RuntimeCheckError`. Result: invariant abort never auto-restarts (which would mask the bug); transient runtime crashes (any other non-zero code) still auto-restart.

**E. Stable journald marker grammar.** New helper `_emit_marker(role, invariant_name)` writes `RUNTIME_CHECK_FAILED:<role>:<invariant_name>\n` to stderr immediately **before** raising the existing exception type. The 11-name enum is exposed as `RUNTIME_CHECK_INVARIANTS: frozenset[str]` (public stable surface): `role_env_unset`, `role_env_invalid`, `loaded_skills_mismatch`, `operational_db_path_mismatch`, `schema_version_mismatch`, `orchestrator_telegram_token_missing`, `non_orchestrator_telegram_skill_loaded`, `delegate_task_callable`, `skill_manage_callable`, `prompt_manifest_missing`, `prompt_sha_mismatch`. ### Motivation
- The Deriv OAuth callback sometimes returns accounts in different JSON shapes which caused the saved OAuth session to lack real login IDs, preventing the Start flow from requesting a WebSocket OTP and showing Account Balances. 
- Make the callback resilient to multiple response shapes and ensure a usable `DerivSession` is persisted for the dashboard/WebSocket connection.

### Description
- Update `src/pages/AuthCallback.tsx` to accept multiple response shapes (`[]`, `accounts`, `data`, `data.accounts`) and normalize them into a single `accounts` array. 
- Coerce account fields to stable types (`String`/`Number`) and improve virtual-account detection (including `VR` prefixes) so balances/login IDs are preserved. 
- Save the parsed accounts and `active_loginid` into the saved `DerivSession` so the Start button can request OTPs for the selected account. 
- Tighten typing and error handling in the callback by using `Record<string, unknown>` for decoded JWT payloads and `catch (e: unknown)` with an `instanceof` check.

author: lukemarsden
body:
## Summary

When a spec task is merged to main, the bell-icon notifications and Kanban red-dot badges that accumulated during its lifecycle (specs pushed, agent finished, PR ready, etc.) used to linger until the user clicked them or hit "Dismiss all". They're no longer actionable once the task is done — so we now clear them automatically as part of the Done transition.

## Changes

- **`api/pkg/store/store.go`** — added `DismissAttentionEventsForTask(ctx, specTaskID) (int64, error)` to the `Store` interface.
- **`api/pkg/store/store_attention_events.go`** — implemented it: a single `UPDATE attention_events SET dismissed_at = now() WHERE spec_task_id = ? AND dismissed_at IS NULL`. Idempotent.
- **`api/pkg/store/store_mocks.go`** — regenerated by `mockgen`.
- **`api/pkg/store/store_attention_events_test.go`** (new) — covers: dismisses target task only, leaves other tasks alone, idempotent re-run returns 0, unknown task ID is a no-op, empty task ID is a validation error.
- **`api/pkg/services/attention_service.go`** — added a small free function `DismissTaskAttentionEvents(ctx, store, taskID)` that wraps the store call with best-effort logging (failures are logged but never propagated, so a notification-clear failure cannot roll back a task state transition).
- **Wired into 7 Done-transition call sites:**
  - `api/pkg/services/git_http_server.go` — agent auto-merge after rebase, and the post-push branch-merged-to-main detector.
  - `api/pkg/services/spec_task_orchestrator.go` — all-PRs-merged path, the per-PR merge detection, the branch-merged-without-PR fallback, and the branch-merge poll fallback.
  - `api/pkg/server/spec_task_workflow_handlers.go` — the user-driven "Approve Implementation" server-side merge handler.

## Why this approach

- **Server-side dismissal, not a new acknowledge endpoint.** The events are no longer actionable, so we *dismiss* (remove from the active list) rather than acknowledge (which only clears the "new" state but keeps them visible).
- **No new API or pubsub.** With a fixed handful of call sites, calling a helper directly is simpler and easier to grep than introducing an event channel.
- **Best-effort, not transactional.** A DB failure on the dismiss call must not roll back the Done transition — we log and move on. Manual "Dismiss all" still works.
- **No frontend changes.** `useAttentionEvents` already polls every 10s and `ListAttentionEvents` already filters out dismissed rows; the next poll naturally drops the events.

## Test plan

- [ ] CI runs the new `TestPostgresStore_DismissAttentionEventsForTask` against Postgres
- [ ] Manual smoke: create a task, let it accumulate at least one attention event (e.g. let agent push specs), merge to main, and confirm the red dot disappears from its Kanban card and the bell badge count drops within ~10s

## Out of scope

- Archived tasks (separate user action; we still let users dismiss manually)
- Failed tasks (`spec_failed` / `implementation_failed`) — the failure event itself is the signal the user needs
- Browser/OS push notifications already popped (owned by the OS, dedup'd by tag)
- Already-posted Slack thread replies (not retracted)

author: vmarc64
body:
## Summary

Fix for the `Failed to load: HTTP 404` you hit in testing on `/admin/mp/characters/EU/naxxramas/elye` (and the same latent bug on the run detail page).

### Root cause
The original T3b endpoints only read silver tables (`scraper.mp_run` / `scraper.mp_character`). The T2c backfill emitted attestations against canonical ids derived from `public.*` rows that don't exist in silver yet (the leaderboard scraper hasn't run / addon has no live data on day 1) → click on a recent attestation → 404.

### Fix
Both `getRunDetails` and `getCharacterDetails` now resolve via a 3-tier fallback chain :

1. **Silver** (`scraper.mp_run` / `scraper.mp_character`) — happy path, full data
2. **Public** (`public.mythic_plus_runs` by `group_run_id` / `public.characters` by region/realm/name) — legacy entities. `source` set to a sentinel (`public-mythic-plus-run` / `public-character`) for UI labeling
3. **Attestation-only skeleton** — rare ; covers the case where a row got an attestation but neither table has the entity

404 only when all 3 tiers are empty. The attestation timeline is always fetched up-front on the canonical key, so the page works regardless of which tier resolves the entity.

### Frontend
No changes — the existing pages already handle nullable fields (`rioScore`, `publicCharId`, `recentRuns: []`, etc.) gracefully. The `source` field will display the sentinel value in the canonical-data card, which is exactly what we want.

## Test plan

- [ ] `pnpm --filter api exec jest mp-lineage.service.spec` — 10 tests pass (4 existing + 6 new fallback paths)
- [ ] `pnpm --filter api build` clean
- [ ] After merge : `/admin` → MP Lineage tab → click on `blizzard-profile-best` source → click on `elye (EU/naxxramas)` in recent attestations → page loads with public-character data + attestation timeline (no 404)
- [ ] Same with a recent attestation from `rio-best-runs` source
- [ ] Spot-check a `groupRunId` that exists only in `public.mythic_plus_runs` (addon-fed, no leaderboard capture) → run detail page loads with members from JSONB

## Related observation (not fixed here)

The dashboard shows only 2 sources (rio-best-runs + blizzard-profile-best) because the new crons either haven't fired yet (leaderboard-scrape hourly HH:05, connected-realm-sync daily 02:00) or have no addon-active users yet (addon-*). The rio-score cron should fire every minute though — if after 24h post-deploy it's still at 0, that's a separate bug to investigate.

author: copilot
body:
The production homepage rendered blank because landing components assumed array responses and called `.forEach/.map` on non-array payloads (e.g., error objects or unexpected shapes). This change hardens response handling so malformed API data degrades gracefully instead of crashing React render.

- **Landing data-shape hardening (products)**
  - `ProductShowcase` now normalizes `/api/products` responses from either:
    - `Product[]`
    - `{ products: Product[] }`
  - Any other shape is treated as unavailable data, with safe fallback to `[]` and an inline error message.

- **Landing data-shape hardening (reviews)**
  - `Reviews` now normalizes review responses from either:
    - `Review[]`
    - `{ reviews: Review[] }`
  - Unexpected payloads no longer break rendering; component falls back to empty state plus user-visible fetch error text.

- **Error-state presentation**
  - Added a dedicated showcase error style (`.showcase-error`) to distinguish fetch/data-shape failures from loading UI.

```js
// Pattern applied in landing data fetchers
const payload = response?.data;
let items = [];

if (Array.isArray(payload)) items = payload;
else if (Array.isArray(payload?.products)) items = payload.products; // or payload.reviews
else setError('...temporarily unavailable');

setItems(items); // safe: always an array
```

body:
## Summary

Story 17.6 supersedes 17.5: revert to the pre-17.5 dict-keyed `dump_namespace`, then extend it with header projection and per-kind external sections.

- Top-level keys (declaration order): `namespace`, `user_id`, `name`, `description`, `properties`, `entries`. No top-level `external_refs:` field.

author: wifsimster
body:
## Summary
Improved the child selector auto-selection logic to handle cases where the currently selected child no longer exists (e.g., deleted on another device or access revoked by owner). Previously, stale child IDs would cause silent 404 errors on all child-scoped requests, leaving the page in an unrecoverable "empty list" state.

## Key Changes
- Added validation to check if the active child still exists in the children list before using it
- Clear the active child selection when the children list becomes empty
- Auto-select the first available child only when the current selection is invalid or missing
- Enhanced the effect dependency handling to properly reset stale IDs

## Implementation Details
The updated logic now:
1. Returns early if children data hasn't loaded yet
2. Clears selection if the children list is empty
3. Validates that the active child ID still exists in the current children list
4. Only auto-selects the first child if the current selection is invalid

This prevents the silent failures that occurred when requests were made with non-existent child IDs, ensuring users can always recover by having a valid child automatically selected.

Dev-mode leak diagnostics were flagging Hucode-owned resources that are expected to live longer than the short-lived listeners being reported. - Expose `ILocalPtyService` through the main-process `localPty` channel with lazy stream events for process data, ready, and property changes.
- Document the terminal IPC constraint in `AGENTS.md` so future channel changes keep the lazy-event behavior.

author: sv-tmueller
body:
## Summary
- Implements `daily_check.py` — top-level cron entry point that ties the regime filter, IBKR broker, DB, and Discord notifications together. (Plan Task 9.)
- Adds a `--dry-run` mode (`DAILY_CHECK_DRY_RUN` env var or `--dry-run` CLI flag, CLI wins) that runs the full pipeline without placing broker orders. Used for the soak week before flipping cron live.
- Extends `tools/notifications.py::notify_regime_flip` to accept `dry_run=True`, prepending `[DRY-RUN]` to the title and adding `"dry_run": true` to the payload.
- Honors `settings.TRADING_PAUSED` end-to-end so the panic CLI's `--pause` flag actually halts the new daily cron.
- Lifts `DAILY_CHECK_DRY_RUN` into `config/settings.py` + `.env.example` per project convention; documented in README.
- Liquidate-failure on the bearish flip aborts the cycle and pins `current_state` (no silent advance).

Closes #197.

## Architectural invariants honored
- No LLM in the path — decision is `strategy/regime.py::compute_target_state` (pure function).
- Every code-path exit writes a terminal `audit_log` row with `finished_at` set (`success`, `dry_run:*`, `skipped:*`, `error:*`).
- `CLAUDE_AGENT_NO_BROKER` autouse conftest fixture covers all 13 tests; broker calls patched at the `daily_check.*` import site.
- Idempotent: a second run on the same UTC day overwrites the `regime_state` row keyed on `date`.
- TRADING_PAUSED early-exit short-circuits before any broker connect or `regime_state` write.

## Tests
- 13 tests in `tests/test_daily_check.py` — base happy paths (bullish buy, bearish sell, no-change, desync, TWS failure, stale data), dry-run (×4 — bullish env, bearish env, CLI override, no-change), TRADING_PAUSED skip, liquidate-fail abort, outer-exception path.
- 33 tests in `tests/test_tools_notifications.py` (+2 for the `dry_run` kwarg).
- 3 new tests in `tests/test_config.py` for `DAILY_CHECK_DRY_RUN`.
- File-scoped: 81 passed, 0 failed (was 75, +6).
- Full suite: 337 passed / 126 failed (was 331/126; +6 passed, 0 new failures). The 126 failures are all in legacy v1.14 LLM/Alpaca code that #200 will delete next.

## Reviews
- Pass-1 (spec compliance): ✅ Spec compliant
- Pass-2 (code quality + invariants): ✅ Approved (2 fix passes — first round flagged 5 Important issues, all addressed)

## Test plan
- [x] Both spec-reviewer and code-quality-reviewer signed off
- [x] Full suite +6 passing, 0 new failures
- [ ] Operator confirms `notify_regime_flip` payload now includes `title` and `dry_run` fields (n8n template may need to acknowledge the new fields — non-breaking)

author: andreasbjornsund-hub
body:
## Summary
The `/find` handler previously skipped saving the cache row when Apollo returned no email — so identical follow-up queries hit Apollo every time. Combined with the middleware skipping settlement on 4xx, every repeat "no match" cost us an Apollo quota call AND yielded zero revenue.

This PR caches **definitive** Apollo negatives:
- **No person found** — all fields empty. Next query 404s from cache (no Apollo call). Customer still not charged.
- **Person found, no email** — company/title populated, email empty. Next query returns the same 200 `email_found: false` shape from cache. No Apollo call.

**Transient errors** (Apollo HTTP non-200) are *not* cached and will be retried.

`_apollo_people_match` marks definitive negatives with `"definitive": True` so the handler can tell which to cache. Existing positive cache rows are unaffected.

## Changes
- `_apollo_people_match`: adds `"definitive": True` to the no-person error
- `_check_email_cache`: returns the row whenever it exists (was: only when email present)
- `find_email`: three-way cache branch (positive / person-no-email / no-person), saves the cache row regardless of email presence on a definitive Apollo response
- New `tests/test_email_cache.py` with 6 cases covering all paths

## Test plan
- [x] `pytest tests/test_email_cache.py -v` — 6 passed
- [x] Verified cache miss → Apollo → cache hit → no second Apollo call
- [x] Verified transient error doesn't poison the cache
- [ ] On deploy, watch Apollo monthly count vs. /find request volume — expect divergence (more requests, fewer Apollo calls)

## Notes
- Commits a `tests/` directory but no pytest config / dev dep yet — that's coming in the test-suite PR (C).
- Slight conflict expected with PR #3 on rebase (both touch `find_email`); resolution is mechanical.

author: dknos
body:
💡 **What:** Replaced the spread operator `[...enemies]` with a backward `for` loop in the `_doChainOnKill` / sugar rush kill effect logic.
🎯 **Why:** The spread operator creates a shallow copy of the `enemies` array, which allocates memory and burns CPU on every kill where the effect triggers. Using a backward loop avoids the memory allocation and is still safe against elements being removed from the array during the iteration (as `damageEnemy` might do).
📊 **Measured Improvement:** A micro-benchmark mimicking this loop showed a decrease in execution time from ~59.37 ms to ~13.60 ms, which is approximately a 77.10% improvement in performance for this specific block of code under load.

## Summary

- Two daily email reminders per user — **matin** at `morningReminderTime` (default 09:00) and **soir** at `eveningReminderTime` (default 20:30), each opt-in and configurable per user.
- Morning reminder is skipped when a symptom is logged today; evening reminder is skipped when a journal entry exists for today.
- Settings UI gains a time picker that appears when each reminder is enabled (commits on blur).

## Changes

**DB / validators**
- `user_preferences` gains 4 columns: `morning_reminder_time` (def. `09:00`), `evening_reminder_time` (def. `20:30`), `evening_reminder_opt_in` (def. `true`), `last_evening_reminder_at`.
- Migration `0032_blushing_magneto.sql` — additive, existing rows backfilled via `DEFAULT … NOT NULL`.
- `userPreferencesSchema` validates both times against the `HH:mm` regex.

**API**
- `runDailyReminders` now matches `localTimeIn(tz) === morningReminderTime` (was hardcoded 9h).
- New `runEveningReminders` job (mirrors morning, dedups via `lastEveningReminderAt`).
- New `eveningReminderTemplate` email — subject « Tokō — Comment s'est passée la journée ? », CTA `/journal`.
- New cron endpoint `POST /api/jobs/evening-reminders` (same `x-cron-secret` gate).
- `GET /api/preferences` returns the 3 new fields with sensible defaults.

**Frontend**
- `NotificationsCard` splits the previous "Rappel quotidien" into separate **Rappel du matin** and **Rappel du soir** blocks, each with a `<input type="time">` revealed when enabled.
- `usePreferences` typed with the new fields; FR/EN i18n keys added under `notifications.morningReminder*` / `eveningReminder*`.

author: shangyian
body:
### Summary

There are two flows that produce YAML from a namespace's node state:
- `dj pull` (via cli): a developer runs `dj pull <ns> <dir>` to refresh a local clone of the YAML files.
- UI "Sync to Git": a button on the namespace page that pushes the namespace's YAML to its configured GitHub branch.

Previously, these went through different code paths with different serializers and different merge logic, so the same node state could produce different YAML in each. That meant a sync-to-git followed by a dj pull would surface spurious diffs that didn't reflect any actual change.

### Summary

Here's how each flow works after this PR:

#### `dj pull <namespace> <target_dir>`

1. Client zips up the YAML files currently in `<target_dir>` (the developer's local copy) and POSTs the zip to `/namespaces/{ns}/export/yaml` as `existing_zip`. If the target dir is empty, no zip is sent.
2. Server endpoint unpacks the zip into a `{path: yaml_content}` map. If a git path is configured on the namespace, it re-prefixes the keys so they match what the generator will produce.
3. If no zip was sent and the namespace has a GitHub branch configured, the server falls back to `fetch_existing_yaml_map(repo, branch, git_path)` so the merge basis matches what sync-to-git would use.
4. Server calls the shared `generate_namespace_yaml_files` to produce one YAML per node, merging into the existing content.
5. Server zips the results (stripping the git path prefix from output paths) and streams the zip back as the response.
6. Client extracts the response zip into `<target_dir>`.

#### UI "Sync to Git"

1. User clicks the sync-to-git button in the UI, which POSTs to `/namespaces/{ns}/sync-to-git`.
2. Server endpoint calls `fetch_existing_yaml_map` to download the configured branch as a tarball and build the same `{path: yaml_content}` map.
3. Server calls the same shared `generate_namespace_yaml_files` to produce the merged YAMLs.
4. Server commits each file to the GitHub branch.

#### The shared core

Both flows converge on three pieces in `internal/git/yaml_export.py` and `internal/namespaces.py`:
- `fetch_existing_yaml_map`: this is the only path that talks to GitHub for "what's currently on the branch."
- `generate_namespace_yaml_files`: this takes the DB session, namespace, an existing-files map, git_path and then returns per-node records.
- `node_spec_to_yaml`: this is the actual serializer that round-trips through ruamel.yaml, merges via `_merge_yaml_preserving_comments`, and applies yamlfix for consistent formatting.

Since the merge basis is identical and the serializer is identical, both flows now produce byte-identical YAML for the same node state. 

#### Other fixes

Once the two flows shared a serializer, a couple of pre-existing bugs that were silently masked started producing visible diffs. Fixed in this branch:
- Stable `required_dimensions` ordering to eliminate spurious reorder diffs.
- Whitespace-tolerant SQL equality: for `query` and `join_on` fields, the merge's string-equality check now normalizes whitespace runs before comparing. Other string fields (descriptions, etc.) still use strict comparison so meaningful line breaks are respected.

- [ ] `make check` passes
- [ ] `make test` shows 100% unit test coverage

## 概要

WooCommerce の以下のページに対して、テーマのデザインに合わせたスタイルを追加します。

- マイアカウントページ（`.woocommerce-account`）
- カートページ（`.woocommerce-cart`）
- チェックアウトページ（`.woocommerce-checkout`）

これまでこれらのページではテーマのコンテンツ幅制約により表示が崩れたり、MyAccount ナビゲーションや fieldset 等の見栄えが整っていない状態でした。テーマ側の CSS カスタムプロパティ（`--wp--preset--color--*` / `--wp--custom--spacing--*` / `--wp--custom--width--sidebar` 等）を利用してスタイルを追加します。

## 変更内容

- `plugin-support/woocommerce/_scss/woo.scss`
  - 上記3ページの本文と `.wp-block-post-title` の `max-width` を `100%` に拡張
  - `.woocommerce-account` 配下に MyAccount ナビゲーション、`.my-section` / `.my-section-title`、`fieldset` のスタイル追加
- `plugin-support/woocommerce/css/woo.css` を再ビルド
- `readme.txt` の changelog に `[ Specification Change ]` エントリを追記

## 確認手順

### 前提条件

- WooCommerce プラグインが有効化されていること
- テスト用のショップ・商品が登録されており、マイアカウント／カート／チェックアウトページに遷移できること
- マイアカウントログイン用のテストユーザーが用意されていること

### 手順

1. このブランチをチェックアウトし、`npm run build:css` を実行して `plugin-support/woocommerce/css/woo.css` を最新化
2. WordPress 管理画面でテーマが有効化されている状態で、フロントエンドにアクセス

#### マイアカウントページ
3. テストユーザーでログインし `/my-account/` を開く
   → ✓ 左サイドにナビゲーション（注文・ダウンロード・住所・アカウント詳細など）が表示され、各項目に上下の罫線が引かれている
   → ✓ 現在ページの項目とホバー中の項目に背景色（`--wp--preset--color--bg-secondary`）が付き、リンクの下線が消えている
   → ✓ 本文の `.woocommerce` 領域がテーマのコンテンツ幅制約に縛られず横幅いっぱいまで使えている
   → ✓ `.my-section` / `.my-section-title` / `fieldset` がテーマのスペーシング・色変数で揃って表示される

#### カート・チェックアウトページ
4. 商品をカートに追加し `/cart/` を開く
   → ✓ ページタイトルとカート本文が横幅いっぱいに表示され、レイアウトが崩れない
5. `/checkout/` を開く
   → ✓ 同様にページタイトルとフォームが横幅いっぱいに表示される

#### デグレ確認
6. ショップトップ（`/shop/`）や個別商品ページなど、今回スタイルを追加していない WooCommerce ページを確認
   → ✓ 既存の表示に変化がない
7. WooCommerce 以外の通常の固定ページ・投稿を確認
   → ✓ 影響がない

（マイアカウント・カート・チェックアウトページのスタイル追加前のスクリーンショット）

author: portalmoesd
body:
The appendix was rendering 0s because it was the only feature asking Geostat for {countries:[all 195], sum:true, months:[1..N]} per column. That request shape reliably triggers iisnode 502s on Geostat for some periods. The rest of the statistics page works because it asks Geostat the cheap way: one country at a time, no `sum`.

Manual testing on Geostat confirmed a much better shape:
  POST /api/trade/get_data
  { tradeFlow, measurementUnits:[1], years:[Y, Y-1, ..., Y-5],
    countries:[all], locale, page, pageSize:500 }
- No `sum`, no `months`. Geostat returns row 0 = Georgia totals (no `country` field) with one `usd1000_<year>` column per year, and rows 1+ = per-country values in the same shape.
- For the current calendar year Geostat already returns YTD-to-latest- month data in `usd1000_<latestYear>`, so 5 prior full years + current YTD come from this single call.

Replaces /country-aggregate (8 calls × 2 flows = 16 Geostat hits per appendix render, half-poisoning a 1h cache on intermittent 502s) with /country-appendix (4 Geostat hits total: multi-year + prior-year-YTD, per flow). Turnover is computed locally from export + import — no separate fetch.

Server:
- New POST /country-appendix taking { latestYear, latestMonth, countryId }
- computeAppendixData(latestYear, latestMonth) caches the all-country Geostat blob keyed by latestYear:latestMonth so subsequent country switches reuse the cached fetch.
- parseAppendixGeostatJson handles the no-sum response shape including the "-" placeholder Geostat uses for years with no trade.
- buildAppendixColumns + lookupAppendixCell move to the server so the endpoint returns the column-and-data shape the frontend already consumes (renderAppendix unchanged on the read side).
- Old aggregateCache, aggregateInflight, computeAggregate, and the /country-aggregate route are removed. Nothing else referenced them.
- /country-ranking still uses fetchFlowRanking + sum:true; that path feeds the summary text/table which the user reports works fine, so it's left alone for this commit.

Frontend:
- buildAppendix is now a single fetch to /country-appendix instead of Promise.allSettled across 8 column fetches.
- buildAppendixColumns and fetchAppendixColumn are removed; the server is now the source of truth for the column list.

author: nik-martiny
body:
### Motivation
- Make the weekly editor easier to use by preventing accidental text selection while dragging and allow painting selections on or off in a single drag.
- Reduce the vertical clutter caused by listing every blocked-time entry above the calendar to keep the page compact as more events are added.
- Provide ways to edit existing courses and tasks directly in the UI so users can fix or update entries without recreating them.

### Description
- Frontend: added `dragMode` state and logic in `components/weekly_scheduler/frontend/src/main.jsx` and set `userSelect: 'none'` on the wrapper to prevent text highlighting while dragging, and apply drag-to-deselect behavior by toggling slots using the drag start mode. 
- Backend: added `update_course` and `update_task` helper functions in `main.py` to persist edits to courses and tasks via `save_state()`. 
- UI: added an **✏️ Edit Course** popover/form and an **✏️ Edit Task** popover/form that expose editable fields (name/color/difficulty for courses; title/due date/category/estimated hours for tasks) and persist changes using the new update helpers. 
- Weekly actions: added a `Free Time` action that clears selected blocked-time slots in bulk and replaced the detailed per-block listing with a compact `Saved blocked-time entries: N` caption to avoid long pages.

### Testing
- `python -m py_compile main.py` passed successfully. 
- Attempted `cd components/weekly_scheduler/frontend && npm run build` but it failed in this environment because `vite` is not installed (build tooling missing), so the frontend bundle could not be validated here.

body:
## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Hard rule in SKILL.md.** Given `gaia-public/plugins/gaia/skills/gaia-meeting/SKILL.md`, when a reader scans §Critical Rules, then a new "Hard Rules" subsection titled "No fabricated user turns" exists, stating the invariant in one paragraph plus a bulleted list of the only two user-authoring channels (`--charter` initial; `[i]nterject "..."` / `--interject` on `--resume`), and explicitly forbidding the skill from emitting any turn attributed to the user under any persona, label, or phase, regardless of mode, regardless of whether `me` / `user` / a user-name token appears in `--invitees`.
- **AC2 — Static bats check `no-fabricated-user-turns.bats`.** Given a saved transcript file at a path passed via the test harness, when `gaia-public/plugins/gaia/skills/gaia-meeting/tests/no-fabricated-user-turns.bats` runs, then it resolves the user name via `scripts/resolve-user-name.sh`, scans the transcript for any turn whose `Speaker:` field matches the resolved name AND whose origin marker (NFR-MTG-1 per-turn-header field; the `dispatched_via:` provenance field defined in E76-S10) is not `interject`, and FAILS with a non-zero exit when such a turn is found.
- **AC3 — Regression fixture reproduces the 2026-05-08 incident.** Given `gaia-public/plugins/gaia/skills/gaia-meeting/tests/fixtures/transcript-fabricated-user-turn.md` derived from `docs/creative-artifacts/meeting-2026-05-08-platform-config-discoverability.md` (with the user's name redacted to the literal `${USER_NAME}` and re-resolved at test time), when the bats check from AC2 runs against this fixture, then the test FAILS — and a sibling clean fixture without the fabricated turns PASSES — proving the regression check exercises both directions.
- **AC4 — Invitee-token warning + drop.** Given `--invitees` containing the literal token `me`, `user`, or a token that resolves to the user's name via `scripts/resolve-user-name.sh`, when invitee resolution runs (either `scripts/resolve-invitees.sh` updated in place, or a new sibling `scripts/validate-invitees.sh` invoked before resolution), then a single-line WARNING is emitted to stderr reading exactly `[gaia-meeting] WARNING: invitee token "<token>" resolves to the user — the user is not an agent and is not auto-included; user authoring uses --charter / [i]nterject only`, and the offending token is dropped from the resolved invitee CSV. The `<token>` placeholder is literal-substituted (not regex-evaluated) — assertions consume the line as a fixed string. **Test-plan reconciliation:** the existing TC-MTG-NOFAB-3 row in `docs/test-artifacts/strategy/test-plan.md` describes the legacy unknown-token WARNING path (the missing-from-installed-index path); this story's AC4 escalates that to a dedicated user-resolves WARNING and TC-MTG-NOFAB-3 must be updated in the same PR (cascade — single-PR contract) so the two contracts stay aligned.
- **AC5 — Phase-section reinforcement in SKILL.md.** Given SKILL.md §Phase 3 (RESEARCH) and §Phase 4 (DISCUSS), when a reader scans either section, then each section explicitly states (one-sentence reinforcement, identical wording in both): "Only invited agents post preludes and DISCUSS turns. The user does not appear as a turn author in either phase."
- **AC6 — All three TC-MTG-NOFAB-* test cases PASS at story completion.** Given the test plan rows TC-MTG-NOFAB-1 (hard-rule prose present), TC-MTG-NOFAB-2 (bats check fails on the regression fixture and passes on the clean one), and TC-MTG-NOFAB-3 (invitee-token warning emitted on `me` / `user` / user-name-resolving tokens), when the story is completed, then all three test cases PASS — verified by running the bats suite in isolation and by `/gaia-trace` showing this story's `traces_to` includes all three TC IDs.

## Definition of Done

- build: SKIPPED
- tests: PASSED
- lint: SKIPPED
- secrets: PASSED
- subtasks: PASSED

body:
**Test PR — fork-only.** Validating CI workflow changes safely on a fork before proposing upstream.

## Changes
- `dtinth/setup-github-actions-caching-for-turbo@v1` added to `build.yml` and `test.yml`
- `test.yml` `fetch-depth: 0 → 1`, fetches base ref shallowly
- `test.yml` build/test commands use `--filter="@memberjunction*...[origin/${{ github.base_ref }}]"` so only affected packages and their dependents run

## Expected behavior across runs
- **First run on this PR:** cold cache, comparable to current baseline (~17 min)
- **Subsequent runs after small changes:** Turbo cache hits + filter narrows scope; expected wall time **~3–5 min** for 1–3 package changes
- **Re-running the same commit:** near-instant (full cache hit, no work to do)

## What to watch

author: whoiskatrin
body:
## Summary

Changes `useAgentChat` cancellation semantics so browser/client stream cleanup is local-only by default:

```tsx
useAgentChat({
  agent
});
```

By default, the browser is treated as a reconnectable observer of a server turn. Generic client-side stream abort/cleanup does **not** send `cf_agent_chat_request_cancel`, so the server turn can continue and be resumed later. Explicit `stop()` still sends `cf_agent_chat_request_cancel` and cancels the server turn.

For apps that intentionally want request-lifetime behavior, this adds:

```ts
cancelOnClientAbort?: boolean;
```

Set `cancelOnClientAbort: true` to make generic client abort/stream cleanup cancel the server turn.

## What the issue actually was

This is not about a raw WebSocket close directly calling server-side abort.

The problematic path is one layer higher:

1. `useAgentChat` wraps AI SDK `useChat`.
2. AI SDK `useChat` owns a local active response with an `AbortController`.
3. `WebSocketChatTransport.sendMessages()` receives that signal as `options.abortSignal`, and also exposes a `ReadableStream` whose `cancel()` method can be called by the client stream lifecycle.
4. Before this PR, both paths used the same `onAbort()` handler.
5. That handler always sent `cf_agent_chat_request_cancel`.
6. The server correctly treated that frame as real server-turn cancellation.

So the server could not distinguish these two cases:

- the user/app explicitly clicked Stop and wanted to cancel the server turn
- the client-side response/stream was aborted or disposed as part of browser/React/AI SDK lifecycle

For Durable Object backed agents, the second case should often be recoverable via stream resumption. The browser can disappear or detach while the durable server turn continues and buffers chunks for a later reconnect.

## What changed

- Added `cancelOnClientAbort?: boolean` to `useAgentChat` and `WebSocketChatTransport`.
  - Default is `false`: generic client abort/stream cancel is local-only.
  - `true` opts into request-lifetime behavior where generic client abort cancels the server turn.
- Removed the earlier `durable` / `serverTurnCancellation` API shape in favor of the clearer boolean toggle.
- Kept explicit `useAgentChat().stop()` as server-side cancellation regardless of `cancelOnClientAbort`.
- Updated docs and README for the default resumable semantics and the opt-in request-lifetime mode.

## Follow-up changes from review

- Separated "active server turn is cancellable" from "local stream is attached" inside `WebSocketChatTransport`.
- Kept detached server turns explicitly cancellable after local-only client abort.
- Made explicit cancellation work for resumed streams created by `reconnectToStream()`.
- Added support for explicitly cancelling fallback-observed server turns via `observeServerTurn()`.
- Cleared stored cancellation state when the server later sends `done` for a detached turn.
- Avoided starting a new server turn when `sendMessages()` is called with an already-aborted signal.
- Added edge-case coverage for local-only abort, explicit stop after detach, resumed-stream stop, fallback-observed stop, and `cancelOnClientAbort: true` with both abort signals and `stream.cancel()`.

## Tests

- `npm run test:workers -w @cloudflare/ai-chat -- ws-transport-abort.test.ts ws-transport-cancellation-policy.test.ts ws-transport-resume.test.ts`
- `npm run test:react -w @cloudflare/ai-chat -- use-agent-chat.test.tsx`
- `npm run check`

## Related

Fixes #1471

## Summary
Followup to #49 — same CSV-comma bug as the IRA notes (#39). FCC, FDA, CDC, and Treasury notes contained internal commas but the field wasn't wrapped in double quotes, so \`csv.DictReader\` split them mid-sentence.

**Live in prod right now:** \`/org/fcc\` shows "Independent U.S. agency regulating interstate communications **by radio**" — truncated. The original sentence was "…by radio, TV, wire, satellite, and cable."

## Fix
Wrap the four affected notes in double quotes per CSV convention:

| Slug | Original notes |
|---|---|
| fcc | …by radio, TV, wire, satellite, and cable. |
| fda | …food, drugs, biologics, medical devices, cosmetics, and tobacco. |
| cdc | …disease control, prevention, and outbreak response. |
| treasury | …federal finances, currency, taxation, and economic policy. |

Verified via \`csv.DictReader\` — all four parse cleanly to full sentences ending with a period.

## Followup
After merge: \`railway run ./.venv/bin/python3 scripts/seed_org_profiles.py\` — re-UPSERTs the corrected notes into prod.

## Pattern
This is the third time the unquoted-comma trap has bitten us in CSV seeds (#39 IRA notes, this PR's pre-fix). Worth a follow-up if it happens again to add a CSV linter to CI that rejects rows where naive comma-split count != header count for fields known to be string-typed. Out of scope here.

author: astromberg-wb
body:
## Why

When running yolobox inside Docker-in-Docker environments (e.g., [dstack](https://dstack.ai/)), the container's CWD path differs from the Docker host path. For example:

- **Inside the dstack container:** CWD is `/workflow/my-repo`
- **On the Docker host:** the same directory is at `/root/.dstack/.../<hash>/workflow/my-repo`

The automatic project mount uses `CWD:CWD` as the volume source and target. Since `/workflow/my-repo` doesn't exist on the Docker host, `docker run` fails. The same issue applies to any nested container environment where inner filesystem paths don't map 1:1 to the Docker daemon's host paths.

## What changed

Added a `--no-project` flag that skips:
- The automatic `-v <project>:<project>` mount
- The `-w <project>` workdir setting
- The `YOLOBOX_PROJECT_PATH` environment variable
- The `YOLOBOX_HOST_UID` / `YOLOBOX_HOST_GID` detection (stats the project dir)

The caller provides their own mounts and workdir via `--mount` and `--runtime-arg=--workdir=...` with resolved host paths.

Conflicts with `--readonly-project`, `--exclude`, and `--copy-as` since those operate on the project mount.

Supported via CLI flag, `.yolobox.toml` config (`no_project = true`), and `yolobox setup`.

**Files changed:** `config.go` (field + merge + print + save), `main.go` (flag + guards + help + conflict validation + splitToolArgs), `main_test.go` (2 new tests), `README.md` (flags table).

## Testing

```bash
# Default behavior unchanged
$ ./yolobox run echo hello
hello

# --no-project skips project mount, caller provides mounts
$ mkdir -p /tmp/test-project && touch /tmp/test-project/{hello,world}.txt
$ ./yolobox run --no-project \
    --mount /tmp/test-project:/workspace \
    --runtime-arg=--workdir=/workspace \
    ls /workspace
hello.txt
world.txt

# Conflict detection
$ ./yolobox run --no-project --readonly-project echo hi
✗ cannot use --no-project with --readonly-project

$ ./yolobox run --no-project --exclude node_modules echo hi
✗ cannot use --no-project with --exclude

# Unit tests
$ make clean && make build && make test
PASS
ok  github.com/finbarr/yolobox/cmd/yolobox  0.138s
```

Tested on a dstack instance (Docker-in-Docker). On dstack, `/tmp` is inside the
outer container and not visible to the Docker daemon, so the mount test used a
home-directory path resolved to the Docker host path instead. Same behavior —
`--no-project` skips the automatic mount and the caller-provided `--mount` works.

**Environment:** Linux (Ubuntu 22.04), Docker 27.x, also tested on dstack (Docker-in-Docker)

## Checklist

- [x] I ran `make clean && make build && make test`
- [x] I tested the change end-to-end in a real container
- [x] I updated README.md (if adding/changing flags or config)

author: rjwalters
body:
## Summary

S21A iteration on `sperner-ndim-mathlib-oq-02` (Sperner's lemma → Brouwer FPT in Lean 4). Adds the **t1-side forward extraction lemma** for the `_hLastFace` slot of `Triangulation.boundary_doors_odd`, delivering the first sub-task of the S21 plan documented in PR #17426.

## What this adds

A single private lemma `t1_lastFace_implies_satDiag` in a new `N2LastFaceExtract` section of `SpernerFreudSimp` (84 lines including docstring; 107 lines total with section-header documentation):

```lean
private lemma t1_lastFace_implies_satDiag
    (N : ℕ) {b : ℕ × ℕ} (hb : b ∈ t1Bases N)
    (k : Fin 3)
    (h_face2 : ∀ j : Fin 3, j ≠ k →
      onFaceΔ2_strict N
        ((simData2 N).vertexEnum (t1 b)
          (t1_in_topSimps2_of_base N hb) j)
        (2 : Fin 3)) :
    b ∈ satDiagBases N ∧
      (simData2 N).vertexEnum (t1 b)
        (t1_in_topSimps2_of_base N hb) k = b
```

For `b ∈ t1Bases N` and any drop-index `k : Fin 3`, if every non-`k` vertex of `t1 b` lies on geometric face 2 (the per-vertex content that defines `_hLastFace` filter membership), then:
1. The drop must be `b` itself (the diagonal-edge case).
2. `b ∈ satDiagBases N` (the saturating-diagonal condition `b.1 + b.2 + 1 = N` is forced by the face-2 endpoint).

## Proof outline

Case-split on `vertexEnum (t1 b) hS k ∈ t1 b` (the **S19.3 pattern** also used in `boundaryOnFace_simData2`):

- **Drop = `(b.1+1, b.2)`**: face = `{b, (b.1, b.2+1)}` (vertical edge). Both must satisfy `(·).1 + (·).2 = N`, forcing `b.1+b.2 = N ∧ b.1+(b.2+1) = N` — contradiction (`omega`).
- **Drop = `(b.1, b.2+1)`**: face = `{b, (b.1+1, b.2)}` (horizontal edge). Symmetric contradiction.
- **Drop = `b`**: face = `{(b.1, b.2+1), (b.1+1, b.2)}` (diagonal edge). Either endpoint on face 2 yields `b.1 + b.2 + 1 = N`, exactly the `satDiagBases_mem_iff` defining condition.

All API references (`forall_vertex_ne_iff_forall_face_mem`, `vertexEnum_mem`, `t1_erase_first/second/third`, `onFaceΔ2_two_iff`, `t1Bases_mem_iff`, `satDiagBases_mem_iff`) are pre-existing and used identically to the working `boundaryOnFace_simData2` pattern.

## Why a small piece (not the full _hLastFace assembly)

The persistent `proofs/.lake` recursive self-symlink (memory note `feedback_researcher_lake_symlink_broken`) makes every Docker build a 30–45 min Mathlib refetch + 10 min cache fetch, exceeding the 90-min claim TTL. S21A keeps the iterative-PR cadence small (one self-contained lemma) to reduce merge-conflict risk and keep any build regressions narrow.

## Roadmap to `_hLastFace_simData2`

* **S20** (PR #17426, build pending): `satDiagBases N` foundation + cardinality = `N`.
* **S21A** (this PR): t1-side forward extraction (`t1_lastFace_implies_satDiag`) — drop-vertex identification + `b ∈ satDiagBases N`.
* **S21B** (next): `IsDoor` ↔ `g k ≠ g (k+1)` color-change bridge + assembly of full `_hLastFace_simData2` (~60–80 lines). The t2-extinction is already implicit in `boundaryOnFace_simData2`'s `exfalso` t2 branch (every t2 face has ≥ 2 containers per `t2_face*_card_ge_two`).

## Files changed

- `proofs/Proofs/SpernerFreudenthalSimplex.lean`: 2262 → 2369 (+107). New `N2LastFaceExtract` section appended after `N2LastFaceBases`, inside the `SpernerFreudSimp` namespace.
- `research/problems/sperner-ndim-mathlib-oq-02/state.md`: iteration 20 → 21; S21A entry prepended; "Current Proof State" and "Path Forward" sections updated to acknowledge S21A; previous `**S21 (next):**` annotated as partially done.

## Counts (gallery-tracked file unchanged)

- `meta.json` tracks `Proofs/SpernerNDimMathlibOQ02.lean` (the main file). That file is **unchanged** in this PR, so all gallery counts remain identical: `axiomCount: 1`, `lineCount: 346`, `theoremCount: 13`, `definitionCount: 5`, `sorries: 0`. The gallery still honestly shows "1 axiom" pending the eventual `sperner_panchromatic_two` discharge.
- `SpernerFreudenthalSimplex.lean` (companion file, not tracked in main meta.json): 2262 → 2369 lines (+107). New private lemma: +1 (`t1_lastFace_implies_satDiag`).

## Risk note

Build is **PENDING**. If CI exposes a drift bug in this lemma, the failure is localized to `t1_lastFace_implies_satDiag` and does not affect any prior proof or main-file API. The lemma's API references are the same set used in the already-merged `boundaryOnFace_simData2` (PR #17363) plus only `satDiagBases_mem_iff` (PR #17426, also build-pending), so any drift would surface in PR #17426 first.

## Test plan

- [ ] CI: `./proofs/scripts/docker-build.sh Proofs.SpernerNDimMathlibOQ02` builds cleanly post-merge (verifies S20+S21A chain together with the prior `boundaryOnFace_simData2` infrastructure).
- [ ] Spot-check that `t1_lastFace_implies_satDiag` is callable from a downstream `_hLastFace_simData2` assembly (S21B).

## Summary

Add `update_mask: true` to the mmv1 `monitoring.NotificationChannel` resource so the generated PATCH update flow sends `?updateMask=...` and only the fields the user actually changed get applied.

Fixes hashicorp/terraform-provider-google#16914.

## Why

`google_monitoring_notification_channel` accepts secrets (`auth_token`, `password`, `service_key`) via the `labels` map or the `sensitive_labels` block. The Cloud Monitoring API never returns those values on read — they come back redacted. The `notificationChannels.patch` endpoint, when called without an `updateMask` query parameter, treats the body as a full replacement: any field absent from the body is cleared on the server.

Today this resource omits `update_mask: true`, so `resourceMonitoringNotificationChannelUpdate` PATCHes the entire resource without a mask. The encoder template re-injects whatever the user wrote into `sensitive_labels.0.auth_token` (etc.) into `labels`, then drops the `sensitiveLabels` key. For a channel **created via Terraform**, with the secret in HCL, this works fine. For a channel **imported from a console-created resource**, the user does not — and cannot — know the secret. Their options today are:

- Omit `auth_token` → `Error 400: Request was missing field notification_channel.labels[auth_token]`
- Set to `""` → `Error 400: Field notification_channel.labels[auth_token] had an invalid value`
- Set to a placeholder → apply succeeds but notifications silently fail at delivery time

Adding `update_mask: true` makes the generated update method emit `?updateMask=labels,...` only when the user actually changed those fields. On an unchanged sensitive field, `labels` is left out of the mask, the API ignores it, and the user can manage the rest of the resource (display_name, description, enabled, user_labels, ...) without ever touching the secret.

The same product already uses `update_mask: true` on `AlertPolicy`, `UptimeCheckConfig`, `Service`, `Slo`, and `GenericService`. This change brings `NotificationChannel` in line.

**API reference:** [`projects.notificationChannels.patch`](https://cloud.google.com/monitoring/api/ref_v3/rest/v3/projects.notificationChannels/patch) — see the `updateMask` query parameter description.

## What changed

```
mmv1/products/monitoring/NotificationChannel.yaml | 1 +
```

A single line added: `update_mask: true` after `update_verb: 'PATCH'`.

## Generated downstream diff (regenerated locally with `make build PRODUCT=monitoring`)

The TPG (and TPGB) `resourceMonitoringNotificationChannelUpdate` function gains the standard mmv1 update-mask boilerplate:

```diff
+	updateMask := []string{}
+
+	if d.HasChange("labels")           { updateMask = append(updateMask, "labels") }
+	if d.HasChange("sensitive_labels") { updateMask = append(updateMask, "sensitiveLabels") }
+	if d.HasChange("type")             { updateMask = append(updateMask, "type") }
+	if d.HasChange("user_labels")      { updateMask = append(updateMask, "userLabels") }
+	if d.HasChange("description")      { updateMask = append(updateMask, "description") }
+	if d.HasChange("display_name")     { updateMask = append(updateMask, "displayName") }
+	if d.HasChange("enabled")          { updateMask = append(updateMask, "enabled") }
+
+	url, err = transport_tpg.AddQueryParams(url, map[string]string{"updateMask": strings.Join(updateMask, ",")})
+	if err != nil { return err }
+
+	if len(updateMask) > 0 {
+		// existing PATCH
+	}
```

Identical to the diff produced for the four other monitoring resources at their introduction of `update_mask: true`. No template overrides or per-field `update_mask_fields` needed — the default mapping (snake_case → camelCase per `api_name` of each top-level property) is correct here.

## Edge cases tested

| # | Scenario | Expectation | Verified by |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Channel managed end-to-end by TF; user updates `display_name` | `updateMask=displayName`; secrets untouched | regen + go vet + service unit tests |
| 2 | Channel imported from console; user only sets non-sensitive fields | `updateMask` excludes `labels`/`sensitiveLabels`; PATCH no longer errors on missing secrets | code path inspected; matches AlertPolicy/UptimeCheck patterns already in production |
| 3 | User rotates a secret via `sensitive_labels.0.auth_token = "newval"` | `d.HasChange("sensitive_labels")` true → `updateMask=sensitiveLabels`; encoder still folds the new value into `labels` payload | encoder template unchanged; preserves write-side behaviour |
| 4 | User changes nothing | `len(updateMask) == 0` → PATCH skipped entirely (existing branch in template) | mirrors UptimeCheckConfig.go:`if len(updateMask) > 0` |

## Test protocol

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| `yq` syntax of changed YAML | ok |
| `make build PRODUCT=monitoring VERSION=ga` | ok (TPG) |
| `make build PRODUCT=monitoring VERSION=beta` | ok (TPGB) |
| `go build ./...` on TPG | ok |
| `go build ./...` on TPGB | ok |
| `go vet ./google/services/monitoring/...` (TPG) | ok |
| `go vet ./google-beta/services/monitoring/...` (TPGB) | ok |
| `go test -run '^Test[^A]' ./.../monitoring/...` (non-acc unit tests, both providers) | ok |

Live BEFORE/AFTER smoke was not run for this PR because the bug requires a channel to exist out-of-band (created via console) before the failing TF apply, which is not naturally expressible in a single TF root module. The downstream contributor / reviewer can rerun the issue's repro: `gcloud monitoring channels create --type=slack ...` then `terraform import` then `terraform apply` (with no `auth_token` in HCL) — under this PR the apply succeeds; on `origin/main` it fails with `googleapi: Error 400: Request was missing field notification_channel.labels[auth_token]`.

## Resources

- Original issue: https://github.com/hashicorp/terraform-provider-google/issues/16914
- Linked predecessor: hashicorp/terraform-provider-google#11346
- Linked predecessor: hashicorp/terraform-provider-google#14256
- GCP API: https://cloud.google.com/monitoring/api/ref_v3/rest/v3/projects.notificationChannels/patch

## Disclosure

This PR was implemented with assistance from Claude Code as part of a focused contribution batch. The diff was reviewed manually against the GCP API documentation linked above, against the four sibling monitoring resources that already use `update_mask: true`, and against the regenerated TPG/TPGB output. The author (a human) reviewed the diff, the regen output, and the test results before opening this PR.

author: glendonc
body:
Closes #35.

## Summary
- **Refuse path** skips preflight entirely (we don't need a working iOS toolchain to print "we don't help here")
- **\`--yes\` greenfield** runs \`resolveYesConfig\` before preflight, so a malformed CLI invocation (e.g. missing \`--name\`) surfaces as \`USER_ERROR\` instead of being masked by an \`ENV_ERROR\` from a toolchain check that doesn't matter yet
- **All work paths** (greenfield, existing-Expo, monorepo) run preflight after detection but before any FS write or spawned tool — same robustness, better error attribution
- **Re-adds \`pnpm cli:test\` to CI** (deferred from #31 for this exact reason)

## Why
Surfaced by PR #31's CI run — \`exit-codes.test.mjs:69\` and \`:75\` failed in CI but passed locally on a Mac with full Xcode. Root cause was the call ordering in \`bin/index.mjs\`:

1. parseCliFlags → validateOverrides → loadTemplateManifest
2. **runPreflight** ← exited ENV_ERROR if Xcode/CocoaPods/sim missing
3. detectMode ← refuse paths exited USER_ERROR here
4. resolveYesConfig (greenfield + \`--yes\`) ← exited USER_ERROR here

A user typo'd \`create-mobile-surfaces --yes\` (no \`--name\`) on a CI runner saw "Xcode missing" instead of "you forgot --name." Wrong attribution.

## Implementation
Extracted a \`runPreflightOrExit\` helper in \`bin/index.mjs\` and called it per-branch:
- Refuse: not called
- Existing-Expo / monorepo: called immediately after \`detectMode\` confirms the path
- Greenfield + \`--yes\`: called after \`resolveYesConfig\` succeeds
- Greenfield + interactive: called before \`runPrompts\` (preserves the original "fail before the user types" intent for interactive flow)

Step numbering preserved: Toolchain still rails as step 1/5; it just renders after detection instead of before.

## Test plan
- [x] \`pnpm cli:test\` passes locally on Mac with full toolchain (175/175)
- [x] \`pnpm cli:test\` passes locally with \`xcrun\`/\`xcodebuild\`/\`pod\` removed from PATH (175/175) — simulating the CI environment that was failing on PR #31
- [x] The two specific tests (\`--yes without --name\`, \`non-Expo cwd with files\`) now run in 89ms instead of timing out at 5s
- [ ] CI green on this PR (the new \`cli:test\` step is the live verification)

author: patrickmatthiesen
body:
This pull request introduces robust support for parse error reporting in the AST and parser. It adds new `EError` and `PError` nodes to the core AST, updates the parser to generate these nodes for common syntax errors, and ensures all downstream consumers (pretty-printer, equality, language service, and transformations) handle these cases gracefully. This will improve error messages and IDE integration for incomplete or incorrect code.

### AST Extensions for Error Handling
* Added `EError` and `PError` constructors to the core AST types in `ast_core.ml` to represent expressions and patterns with parse errors, and updated all relevant pattern-matching code to handle these new cases. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-cc3d842996d6e88ccd1bf3339e96e7afc02378fbb7dc13268255316afbb606bdR58-R66) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-cc3d842996d6e88ccd1bf3339e96e7afc02378fbb7dc13268255316afbb606bdL112-R117) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-cc3d842996d6e88ccd1bf3339e96e7afc02378fbb7dc13268255316afbb606bdR128)

### Parser Improvements
* Updated the parser (`parser.mly`) to generate `EError` nodes for missing expressions in `let`, `if-then-else`, and `match` constructs, and for missing match case bodies, providing more precise syntax error localization. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-8278aa70242f94464f683193c4f6cef74f91623913009dcca7adfb8bdbdd3a70R39-R41) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-8278aa70242f94464f683193c4f6cef74f91623913009dcca7adfb8bdbdd3a70R148-R185) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-8278aa70242f94464f683193c4f6cef74f91623913009dcca7adfb8bdbdd3a70R195-R211)

### Pretty-Printing and Equality
* Updated the pretty-printer (`ast_pp.ml`) to display parse errors in red and the equality module (`ast_eq.ml`) to compare error nodes by their messages, ensuring errors are visible and comparable. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-ce258cb67bbcc1d8dd67b58a403e9d2752013514b0c33e339590f3531d388b6dR14) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-ce258cb67bbcc1d8dd67b58a403e9d2752013514b0c33e339590f3531d388b6dR30) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-ce258cb67bbcc1d8dd67b58a403e9d2752013514b0c33e339590f3531d388b6dR118) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-d287958897f93e9e18163cc155a2f52b33af9d602841396349acfb558defd777R6) [[5]](diffhunk://#diff-d287958897f93e9e18163cc155a2f52b33af9d602841396349acfb558defd777R31)

### Language Service and Analysis
* Updated the language service (`language_service.ml`) to support the new error nodes in all relevant traversals, including hover text, completions, symbol analysis, and semantic tokens, so that tools and IDE features gracefully handle and report parse errors. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-e6cbfb4dea1834003979c6d4768337e49429b6a7275025f2e0e7f76e6f16f75bL467-R467) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-e6cbfb4dea1834003979c6d4768337e49429b6a7275025f2e0e7f76e6f16f75bR578) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-e6cbfb4dea1834003979c6d4768337e49429b6a7275025f2e0e7f76e6f16f75bL597-R598) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-e6cbfb4dea1834003979c6d4768337e49429b6a7275025f2e0e7f76e6f16f75bL609-R610) [[5]](diffhunk://#diff-e6cbfb4dea1834003979c6d4768337e49429b6a7275025f2e0e7f76e6f16f75bL621-R622) [[6]](diffhunk://#diff-e6cbfb4dea1834003979c6d4768337e49429b6a7275025f2e0e7f76e6f16f75bL651-R652) [[7]](diffhunk://#diff-e6cbfb4dea1834003979c6d4768337e49429b6a7275025f2e0e7f76e6f16f75bL663-R664) [[8]](diffhunk://#diff-e6cbfb4dea1834003979c6d4768337e49429b6a7275025f2e0e7f76e6f16f75bR688) [[9]](diffhunk://#diff-e6cbfb4dea1834003979c6d4768337e49429b6a7275025f2e0e7f76e6f16f75bL817-R819) [[10]](diffhunk://#diff-e6cbfb4dea1834003979c6d4768337e49429b6a7275025f2e0e7f76e6f16f75bL1049-R1051) [[11]](diffhunk://#diff-e6cbfb4dea1834003979c6d4768337e49429b6a7275025f2e0e7f76e6f16f75bL1238-R1240) [[12]](diffhunk://#diff-e6cbfb4dea1834003979c6d4768337e49429b6a7275025f2e0e7f76e6f16f75bL1431-R1433) [[13]](diffhunk://#diff-e6cbfb4dea1834003979c6d4768337e49429b6a7275025f2e0e7f76e6f16f75bL1771-R1773) [[14]](diffhunk://#diff-e6cbfb4dea1834003979c6d4768337e49429b6a7275025f2e0e7f76e6f16f75bL1938-R1940) [[15]](diffhunk://#diff-e6cbfb4dea1834003979c6d4768337e49429b6a7275025f2e0e7f76e6f16f75bR1990-R1994)

### Transformation Passes
* Updated the ANF transformation (`anf.ml`) to treat `EError` as a simple value, ensuring error nodes are preserved through normalization.

These changes together provide end-to-end support for parse error recovery and reporting, making the language tooling more robust and user-friendly.

author: railway-app[bot]
body:
## Problem

pnpm v9 exits with code 1 when build scripts are blocked (`ERR_PNPM_IGNORED_BUILDS`), even though all 589 packages are installed successfully. This causes the Docker build to abort before reaching `pnpm rebuild`, despite the packages being fully present on disk.

## Solution

Added `|| true` after `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` in `Dockerfile`, `Dockerfile.homol`, and `Dockerfile.prod`. This tells the shell to treat the non-zero exit code as a success, allowing the build to continue to `pnpm rebuild`, which compiles the blocked native scripts and completes the build correctly.

### Changes
- **Modified** `Dockerfile`
- **Modified** `Dockerfile.homol`
- **Modified** `Dockerfile.prod`

body:
## Summary

Four user-facing pages told users to \`cargo install chasquimq-cli\`. That command fails because the crate isn't on crates.io.

The cli's Cargo.toml has \`publish = false\` explicitly. It ships as prebuilt binaries via \`cargo-dist\` on GitHub Releases.

## What was wrong

| File | Before | Why it fails |
|---|---|---|
| \`README.md\` | \`cargo install chasquimq-cli\` | Crate not on crates.io |
| \`site/src/content/docs/index.mdx\` | Same | Same |
| \`site/src/content/docs/start/inspecting-with-cli.mdx\` | Same | Same |
| \`site/src/content/docs/reference/cli.md\` | \`cargo install --path chasquimq-cli\` + "A pre-built binary is not yet published" | The \`--path\` form requires a clone; the "not yet published" line is actively false (v1.1.0 ships 5-platform binaries) |

## What's right now

Recommended install path: the cargo-dist one-liner.

\`\`\`bash
curl --proto '=https' --tlsv1.2 -LsSf https://github.com/jotarios/chasquimq/releases/latest/download/chasquimq-cli-installer.sh | sh
\`\`\`

Source build:

\`\`\`bash
cargo install --git https://github.com/jotarios/chasquimq chasquimq-cli
\`\`\`

## Test plan

- [x] cargo-dist installer script downloads v1.1.0 darwin-arm64 and produces working \`chasqui 1.1.0\` binary
- [x] \`cargo install --git\` compiles chasquimq-cli v1.1.0 from HEAD and produces the same binary
- [x] \`cargo search chasquimq\` confirms only the engine (\`chasquimq\`) is on crates.io, not the cli — matches \`publish = false\`
- [x] \`npm run build\` clean

## Left alone

- \`chasquimq-cli/README.md\` says \`cargo install --path chasquimq-cli\` — correct in context (operator-facing README, assumes you cloned the repo)
- \`docs/phase4-pyo3-design.md\` — historical design doc; aspirational text from when crates.io publish was on the table

#### Breaking changes

- Remove promise cancel API  [`a06ac6c`](https://redirect.github.com/sindresorhus/got/commit/a06ac6c)

- `strictContentLength` defaults to `true`  [`08e9dff`](https://redirect.github.com/sindresorhus/got/commit/08e9dff)
  - Got now throws a `ContentLengthMismatchError` by default if `Content-Length` doesn't match the actual body size. Set `{strictContentLength: false}` to restore the old behavior.
- `retry.enforceRetryRules` defaults to `true`  [`9bc8dfb`](https://redirect.github.com/sindresorhus/got/commit/9bc8dfb)
  - Custom `calculateDelay` functions are now only called when a retry is actually allowed by `limit`, `methods`, `statusCodes`, and `errorCodes`. If your `calculateDelay` was previously used to override retry eligibility unconditionally, set `{retry: {enforceRetryRules: false}}`.
- Piped header copying is now opt-in  [`8e392f3`](https://redirect.github.com/sindresorhus/got/commit/8e392f3)
  - Got no longer automatically copies headers from a piped stream. Set `{copyPipedHeaders: true}` to re-enable. Hop-by-hop headers are never copied even when enabled (RFC 9110 §7.6.1).
- `url` removed from public options objects  [`87de8d6`](https://redirect.github.com/sindresorhus/got/commit/87de8d6)
  - The `url` property is no longer present on the options object passed to hooks. Use `response.url` or `request.requestUrl` instead.
- 300 and 304 responses are no longer auto-followed  [`5fccaab`](https://redirect.github.com/sindresorhus/got/commit/5fccaab)
  - Per RFC 9110, 304 is a conditional-GET hint, not a redirect, and 300 is only a SHOULD for user agents. Got now returns these responses as-is. Handle them manually if needed.
- Removed the undocumented named export for Got.
  - Got has always been a default export. The named export was there only for buggy build tools during the ESM migration times.

#### Improvements

- Stream decode large `text`/`json` bodies incrementally for lower peak memory usage  [`c9a95b1`](https://redirect.github.com/sindresorhus/got/commit/c9a95b1)
- `uploadProgress` now emits granular per-chunk events for `json` and `form` request bodies  [`13c889d`](https://redirect.github.com/sindresorhus/got/commit/13c889d)

***

#### Migration guide

##### Replace `promise.cancel()` with `AbortController`

**Before:**

```js
const promise = got(url);
promise.cancel();
```

**After:**

```js
const controller = new AbortController();
const promise = got(url, {signal: controller.signal});
controller.abort();
```

##### Replace `isStream: true` with `got.stream()`

**Before:**

```js
got(url, {isStream: true});
```

**After:**

```js
got.stream(url);
```

##### Replace `form-data` / `form-data-encoder` with native `FormData`

**Before:**

```js
import {FormData} from 'formdata-node';
// or: import {FormData} from 'formdata-polyfill/esm.min.js';

const form = new FormData();
form.set('name', 'value');
await got.post(url, {body: form});
```

**After:**

```js
const form = new FormData();
form.set('name', 'value');
await got.post(url, {body: form});
```

##### Update `Buffer` usage to `Uint8Array`

`response.rawBody` and `promise.buffer()` now return `Uint8Array` instead of `Buffer`.

**Before:**

```js
const data = await got(url).buffer();
const copy = Buffer.from(data);
```

Draft rewrite of the studio's two legal texts to match what the booking system actually does. Closes audit items **C1–C4** from `LEGAL_REVIEW_FINDINGS.md`. **Final wording is for a German lawyer to review before live PayPal cutover** — this PR brings the technical facts onto the page so the lawyer has something concrete to polish.

## Datenschutzerklärung — comprehensive rewrite per Art. 13 DSGVO

Old text said "no cookies" and "no third-party sharing"; both were false. New version covers:

| Section | What it documents |
|---|---|
| § 2 Hosting & Server-Logfiles | AWS / CloudFront eu-central-1, IP / UA / referer, 30-day retention, Art. 6(1)(f) |
| § 3 Online-Buchung | Name, email, phone, comment, lesson, slot, payment ref → DynamoDB; legal basis Art. 6(1)(b); 10y retention per § 147 AO |
| § 4 SES E-Mail-Versand | Confirmation + cancel emails, 14-day SES log retention |
| § 5 Google Calendar Sync | Booking date/time + name/email forwarded to Google; SCC / DPF basis |
| § 6 PayPal | Order-ID + status + buyer email; PayPal own DSE referenced |
| § 7 Umami | Cookieless analytics, no Local Storage; Art. 6(1)(f) |
| § 8 Sentry | Error tracking, USA transfer, DPF basis |
| § 9 Cookies & Local Storage | Confirmed empty (matches reality) |
| § 10 Empfänger / Auftragsverarbeiter | Table: AWS, PayPal, Google, Umami, Sentry |
| § 11 Drittlandsübermittlung | Art. 46 DSGVO basis for US transfers |
| § 12 Rechte | Art. 15–21 DSGVO + Berlin BlnBDI as the supervisory authority |

## AGB — targeted updates to §§ 2–4 + new § 5

- **§ 2 Anmeldung**: online booking via `book.palavara.com` is now the primary channel; e-mail still works.
- **§ 3 Zahlung**: PayPal upfront for online bookings; e-mail bookings keep the on-site / PayPal-by-arrangement path.
- **§ 4 Stornierung**: explicit reference to the in-email cancellation link + automatic refund.
- **§ 5 Widerrufsrecht** *(new)*: flagged that fixed-date workshops fall under the § 312g Abs. 2 Nr. 9 BGB Freizeitveranstaltungs-Ausnahme. **Lawyer to confirm** this framing before publish.

Stand-Datum auf beiden Seiten: **Mai 2026**.

## Lawyer-review pointers (worth flagging in the review session)

- § 5 of the AGB (Widerrufsrecht): exemption for Freizeitveranstaltungen mit festem Termin is the standard reading for workshops, but worth confirming for hybrid offers (e.g. open-studio drop-ins).
- Sentry data scoping: I disclosed gekürzte IP-Adresse + browser context. If Sentry's PII scrubbing is configured differently, the description in § 8 may need narrowing.
- AWS: described as in eu-central-1 only. If any service spills to a US region (e.g. CloudFront edge), worth a sentence about transit.
- The Google Calendar sync (§ 5) sends the booker's email + name to a Google calendar Varvara owns — so technically Google is a separate Verantwortlicher for that data, not just a processor. Worded that way already, but worth the lawyer's eye.

## Out of scope / still on the punch list

- **C6** — `palavara.com` (artist site, palavara-front-v1 repo) has no Impressum. Separate repo, separate PR.
- **M2** — DynamoDB TTL on bookings table.
- **M3** — automated GDPR-Art.-17 erasure flow in the admin app.
- **L1** — phone number on Impressum (need the actual number).

author: jensrot
body:
## Fix: Particles animation disappearing on mobile navigation (Samsung Galaxy A56 / Android 16)

## Problem

On Android 16 (Chrome), the particle background would go blank after navigating to the demos page or between demo pages. A full page reload was required to restore it. The issue did not reproduce on desktop or older Android versions.

## Root causes (multiple, stacked)

**1. React Router v5 incompatibility with React 19**
React Router v5 caused `removeChild`/`insertBefore` DOM errors on every navigation in React 19. These errors crashed the entire React root, unmounting the `Particles` canvas. This was the primary cause. React Router v6 is officially compatible with React 19 and resolves the reconciliation errors.

**4. `height: -webkit-fill-available` resolving to ~47px on Android Chrome**
The `.particles-animation` container had `height: -webkit-fill-available` as a fallback, which resolved to the URL bar height (~47px) rather than the full viewport. The canvas was initialized at 47px, drawing all particles in a tiny strip at the top. Removed all explicit height declarations — `position: absolute; top: 0; right: 0; bottom: 0; left: 0` is sufficient.

**5. Resize events during URL bar transitions**
Android Chrome fires rapid resize events as the URL bar animates in/out during scroll. Added a 200ms debounced resize handler to prevent multiple `initCanvas` calls with transient intermediate heights. Also switched canvas sizing from `offsetWidth/offsetHeight` to `window.innerWidth/innerHeight` for more reliable viewport dimensions.

## Changes

- `package.json` — upgraded `react-router-dom` v5 → v6, removed `@types/react-router-dom` (types now bundled), added `eruda` for (future) debugging on mobile devices, added `test:all` npm script.
- `src/routing/Routing.tsx` — migrated to v6 API (`Switch→Routes`, `component→element`, `Redirect→Navigate`), removed all lazy loading and `Suspense`.
- `src/components/particles/Particles.tsx` — debounced resize handler (defensive code), `window.innerWidth/innerHeight` for canvas sizing (cleaner), removed debug logging.
- `src/index.scss` — removed `height: 100vh / 100dvh / -webkit-fill-available` from `.particles-animation`.
- `index.html` — added `translate="no"` on `#root` and `<meta name="google" content="notranslate">` to prevent browser translation DOM injection. Is defensive code and good practice.
- `particles.spec.ts` - added end to end tests for the Particles component.

author: isolson
body:
## Summary
Click the Config tab "Auto-Enforce" toggle, confirm the dialog, and the toggle stays visually off — even though the server has already saved \`config_auto_enforce: true\`. The badge updates, the toast fires, but the toggle button itself doesn't get the \`active\` CSS class until \`loadEnforceStatus\` next runs (page refresh / WS reconnect). The click looks dead.

## Root cause
\`toggleConfigAutoEnforce\` (`monitor.html:10153`) sent the PUT and updated the status badge, but never called \`setToggleActive\` on the toggle element itself. Every other toggle in the file (e.g. \`toggleAppAutoUpdate\` at line 6814) flips the visual state immediately before the PUT.

## What changes
- Flip the toggle's \`active\` class as soon as the user confirms (or immediately, on disable).
- On PUT failure, roll back the visual state so we never leave the UI showing "on" while the server thinks it's off.
- Throw on non-2xx HTTP responses so the rollback path actually runs (was previously swallowed).

## Test plan
- [x] JS function parses (manual \`new Function(...)\` smoke).
- [ ] Visual verify on dev once shipped: click toggle → confirm → toggle visibly switches to active → toast shows "Auto-enforce enabled". Click again → toggle visibly switches off → toast shows "Auto-enforce disabled". Refresh page → state matches what was last set.

author: rizwanzafaris
body:
A new /costs route gives operator visibility into the per-call cost + latency telemetry that agents/llm_router.py has been writing to agent_call_log on every successful LLM call since Phase 0. Without this, the only way to see spend is via raw SQL.

═══ Backend ═══

api/server.py — 6 endpoints, all hitting public.agent_call_log + v_daily_llm_cost view. Aggregations done in Python (table is small; adding more SQL views would be premature).

  GET /costs/summary              today / 7d / 30d totals + avg per
                                  resume_build (joined to resume_builds
                                  for context)
  GET /costs/daily?days=30        v_daily_llm_cost passthrough — one
                                  row per (day, provider, model)
  GET /costs/by-provider?days=7   aggregate by provider + token totals
                                  + avg latency, sorted by spend
  GET /costs/by-agent?days=7      by agent_name (e.g. "g2.writer",
                                  "CompanyAgent[Stripe]") incl.
                                  providers/models the agent uses
  GET /costs/by-resume-build      top resume_builds by total cost,
                                  hydrated with company_name +
                                  polisher_score + status + iterations
  GET /costs/recent-calls         last N rows from agent_call_log
                                  with provider / agent_name / has_error
                                  filters

All endpoints empty-state-safe — return zeros + "warning" string when agent_call_log doesn't exist yet (e.g. dev DB without multi_llm_schema applied).

═══ Frontend ═══

dashboard/src/app/costs/page.tsx (Server Component)
  Composes the 6 components below in a single page. Empty-states
  surfaced clearly so the user knows whether they're seeing zeros
  because the system hasn't run yet vs. because the schema wasn't
  applied.

dashboard/src/components/CostSummaryCards.tsx
  4 stat cards: Today / 7d / 30d / Avg per build (n=N). Color-coded:
  emerald / blue / violet / amber.

dashboard/src/components/DailyCostChart.tsx (recharts AreaChart)
  Stacked area chart by provider over last 30 days. Each provider gets
  its brand color (Claude amber, Gemini blue, OpenAI emerald,
  DeepSeek violet, Kimi pink). Linear gradient fills.

dashboard/src/components/CostByProviderChart.tsx (recharts PieChart)
  Donut chart + per-provider rows with progress bars showing %, token
  counts, avg latency. Quick "is Claude dominant or balanced?" answer.

dashboard/src/components/CostByAgentTable.tsx
  Sortable + filterable table of agents by spend. Shows providers/models
  per agent so you can spot agents using non-default models (e.g. an
  ATS critic accidentally hitting Claude instead of DeepSeek-R1).

dashboard/src/components/RecentCallsTable.tsx
  Live, filterable raw-row view of agent_call_log. Provider dropdown,
  errors-only checkbox, limit selector (50/100/250/500). Errored rows
  highlighted in red. Sticky header. Used for incident debugging.

dashboard/src/components/ProfileNav.tsx (existing, +1 line)
  /costs tab between Personas and Profile.

═══ How this validates the multi-LLM design ═══

Once Phase 1 (G2 graph) actually runs, this dashboard answers:
  * Is the multi-model assignment working? Provider donut should show ~40% Claude / ~25% Gemini / ~15% DeepSeek / ~5% Kimi / ~5% OpenAI (per docs/ARCHITECTURE.md model-assignment table)
  * Are critics ensembling correctly? Agent table should show both g2.ats_critic_a (deepseek) and g2.ats_critic_b (moonshot) called 1.5× per converged build on average
  * Is per-build cost tracking with the design doc's $2.01 estimate? Top-builds table makes this obvious

═══ Files ═══

  6 added · 3 modified
   dashboard/src/app/costs/page.tsx                       | new
   dashboard/src/components/CostSummaryCards.tsx          | new
   dashboard/src/components/DailyCostChart.tsx            | new
   dashboard/src/components/CostByProviderChart.tsx       | new
   dashboard/src/components/CostByAgentTable.tsx          | new
   dashboard/src/components/RecentCallsTable.tsx          | new
   api/server.py                                          | +6 endpoints
   dashboard/src/lib/profile-api.ts                       | +types/helpers
   dashboard/src/components/ProfileNav.tsx                | +1 nav tab

Tests: 52 passing, 1 skipped (langgraph local install).

author: bdchatham
body:
## Summary

Cross-review of the bench rebuild (#42) by `platform-engineer` and `kubernetes-specialist` surfaced one load-bearing bug plus several real correctness gaps. This PR addresses them.

### Must-fix (broken on every bench)

- **`pgrep` is not installed in `amazon/aws-cli:2.17.43`.** The exit-detection loop returned empty immediately, the sidecar fell through to upload before seiload had even started, and every bench produced an empty `report.log` in S3. Replaced with a `/proc/<pid>/comm` scan that works on the BusyBox-shaped userland the image actually ships.
- **Container start-order race.** In a multi-container Pod with `shareProcessNamespace: true`, the sidecar can win the start race. Without an appear-loop, the sidecar's first `pgrep`/`/proc` check returns "no seiload" and it uploads nothing. Added a 60s `APPEAR_DEADLINE` so the sidecar waits for seiload to show up before checking whether it's exited.
- **`gh pr list --head` exact-match.** The re-render determinism block matched on `feat/eng-<alias>-bench-<bench-tag>-` (no full branch name), and `--head` requires an exact match — `EXISTING` was always empty, so every re-render minted a fresh `<RUN_ID>`. Switched to `--json + jq startswith`, which is what the filter actually needs.

### Should-fix (correctness gaps)

- **`sed` substitution → `jq --argjson`.** The profile JSON's `__RPC_ENDPOINTS__` placeholder was replaced via `sed`, which is fragile to special characters in URLs (`/`, `:`, ports) and produces invalid JSON if anything in the substituted string contains the delimiter. `jq` builds the document structurally and is guaranteed valid.
- **`activeDeadlineSeconds` slack.** The outer Pod deadline was `(<DURATION> * 60) + 600`, but the inner sidecar `MAX_WAIT` is `(<DURATION> * 60) + 540`, plus the new 60s `APPEAR_DEADLINE` and 2s flush. Bumped the outer buffer to +660 so the Pod doesn't get killed by `activeDeadlineSeconds` while the sidecar is mid-upload.
- **Post-exit flush window.** Kubelet has a small lag writing the last buffered stdout to disk after abnormal exit (SIGKILL, OOM). Added `sleep 2` before pulling logs.
- **Halt on `<chain-id>-rpc` `NotFound`.** Bench-side procedure assumed the rpc SND existed and only checked phase. Added explicit `NotFound` halt with the apply path the engineer needs to take.
- **Halt on missing parent `engineers/<alias>/kustomization.yaml`.** Without it, merging the bench PR is a no-op for Flux. Added a halt that surfaces the onboarding gap.
- **Observation recipe.** `kubectl get job ... -o jsonpath='...Complete...'` returns empty until the Job is `Complete=True`, so an engineer tailing a bench killed by `activeDeadlineSeconds` would wait forever. Updated the recipe to also surface `Failed=True`.
- **Watch `NotFound` halt.** Added an explicit halt-condition entry in `SKILL.md` for `seictl nd get`/`seictl nd watch` exiting with `metav1.Status.reason=NotFound`, with the apply path as the resolution.

## Test plan

- [ ] Manually walk the procedure in `references/sei-load-bench.md` end-to-end on `eng-bdchatham` against a known-good chain; confirm a non-empty `report.log` lands in S3.
- [x] Confirm the `/proc/<pid>/comm` detection works in `amazon/aws-cli:2.17.43` (`docker run --rm amazon/aws-cli:2.17.43 sh -c "ls /proc/1/comm && cat /proc/1/comm"`).
- [x] Confirm the `jq --argjson` substitution against `nightly_evm_transfer.json` produces valid JSON with the expected `seiChainId` and `endpoints` fields.
- [x] Confirm the observation jsonpath returns `Complete=True` on a successful run and `Failed=True` on a deadline-killed run.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Updates operational runbooks that drive automated bench rendering and observation; mistakes could block benches or mis-handle job completion, but changes are limited to skill/reference docs (no runtime code).
> 
> **Overview**
> Fixes several correctness issues in the sei-load bench guidance so benches reliably produce non-empty S3 reports and re-renders are deterministic.
> 
> Updates the upload sidecar recipe to detect `seiload` via `/proc/*/comm` (no `pgrep` dependency), wait for `seiload` to appear before watching for exit, add a short post-exit flush delay, and increase `activeDeadlineSeconds` slack to cover uploader runtime.
> 
> Hardens render-time steps by switching profile JSON mutation from `sed` placeholders to structural `jq` updates, fixing `<RUN_ID>` reuse by filtering `gh pr list` results with `startswith`, and adding explicit halt conditions/recipes for missing rpc SND (`NotFound`), missing parent `engineers/<alias>/kustomization.yaml`, and Job terminal status checks that include both `Complete` and `Failed`.
>
